added.summary: The paper application can be mailed to the VCCB office in Anchorage.
added.quote: You may fill out and send in the application by mail. 4300 Boniface Pkwy Anchorage, AK 99504
added.pinpoint: VCCB Application page, How to Apply, Mail
added.source_title: Alaska VCCB, Application and Forms page

added.summary: The paper application can be faxed to the VCCB.
added.quote: You may fill out and fax in the application. fax: (907) 465-2379
added.pinpoint: VCCB Application page, How to Apply, Fax
added.source_title: Alaska VCCB, Application and Forms page

added.summary: The application can be emailed to the VCCB; the application's contact block gives the email address and its instructions say it can be submitted by email.
added.quote: Email: VCCB@alaska.gov
added.pinpoint: Application (05/2026), contact block on page 1 and on the Claim Application and Instructions page
added.source_title: Alaska VCCB Application for Crime Victim Compensation (05/2026)

added.summary: An application can also be filed online through the VCCB's secure web portal, reached from the VCCB website.
added.quote: Please visit https://vccb.alaska.gov to access the secure web application portal to file an application online.
added.pinpoint: Claim Application and Instructions, Is there another way to apply?
added.source_title: Alaska VCCB Application for Crime Victim Compensation (05/2026)

added.summary: The signed Release of Information on the last page of the application must be included however the application is sent.
added.quote: Whether applying online, by email, fax or through a printed application, please ensure the Release of Information on the final page is signed and included.
added.pinpoint: VCCB Application page, How to Apply
added.source_title: Alaska VCCB, Application and Forms page

added.summary: Include a copy of the police report if you have it; you do not need to wait for it before applying.
added.quote: Please include any documentation you have available such as a copy of the police report, bills, receipts, or other crime-related information.
added.pinpoint: Claim Application and Instructions, Do I need to include any other documentation with the application?
added.source_title: Alaska VCCB Application for Crime Victim Compensation (05/2026)

added.summary: Submit invoices or statements for claimed services, or a page listing each provider and dates of service so the VCCB can request the records.
added.quote: Billing Records: Submit invoices, statements, or receipts for all medical, dental, counseling, or other claimed services.
added.pinpoint: Application (05/2026), Section 5: Crime-Related Expenses, Billing Records
added.source_title: Alaska VCCB Application for Crime Victim Compensation (05/2026)

added.summary: If you paid for services yourself, save and send the receipts as verification.
added.quote: please save your receipts to send in as verification.
added.pinpoint: VCCB Application page, Additional Forms
added.source_title: Alaska VCCB, Application and Forms page

added.summary: Copies of insurance information strengthen the application.
added.quote: To strengthen your application, include copies of any supporting documents, such as bills or insurance information.
added.pinpoint: VCCB Application page, How to Apply
added.source_title: Alaska VCCB, Application and Forms page

added.summary: By statute the applicant submits reports from the physicians who treated or examined the victim, if reasonably available.
added.quote: the applicant shall, before a hearing on an application under this chapter, submit reports, if reasonably available, from all physicians or surgeons who have treated or examined the victim in relation to the injury for which compensation is claimed
added.source_title: AS 18.67.010 to 18.67.180, Violent Crimes Compensation Board (Alaska Statutes, print view)

added.summary: For lost wages, the VCCB contacts the employer for wage and date information without sharing case details.
added.quote: Your employer will be contacted for wage and date information, however no details of your case will be shared
added.pinpoint: VCCB Application page, Additional Forms, Loss of Income
added.source_title: Alaska VCCB, Application and Forms page

added.summary: A treatment plan is required for counseling beyond the initial award.
added.quote: there are session rate limits and treatment plans are required for services beyond the initial award
added.pinpoint: VCCB Application page, Additional Forms, Counseling
added.source_title: Alaska VCCB, Application and Forms page

added.summary: Relocation requests need the Request for Relocation Assistance form completed before expenses are covered.
added.quote: This Request for Relocation Assistance must be completed prior to any expenses being covered.
added.pinpoint: VCCB Application page, Additional Forms, Relocation
added.source_title: Alaska VCCB, Application and Forms page

added.summary: Rental assistance requests need the Request for Rental Assistance form and documentation such as a lease copy.
added.quote: Request for Rental Assistance must be filled out along with documentation, such as a copy of your lease
added.pinpoint: VCCB Application page, Additional Forms, Rental Assistance
added.source_title: Alaska VCCB, Application and Forms page

added.summary: Mail the completed application to the Alabama Crime Victims Compensation Commission, P.O. Box 231267, Montgomery, Alabama 36123-1267.
added.quote: The completed application can be returned by: FAX: (334)290-4455 Email: info@acvcc.alabama.gov Mail: Alabama Crime Victims Compensation Commission P.O. Box 231267 Montgomery, Alabama 36123-1267
added.pinpoint: Compensation page, How Do I File A Claim?
added.source_title: ACVCC: Compensation

added.summary: Email the completed application to info@acvcc.alabama.gov.
added.quote: Please download the completed application and email it to info@acvcc.alabama.gov or fax it to 334-290-4455.
added.pinpoint: Application, Claim Authorization page, submission box
added.source_title: ACVCC application for compensation (MAR 2026)

added.summary: Fax the completed application to 334-290-4455.
added.quote: Please download the completed application and email it to info@acvcc.alabama.gov or fax it to 334-290-4455.
added.pinpoint: Application, Claim Authorization page, submission box
added.source_title: ACVCC application for compensation (MAR 2026)

added.summary: The application must be signed; a fax or electronic signature is accepted, but the Commission may ask for an original notarized signature.
added.quote: The claimant must submit an application that has been signed by either facsimile signature or electronic signature.
added.pinpoint: Ala. Admin. Code r. 262-X-4-.02(10)
added.source_title: Ala. Admin. Code r. 262-X-4-.02

added.summary: Include proof of U.S. citizenship or that you are an alien eligible for public benefits.
added.quote: You must submit proof of US citizenship or that you are an alien eligible for public benefits.
added.pinpoint: Application, Section 1 note
added.source_title: ACVCC application for compensation (MAR 2026)

added.summary: Include a copy of the police report if one is available.
added.quote: Complete this section and, if one is available, provide a copy of the Police Report.
added.pinpoint: Application, Section 5 (Crime Information)
added.source_title: ACVCC application for compensation (MAR 2026)

added.summary: For each type of compensation you request, include the related bills or receipts.
added.quote: Provide any corresponding and directly related bills/receipts.
added.pinpoint: Application, Section 6 (Compensation Request)
added.source_title: ACVCC application for compensation (MAR 2026)

added.summary: If you are asking for medical expenses, the victim or a representative must sign and date the health information authorization in the application.
added.quote: Either the patient (victim) or their representative must sign and date this authorization if consideration of medical expenses is being requested.
added.pinpoint: Application, Patient Authorization for Use and Disclosure of Protected Health Information
added.source_title: ACVCC application for compensation (MAR 2026)

added.summary: If you file more than one year after the incident, explain the good cause in writing.
added.quote: The claim must be filed within one (1) year of the incident, or good cause must be submitted in writing.
added.pinpoint: Application Form page, Additional Requirements
added.source_title: ACVCC: Application Form page

added.summary: If the crime was not reported to law enforcement within 72 hours, explain the good cause in writing.
added.quote: The crime must be reported to the proper law enforcement agency within 72 hours of the incident, or good cause must be submitted in writing.
added.pinpoint: Application Form page, Additional Requirements
added.source_title: ACVCC: Application Form page

added.summary: If someone other than the victim signs as claimant, include documentation that they are legally authorized to act for the victim.
added.quote: The claimant (if other than victim) must be the person legally authorized to act on the behalf of the victim. Documentation of this authority must be provided.
added.pinpoint: Application, Claim Authorization page, signature note
added.source_title: ACVCC application for compensation (MAR 2026)

added.summary: If the victim is 19 or older but incapacitated, include proof of guardianship or conservatorship.
added.quote: If the victim is 19 or older, but is incapacitated, you will have to provide proof of guardianship/conservatorship over the victim.
added.pinpoint: Application, Section 3 (Claimant Information)
added.source_title: ACVCC application for compensation (MAR 2026)

added.summary: For lost wages, include written documentation from your employer or a W-2.
added.quote: Lost wages shall be verified by obtaining written documentation from the employer or by submission of a W-2 tax document.
added.pinpoint: Ala. Admin. Code r. 262-X-4-.04(8)
added.source_title: Ala. Admin. Code r. 262-X-4-.04

added.summary: For lost wages, if you are self-employed, include a tax transcript from the IRS.
added.quote: A tax transcript from the IRS is required if the person seeking reimbursement of his/her lost wages is self-employed.
added.pinpoint: Ala. Admin. Code r. 262-X-4-.04(8)
added.source_title: Ala. Admin. Code r. 262-X-4-.04

added.summary: A sexual assault victim can claim up to two weeks of lost wages without a doctor's excuse; beyond two weeks, include a doctor's excuse.
added.quote: A victim of sexual assault may be granted compensation for maximum of two weeks of lost wages without a doctor's excuse. A doctor's excuse must be provided for lost wages in excess of two weeks to be considered for reimbursement.
added.pinpoint: Ala. Admin. Code r. 262-X-4-.04(28)
added.source_title: Ala. Admin. Code r. 262-X-4-.04

added.summary: For counseling, the Commission needs a letter from the clinician certifying that therapy is necessary because of the victimization.
added.quote: ACVCC must receive a letter from the clinician certifying that the victim is engaged in necessary therapy due to his/her victimization.
added.pinpoint: Ala. Admin. Code r. 262-X-4-.07(2)(a)
added.source_title: Ala. Admin. Code r. 262-X-4-.07

added.summary: For ongoing counseling, the clinician must send quarterly updates certifying the treatment is still necessary.
added.quote: Quarterly updates from the clinician certifying that the treatment is necessary and the result of victimization must be submitted in order for payment to be considered.
added.pinpoint: Ala. Admin. Code r. 262-X-4-.07(2)(b)
added.source_title: Ala. Admin. Code r. 262-X-4-.07

added.summary: For counseling, the clinician must provide an itemized bill for the treatment sessions.
added.quote: The clinician must provide an itemized bill for treatment sessions.
added.pinpoint: Ala. Admin. Code r. 262-X-4-.07(2)(c)
added.source_title: Ala. Admin. Code r. 262-X-4-.07

added.summary: For moving expenses, include written estimates or receipts.
added.quote: Written estimates and/or receipts are required for payment of moving expenses.
added.pinpoint: Ala. Admin. Code r. 262-X-4-.04(14)(a)
added.source_title: Ala. Admin. Code r. 262-X-4-.04

added.summary: For temporary relocation, include a copy of the hotel bill, credit card receipt, or another verifiable document.
added.quote: A copy of the hotel bill, credit card receipt, or other verifiable document is required for verification.
added.pinpoint: Ala. Admin. Code r. 262-X-4-.04(14)(b)
added.source_title: Ala. Admin. Code r. 262-X-4-.04

added.summary: The program offers an online application, which its Documents and Forms page marks as the preferred way to apply.
added.quote: We offer an ONLINE APPLICATION process for Victim Compensation! Access the Online Application
added.pinpoint: CVRB home page, Crime Victim Compensation Application
added.source_title: Arkansas DPS, Crime Victims Reparations Board home page

added.summary: A paper application can be sent to the Crime Victims Reparations office, listed on the DPS site at 322 South Main Street, Suite 615, Little Rock, AR 72201.
added.quote: Victims may apply for compensation by submitting an application to the Arkansas Crime Victim's Reparations office. Applications are available from the Arkansas Crime Victim's Reparations office or from one of Arkansas's 28 elected prosecutors. These programs are funded by fees collected from criminal offenders and a federal grant through the Victims of Crime Act, administered by the U.S. Department of Justice. Contact CVRB 322 South Main Street, Suite 615 Little Rock, AR 72201
added.pinpoint: About CVRB page, applying and Contact CVRB
added.source_title: Arkansas DPS, About CVRB page

added.summary: Attach a copy of the law enforcement agency's incident report to the application.
added.quote: NOTE: You must attach a copy of the law-enforcement agency's incident report to this application.
added.pinpoint: Application, Section B, Crime Information
added.source_title: Arkansas CVRB, Application for Crime Victim Compensation (10-6-2023)

added.summary: When asking for medical or counseling costs, attach copies of all itemized medical and counseling bills or other statements verifying the expenses.
added.quote: NOTE: In addition to completing this section, you must attach copies of all itemized medical bills, mental health counseling bills, or other statements verifying expenses.
added.pinpoint: Application, Section C, Request for Medical Treatment/Mental-Health Counseling
added.source_title: Arkansas CVRB, Application for Crime Victim Compensation (10-6-2023)

added.summary: For lost wages, attach your most recent pay stub, or if self-employed, your tax returns from the last three years.
added.quote: Attach a copy of your most recent pay stub from your employer. If you are self-employed, you must furnish copies of your tax returns from the last three (3) years so lost wages can be most accurately determined.
added.pinpoint: Application, Section D, Request for Lost Wages
added.source_title: Arkansas CVRB, Application for Crime Victim Compensation (10-6-2023)

added.summary: For lost wages, give the name and address of the physician who can verify your time off, or attach a recent disability statement.
added.quote: You must also provide the complete name and address of the physician who can verify your disability period, or you may attach a copy of a recent disability statement.
added.pinpoint: Application, Section D, Request for Lost Wages
added.source_title: Arkansas CVRB, Application for Crime Victim Compensation (10-6-2023)

added.summary: For funeral or burial expenses, include a copy of the funeral bill and the death certificate.
added.quote: NOTE: You must submit a copy of the funeral bill and the death certificate with this application.
added.pinpoint: Application, Section E, Request for Funeral/Burial Expenses
added.source_title: Arkansas CVRB, Application for Crime Victim Compensation (10-6-2023)

added.summary: For loss of support after a victim's death, include the victim's last three years of tax returns, Social Security benefit verification, and proof of guardianship for a minor dependent.
added.quote: NOTE: You must attach copies of the deceased victim's last three (3) years' tax returns. You must also provide verification regarding the denial or receipt of any benefits from the Social Security Administration. You must be the legal guardian of a minor dependent to request loss of support on their behalf and must provide verification of guardianship.
added.pinpoint: Application, Section F, Request for Loss of Support
added.source_title: Arkansas CVRB, Application for Crime Victim Compensation (10-6-2023)

added.summary: For crime scene cleanup, attach receipts or other supporting documentation.
added.quote: Receipts or supporting documentation must be attached to this application.
added.pinpoint: Application, Section G, Request for Assistance with Crime Scene Clean Up
added.source_title: Arkansas CVRB, Application for Crime Victim Compensation (10-6-2023)

added.title: Arkansas.gov state portal, Crime Victims Reparations Board agency page

added.summary: For a crime in Maricopa County, the Maricopa edition of the application says to mail it to the Victim Compensation Program at 225 West Madison Street, Phoenix, AZ 85003.

Please sign and date sections 9-12 on pages 4 and 5 mail to / Favor poner la fecha, firmar las secciones 9-12 en

For more information or to find your county program, call /

added.summary: Send a copy of every bill for each expense being claimed along with the claim form.
added.quote: A copy of all bills, contracts, receipts, and insurance statements relating to each expense claimed under subsection (D)(6)
added.source_title: A.A.C. Title 10, Chapter 4 (Arizona Criminal Justice Commission), Article 1 Crime Victim Compensation Program, Supp. 26-1

added.summary: Send copies of receipts for each expense being claimed.
added.quote: A copy of all bills, contracts, receipts, and insurance statements relating to each expense claimed under subsection (D)(6)
added.source_title: A.A.C. Title 10, Chapter 4 (Arizona Criminal Justice Commission), Article 1 Crime Victim Compensation Program, Supp. 26-1

added.summary: Send copies of insurance statements for each expense being claimed, since the program pays only after other sources.
added.quote: A copy of all bills, contracts, receipts, and insurance statements relating to each expense claimed under subsection (D)(6)
added.source_title: A.A.C. Title 10, Chapter 4 (Arizona Criminal Justice Commission), Article 1 Crime Victim Compensation Program, Supp. 26-1

added.summary: If claiming lost wages, include a signed statement on the employer's official letterhead verifying the work loss.
added.quote: If work loss expenses are claimed, a signed statement on official letterhead: a. From the claimant’s employer verifying the information provided under subsection (D)(6)(c)
added.source_title: A.A.C. Title 10, Chapter 4 (Arizona Criminal Justice Commission), Article 1 Crime Victim Compensation Program, Supp. 26-1

added.summary: If claiming lost wages, a doctor or mental health therapist must also confirm in writing that the victim could not work because of crime-related injuries.
added.quote: Written verification must also be provided by a doctor or mental health therapist stating the victim was unable to work as a result of crime related injuries.
added.pinpoint: Application, Section 4, Work Loss Requirement
added.source_title: ACJC Victim Compensation application (June 2015)

added.summary: If asking for travel costs, attach a detailed log with travel dates, mileage, and any fares or fees; gas, food, and lodging are not included.
added.quote: If this box is checked, please attach a detailed log of travel expenses including travel dates, mileage and any fares or fees paid. Gas, food, or lodging expenses may not be included.
added.pinpoint: Application, Section 3, travel expenses box
added.source_title: ACJC Victim Compensation application (June 2015)

added.summary: Sign and date the repayment promise, information release, health information authorization, and certification sections at the end of the application.
added.quote: Please sign and date sections 9-12 on pages 4 and 5 mail to
added.pinpoint: Application, page 3
added.source_title: ACJC Victim Compensation application (June 2015)

added.summary: The county program can ask for more documentation to confirm eligibility and each expense.
added.quote: Any documentation required by the operational unit to fully investigate and substantiate claimant eligibility and all claim expense requests.
added.source_title: A.A.C. Title 10, Chapter 4 (Arizona Criminal Justice Commission), Article 1 Crime Victim Compensation Program, Supp. 26-1

added.summary: The county board must decide within 60 days after the county program receives a complete claim, unless there is good cause for delay.
added.quote: The Board shall make a decision within 60 days after the operational unit receives a complete and actionable claim under R10-4-107 unless good cause for delay exists.
added.source_title: A.A.C. Title 10, Chapter 4 (Arizona Criminal Justice Commission), Article 1 Crime Victim Compensation Program, Supp. 26-1

or

added.summary: Mail the claim form to VCAP at 900 N. King Street, 4th Floor, Wilmington, DE 19801.
added.quote: You must submit a claim form to get the process started. Your claim can be submitted in the following ways: Mail: 900 N. King Street, 4th Floor Wilmington, DE 19801
added.pinpoint: VCAP brochure (English), How do I file a claim?
added.source_title: VCAP brochure (English)

added.summary: Fax the claim form to VCAP at (302) 577-1326.
added.quote: Fax: (302) 577-1326 If you would prefer to apply online, please visit: https://ccvcde.org
added.pinpoint: VCAP brochure (English), How do I file a claim?
added.source_title: VCAP brochure (English)

added.summary: Apply online through the VCAP claim portal at https://ccvcde.org.
added.quote: If you would prefer to apply online, please visit: https://ccvcde.org
added.pinpoint: VCAP brochure (English), How do I file a claim?
added.source_title: VCAP brochure (English)

added.summary: The claim must be filed in writing on VCAP's own claim form and signed by the claimant.
added.quote: All claims filed with the Agency must be in writing on the Agency's provided claim form and signed by the claimant.
added.source_title: 11 Del. C. ch. 90, Compensation for Innocent Victims of Crime (sections 9001 to 9025)

added.summary: The official claim form includes subrogation, authorization, and consent agreements that must be part of the filing.
added.quote: claims must be filed in the office of VCAP on official forms which include subrogation, authorization, and consent agreements.
added.pinpoint: 1 Del. Admin. Code 301-11.1
added.source_title: 1 Del. Admin. Code 301, Victims' Compensation Assistance Program Rules and Regulations

added.summary: Every loss must be backed by documentation before VCAP awards compensation.
added.quote: All losses must be supported by documentation prior to compensation being awarded.
added.pinpoint: Delaware DOJ VCAP page, FAQs, Are there any limits?
added.source_title: Delaware DOJ, Victims' Compensation Assistance Program page and FAQs

added.summary: If VCAP asks for more documentation while investigating, it must be sent within 45 days of the request.
added.quote: If VCAP, in its investigation of a claim, requires further documentation from the claimant, such documentation must be submitted to VCAP no later than 45 days of the date of VCAP's request.
added.pinpoint: 1 Del. Admin. Code 301-11.2
added.source_title: 1 Del. Admin. Code 301, Victims' Compensation Assistance Program Rules and Regulations

added.summary: Survivors claiming temporary housing, rent, security deposit, furniture, or moving costs must send documentation within 45 days of VCAP's request.
added.quote: A victim who seeks compensation for temporary housing, rent, security deposit, furniture and/or moving expenses must submit documentation within 45 days of VCAP's request therefor, unless an extension is granted by the Agency.
added.pinpoint: 1 Del. Admin. Code 301-11.3
added.source_title: 1 Del. Admin. Code 301, Victims' Compensation Assistance Program Rules and Regulations

added.summary: If the injury happened on the job, the survivor must file a workers' compensation claim and send proof of it before applying to VCAP.
added.quote: If the victim seeks compensation for an injury sustained while in the course and scope of employment, the victim must submit a claim for worker's compensation, and provide documentation thereof, before making application to VCAP for compensation.
added.pinpoint: 1 Del. Admin. Code 301-11.4
added.source_title: 1 Del. Admin. Code 301, Victims' Compensation Assistance Program Rules and Regulations

added.summary: To ask for an emergency award, the claimant must request it in writing with the claim form and show just cause.
added.quote: The claimant, must, in writing, request an emergency award when submitting his claim form and show just cause as to why such an award should be considered.
added.pinpoint: 1 Del. Admin. Code 301-23.0
added.source_title: 1 Del. Admin. Code 301, Victims' Compensation Assistance Program Rules and Regulations

added.summary: A decision on a claim can take up to 60 days, and longer in rare cases.
added.quote: It can take up to 60 days to make a decision on your claim. In rare cases, it can take longer.
added.pinpoint: VCAP brochure (English), What can I expect next?
added.source_title: VCAP brochure (English)

added.quote: (a) In person or by private delivery to the Crime Victims Compensation Board, 500 Mero Street, 2 SC1, Frankfort, Kentucky 40601;
added.pinpoint: 802 KAR 3:010 Section 4(2)(a)
added.source_title: 802 KAR 3:010 Crime victims compensation

added.summary: A claim can be mailed to the Board's office in Frankfort.
added.quote: (a) In person or by private delivery to the Crime Victims Compensation Board, 500 Mero Street, 2 SC1, Frankfort, Kentucky 40601; (b) By mail to the address listed above;
added.pinpoint: 802 KAR 3:010 Section 4(2)(b)
added.source_title: 802 KAR 3:010 Crime victims compensation

added.summary: A claim can be emailed to the Board if the whole claim fits in a single email.
added.quote: (c) By electronic mail to crimevictims@ky.gov, if the document can be sent in one (1) electronic message;
added.pinpoint: 802 KAR 3:010 Section 4(2)(c)
added.source_title: 802 KAR 3:010 Crime victims compensation

added.summary: A claim can be filed through the Board's online claims portal.
added.quote: (d) Through the online claims portal at: https://kycc.ky.gov/CVOnline/home
added.pinpoint: 802 KAR 3:010 Section 4(2)(d)
added.source_title: 802 KAR 3:010 Crime victims compensation

added.summary: The Board's FAQ says a paper claim form can also be faxed.
added.quote: Paper claim forms can be submitted to the Board by fax (502-573-4817)
added.pinpoint: CVCB FAQ (updated August 2024), Where should I send my paper claim form?
added.source_title: Crime Victims Compensation Board FAQ (updated August 2024)

added.summary: The Board's checklist asks for a police report along with the claim form, if applicable.
added.quote: In addition to the claim form, you will need to submit, if applicable, 1) Police Report
added.pinpoint: CVCB Documents to include, item 1
added.source_title: CVCB Documents to include (claim checklist)

added.summary: For medical expenses, the claimant must send copies of itemized medical billing statements.
added.quote: Claimants requesting reimbursement or payment for medical expenses incurred as a result of the crime shall submit the following documentation as proof of the eligible expenses: (1) Copies of itemized medical billing statements for medical treatment provided to the claimant as a direct result of the crime.
added.pinpoint: 802 KAR 3:030 Section 8(1)
added.source_title: 802 KAR 3:030 Crime victims compensation awards

added.summary: If itemized medical bills are not available, non-itemized bills are accepted when the medical records from the visit are sent with them.
added.quote: (2) If itemized billing statements are not available, non-itemized medical billing statements shall be accepted if: (a) The medical records from the visit are submitted along with the non-itemized medical billing statements;
added.pinpoint: 802 KAR 3:030 Section 8(2)(a)
added.source_title: 802 KAR 3:030 Crime victims compensation awards

added.summary: The claim form says each listed expense needs documentation such as itemized bills, receipts, service contracts, invoices, or other proof of payment or balance due.
added.quote: You must include documentation of the expense, such as itemized bills, receipts, service contracts, invoices, or other proof of payment and/or balance due.
added.pinpoint: Crime Victim Compensation Form (July 2024), Section 7
added.source_title: Crime Victim Compensation Form (revised July 2024)

added.summary: For counseling expenses, the claimant must send a Mental Health Counselor's Report from the therapist and the treatment plan, along with itemized bills.
added.quote: (1) Claimants requesting reimbursement or payment of mental health counseling expenses shall submit the following documentation as proof of the eligible expenses: (a) Mental Health Counselor's Report completed by the claimant's or victim's therapist or mental health clinician; (b) Treatment plan devised by the claimant or victim's therapist or mental health clinician;
added.pinpoint: 802 KAR 3:030 Section 9(1)
added.source_title: 802 KAR 3:030 Crime victims compensation awards

added.summary: A claim for lost wages or loss of support must include a notarized Employment Verification form, plus a Physician Statement or Mental Health Counselor's Report if Board staff ask for one.
added.quote: (3) If applying for lost wages or loss of support, a claim shall be supplemented by: (a) A notarized Employment Verification form; and (b) If requested by Board staff: 1. A Physician Statement form; or 2. A Mental Health Counselor's Report form.
added.pinpoint: 802 KAR 3:010 Section 4(3)
added.source_title: 802 KAR 3:010 Crime victims compensation

added.summary: A self-employed claimant seeking lost earnings sends the preceding two years of tax returns.
added.quote: If you are selfemployed, please submit the preceding two years' worth of tax returns.
added.pinpoint: CVCB Documents to include, item 4(a)
added.source_title: CVCB Documents to include (claim checklist)

added.summary: Anyone asking for an emergency award completes, signs, and dates the Emergency Award Request Form and attaches it to the claim form.
added.quote: If yes, please complete, sign, and date the attached Emergency Award Request Form and attach it to your claim form.
added.pinpoint: Crime Victim Compensation Form (July 2024), Section 4
added.source_title: Crime Victim Compensation Form (revised July 2024)

added.summary: A survivor seeking the lump sum for a sexual assault claim filed more than ten years after the crime must send proof of the crime date, that the kit was collected and when, that it went untested for a long time, and anecdotal proof of damages.
added.quote: (1) For purposes of KRS 49.370(7), a claimant seeking an award under this provision shall submit: (a) Proof that the crime occurred more than ten (10) years prior to the date of filing of the claim; (b) Proof that the sexual assault kit was collected; (c) Proof of the collection date of the biological material; (d) Proof that the biological material went untested for an extended period; and (e) Anecdotal proof of the damages incurred as a result of the crime.
added.pinpoint: 802 KAR 3:010 Section 8(1)
added.source_title: 802 KAR 3:010 Crime victims compensation

added.summary: For funeral expenses, the checklist asks for the signed funeral service contract.
added.quote: 3) Signed funeral service contract for funeral expenses
added.pinpoint: CVCB Documents to include, item 3
added.source_title: CVCB Documents to include (claim checklist)

added.summary: For loss of support, the checklist asks for documentation of the support the supporter brought into the household at the time of the crime.
added.quote: a. Documentation outlining amount of support brought into household by the supporter at the time of the crime.
added.pinpoint: CVCB Documents to include, item 5(a)
added.source_title: CVCB Documents to include (claim checklist)

added.summary: For claims filed after July 1, 2026, the investigator must finish the investigative report within 90 days after the claim is assigned; this is the investigation step, not the Board's final decision.
added.quote: (3) For claims filed after July 1, 2026, the claims investigator shall complete an investigative report on the claim within ninety (90) days after it is assigned by the Board Clerk to the claims investigator.
added.pinpoint: 802 KAR 3:010 Section 6(3)
added.source_title: 802 KAR 3:010 Crime victims compensation

added.title: CVCB Documents to include (claim checklist)

added.summary: You can mail the application to the Crime Victims' Compensation board office at LCLE in Baton Rouge.
added.quote: Or Write to: Crime Victims’ Compensation Louisiana Commission on Law Enforcement PO Box 3133 Baton Rouge, LA 70821
added.pinpoint: LCLE CVC program page, For More Information
added.source_title: LCLE Crime Victims' Compensation Fund program page

added.summary: Applications for an adult victim of a sexually oriented offense are sent directly to the board office.
added.quote: Applications involving an adult victim of a sexually-oriented criminal offense are sent directly to the board’s office.
added.pinpoint: LAC 22:XIII.303(A)(1)
added.source_title: LAC Title 22, Part XIII, Crime Victims Reparations Board rules (Feb 2025)

added.summary: The form says to mail the original application, police report, and itemized claims to the parish claim investigator or the board office.
added.quote: Please mail the original application, along with the Claim Investigator Review, the complete police report, newspaper articles (if available) and any claims (including claim forms and itemized invoices) to you Parish Claim’s Investigator or the CVR Board Office.
added.pinpoint: Application instructions page (form revised Feb 19, 2025)
added.source_title: Application for Crime Victims Reparations (form revised Feb 2025)

added.summary: The claimant must sign the application.
added.quote: The claimant MUST sign the application.
added.pinpoint: Application instructions, eligibility only item 1(b)
added.source_title: Application for Crime Victims Reparations (form revised Feb 2025)

added.summary: An application is valid only if reasonable documentation of the crime is submitted with it.
added.quote: Crime Victims Reparations applications shall be valid only if reasonable documentation of the crime is submitted with the application.
added.pinpoint: Application instructions, eligibility only item 5
added.source_title: Application for Crime Victims Reparations (form revised Feb 2025)

added.summary: A report from law enforcement counts as reasonable documentation of the crime.
added.quote: A report from law enforcement, rather than a police report.
added.pinpoint: Resume Digest of Act 684 on La. R.S. 46:1806(A)(2)(a)
added.source_title: Resume Digest, Act 684 (HB 969), 2026 Regular Session

added.summary: Court records about the crime count as reasonable documentation.
added.quote: Court records pertaining to the crime, rather than evidencing the criminal prosecution.
added.pinpoint: Resume Digest of Act 684 on La. R.S. 46:1806(A)(2)(b)
added.source_title: Resume Digest, Act 684 (HB 969), 2026 Regular Session

added.summary: An attestation from a healthcare provider who examined the injury counts as reasonable documentation.
added.quote: An attestation from a healthcare provider who conducted an examination of the personal injury suffered by the victim.
added.pinpoint: Resume Digest of Act 684 on La. R.S. 46:1806(A)(2)(c)
added.source_title: Resume Digest, Act 684 (HB 969), 2026 Regular Session

added.summary: An attestation from the provider or coroner who did a forensic medical exam counts as reasonable documentation.
added.quote: An attestation from a healthcare provider or coroner who conducted a forensic medical examination on the victim.
added.pinpoint: Resume Digest of Act 684 on La. R.S. 46:1806(A)(2)(d)
added.source_title: Resume Digest, Act 684 (HB 969), 2026 Regular Session

added.summary: Each expense other than the forensic exam needs an itemized bill, not a billing statement.
added.quote: An itemized bill, not a billing statement, must accompany the application for each non-FME expense claimed.
added.pinpoint: LAC 22:XIII.303(A)(4)
added.source_title: LAC Title 22, Part XIII, Crime Victims Reparations Board rules (Feb 2025)

added.summary: Bills must show the victim or claimant as guarantor and the balance owed.
added.quote: All invoices, bills, etc. must indicate the victim/claimant as the guarantor and indicate balances owed.
added.pinpoint: LAC 22:XIII.303(A)(5)
added.source_title: LAC Title 22, Part XIII, Crime Victims Reparations Board rules (Feb 2025)

added.summary: Each type of claim form says which documents support that expense.
added.quote: Each type of claim form used by the board should identify the documents that must be submitted by the victim/claimant to support and verify a claimed expense.
added.pinpoint: LAC 22:XIII.501(B)(1)
added.source_title: LAC Title 22, Part XIII, Crime Victims Reparations Board rules (Feb 2025)

added.summary: Lost wages need verification from the employer.
added.quote: wage verification by the employer is required.
added.source_title: LAC Title 22, Part XIII, Crime Victims Reparations Board rules (Feb 2025)

added.summary: For lost wages, a medical doctor must document that the survivor could not work because of the crime.
added.quote: The inability to work must be directly related to the victimization and documented by the appropriate medical doctor.
added.pinpoint: LAC 22:XIII.503(D)(2)
added.source_title: LAC Title 22, Part XIII, Crime Victims Reparations Board rules (Feb 2025)

added.summary: Send news articles about the incident if there are any.
added.quote: Submit copies of newspaper articles, press releases, etc., that describe the incident, when available.
added.pinpoint: Application instructions, eligibility only item 4
added.source_title: Application for Crime Victims Reparations (form revised Feb 2025)

added.summary: The form asks for a letter of explanation when filing after the deadline it prints.
added.quote: If you are filing later than one year, you must attach a letter of explanation.
added.pinpoint: Application form page 1
added.source_title: Application for Crime Victims Reparations (form revised Feb 2025)

added.summary: An eligibility decision usually comes within 30 to 45 days.
added.quote: A decision about whether the victim or claimant is eligible is usually made within 30 to 45 days.
added.pinpoint: LCLE CVC program page, How the Application is Reviewed
added.source_title: LCLE Crime Victims' Compensation Fund program page

added.title: LCLE CVC Claims page (online applications listed as coming soon)

Boston, MA 02108

Massachusetts Office for Victim Assistance
One Ashburton Place, Suite 1310
Boston, MA 02108

added.summary: The signed application can be emailed to the Victim Compensation correspondence address printed on the form.

Return signed and completed application via mail, fax, or email to:

Massachusetts Office for Victim Assistance

added.summary: Attach copies of receipts for the expenses being claimed.
added.quote: Please check types of expenses for which you seek compensation and attach copies of bills and/or receipts.

added.summary: The claim must come with copies of bills and other documents that verify it.
added.quote: The claim must be accompanied by copies of bills and other supporting documentation necessary to verify the claim
added.source_title: 124 CMR 2.00, Compensation for Victims of Violent Crimes (MOVA; effective 8/4/25, Mass. Register #1564)

added.summary: A survivor who declined the forensic exam kit, or was past the kit window, must send a copy of the police report with the application.
added.quote: In these circumstances, patients must submit a copy of their police report with their Victim Compensation Application.
added.pinpoint: MA SANE Protocol, Section X (Patient declines MSAECK or patient ineligible for MSAECK)
added.source_title: Mass.gov DPH, MA SANE Protocol Section X: Victim Compensation

added.summary: For lost wages, MOVA can ask for the employer's verification of employment, dates missed, net weekly pay and leave used.

verification from the victim's employer (or, if self-employed, from the victim's own

added.source_title: 124 CMR 2.00, Compensation for Victims of Violent Crimes (MOVA; effective 8/4/25, Mass. Register #1564)

added.summary: For lost wages, MOVA can ask for a letter from a treating provider saying the victim cannot work, or can work only part time, because of the crime.
added.quote:
Upon request by the Agency, the victim must submit a disability letter from a treating health
care provider demonstrating that the victim is disabled from working full time, or limited to
working part time, as a direct result of the crime
added.source_title: 124 CMR 2.00, Compensation for Victims of Violent Crimes (MOVA; effective 8/4/25, Mass. Register #1564)

added.summary: MOVA says a decision generally comes 4 to 6 months after applying.
added.quote: In general, you will receive a decision 4 to 6 months later.

added.source_title: Mass.gov, Applying for Victims of Violent Crime Assistance (MOVA)

added.summary: A survivor applies online through the Attorney General's victims' compensation portal.
added.quote: Apply online for victims' compensation
added.pinpoint: AG Victims' Compensation page, Victims links
added.source_title: Maine AG: Victims' Compensation

added.summary: The application must be signed, and it includes release forms that let staff collect and verify information.
added.quote: The application must be signed and sent to the Victims' Compensation Board. Release forms are included with the application to allow staff to compile and verify information.
added.pinpoint: AG Program Law and History, Application Process
added.source_title: Maine AG: Victims' Compensation Program Law and History

added.summary: A claim must include documentation of every expense claimed, including medical reports and records.
added.quote: Claims must include documentation of all eligible expenses and losses for which the claimant seeks compensation, including but not limited to medical reports, records and bills, funeral bills and employment records when lost wages are sought.
added.source_title: 5 M.R.S. 3360-D (Claims)

added.summary: A claim must include the bills for the expenses claimed, such as medical bills.
added.quote: Claims must include documentation of all eligible expenses and losses for which the claimant seeks compensation, including but not limited to medical reports, records and bills, funeral bills and employment records when lost wages are sought.
added.source_title: 5 M.R.S. 3360-D (Claims)

added.summary: A survivor claiming lost wages must include employment records.
added.quote: Claims must include documentation of all eligible expenses and losses for which the claimant seeks compensation, including but not limited to medical reports, records and bills, funeral bills and employment records when lost wages are sought.
added.source_title: 5 M.R.S. 3360-D (Claims)

added.summary: A claim must include records about insurance, workers' compensation, and state or federal assistance programs.
added.quote: Claims must include records related to insurance, workers' compensation, federal and state entitlement and assistance programs.
added.source_title: 5 M.R.S. 3360-D (Claims)

added.summary: The claim must give the date and circumstances of the crime and name the law enforcement agency it was reported to.
added.quote: Claims must specify the date, the nature and circumstances of the crime and the law enforcement agency to which the crime was reported.
added.source_title: 5 M.R.S. 3360-D (Claims)

added.summary: For counseling costs, the counselor must send a completed treatment plan; the case cannot go to the Board without it.
added.quote: Your case cannot go before the Board without the completed treatment plan.
added.pinpoint: AG Mental Health Counseling Guidelines
added.source_title: Maine AG: Mental Health Counseling Guidelines

added.summary: An attorney is not required; if one represents you, the attorney must file a Letter of Appearance with the application.

added.summary: For medical, dental, equipment, remedial treatment, or counseling costs, include itemized copies of all bills.

added.summary: For medical, dental, equipment, remedial treatment, or counseling costs, include copies of any paid receipts.

added.source_title: Crime Victim Services Compensation Application Checklist (English, Revised 02/2025)

added.summary: For a future procedure that needs preauthorization, include an itemized estimate from the provider.
added.quote: If you are applying for a procedure that has not taken place yet, and you need a preauthorization, please provide an itemized estimate from the provider for the procedure.
added.pinpoint: Application Checklist, Medical, Dental, Equipment, Nonmedical Remedial Treatment, and/or Counseling, item 4
added.source_title: Crime Victim Services Compensation Application Checklist (English, Revised 02/2025)

added.summary: For counseling, include your mental health provider's name, phone number, address, email, and fax number if available.
added.quote: If you are applying for counseling, provide your mental health provider's contact information, including name, phone number, address, email address, and fax number, if available.
added.pinpoint: Application Checklist, Medical, Dental, Equipment, Nonmedical Remedial Treatment, and/or Counseling, item 6
added.source_title: Crime Victim Services Compensation Application Checklist (English, Revised 02/2025)

added.summary: For lost earnings, if not self-employed, include 2 or 3 pay stubs from just before the injury showing gross pay, net pay, and tax deductions.
added.quote: If you are applying for loss of earnings and are NOT self-employed, provide copies of 2 or 3 pay stubs paid just before the date of injury showing gross pay, net pay, and tax deductions.
added.pinpoint: Application Checklist, Loss of Earnings or Support, item 1
added.source_title: Crime Victim Services Compensation Application Checklist (English, Revised 02/2025)

added.summary: For lost earnings, if self-employed, include your most recent federal and state income tax return with Schedule C.
added.quote: If you are applying for loss of earnings and ARE self-employed, provide a copy of the most recent Federal and State Income Tax Return including Schedule C.
added.pinpoint: Application Checklist, Loss of Earnings or Support, item 2
added.source_title: Crime Victim Services Compensation Application Checklist (English, Revised 02/2025)

added.summary: For lost earnings, include a written statement from your physician verifying the disability and the dates you were off work.
added.quote: If you are applying for loss of earnings, submit a written disability statement from your physician verifying your disability and specific dates off work.
added.pinpoint: Application Checklist, Loss of Earnings or Support, item 3
added.source_title: Crime Victim Services Compensation Application Checklist (English, Revised 02/2025)

added.summary: For relocation, include a signed lease in your name that shows the landlord's name, address, and phone number.
added.quote: Submit a signed copy of the lease with the victim's or claimant's name on the lease. The lease must show the name, address, and phone number of the landlord or property owner.
added.pinpoint: Application Checklist, Relocation (Temporary) or Relocation (Permanent), item 1
added.source_title: Crime Victim Services Compensation Application Checklist (English, Revised 02/2025)

added.summary: For relocation, include a written estimate from the utility provider to start utilities, in your name.
added.quote: Submit a written estimate from utility provider(s) to start utilities. Victim's or claimant's name must be on the estimate or invoice.
added.pinpoint: Application Checklist, Relocation (Temporary) or Relocation (Permanent), item 2
added.source_title: Crime Victim Services Compensation Application Checklist (English, Revised 02/2025)

added.summary: For relocation, include a written estimate or invoice for moving services, in your name.
added.quote: Submit a written estimate or invoice for moving services. Victim's or claimant's name must be on the estimate or invoice.
added.pinpoint: Application Checklist, Relocation (Temporary) or Relocation (Permanent), item 3
added.source_title: Crime Victim Services Compensation Application Checklist (English, Revised 02/2025)

added.summary: For temporary lodging, include the written lease or lodging agreement, in your name.
added.quote: Submit a written lease or agreement for temporary lodging. Victim's or claimant's name must be on the lease or agreement.
added.pinpoint: Application Checklist, Relocation (Temporary) or Relocation (Permanent), item 4
added.source_title: Crime Victim Services Compensation Application Checklist (English, Revised 02/2025)

added.summary: If you already paid relocation costs, include the receipts.
added.quote: If you have made any payments out-of-pocket for your relocation expenses, please submit receipt(s) to verify your payment(s).
added.pinpoint: Application Checklist, Relocation (Temporary) or Relocation (Permanent), item 5
added.source_title: Crime Victim Services Compensation Application Checklist (English, Revised 02/2025)

added.summary: For residential security at a rental, include the landlord's name and contact information; the landlord's authorization may be requested.
added.quote: If your residence is a rental, please provide the landlord's name and contact information.
added.pinpoint: Application Checklist, Residential Security, item 1
added.source_title: Crime Victim Services Compensation Application Checklist (English, Revised 02/2025)

added.summary: For residential security, include your homeowner's or renter's insurance coverage, if you have it.
added.quote: Submit the homeowner's or renter's insurance policy coverage, if applicable.
added.pinpoint: Application Checklist, Residential Security, item 2
added.source_title: Crime Victim Services Compensation Application Checklist (English, Revised 02/2025)

added.summary: For residential security, include an itemization of costs and installation fees, plus receipts if you paid.
added.quote: Submit itemization of costs, installation fees, and receipt(s) showing payment, if applicable.
added.pinpoint: Application Checklist, Residential Security, item 3
added.source_title: Crime Victim Services Compensation Application Checklist (English, Revised 02/2025)

added.summary: For replacement of items held as evidence, such as clothing or bedding, include verification that they were held as evidence.
added.quote: Submit verification of items held as evidence in this crime.
added.pinpoint: Application Checklist, Replacement Costs, item 1
added.source_title: Crime Victim Services Compensation Application Checklist (English, Revised 02/2025)

added.summary: For items held as evidence, include itemized receipts or estimates for replacing them.
added.quote: Submit itemized receipt(s) for the items held as evidence and/or estimate(s) for the replacement of the items held as evidence.
added.pinpoint: Application Checklist, Replacement Costs, item 2
added.source_title: Crime Victim Services Compensation Application Checklist (English, Revised 02/2025)

added.summary: For crime scene clean-up, include an itemized invoice or estimate, and receipts if you paid.
added.quote: Submit an itemized invoice or estimate for clean-up. If you made payment, please submit receipt(s) to verify.
added.pinpoint: Application Checklist, Crime Scene Clean-Up, item 1
added.source_title: Crime Victim Services Compensation Application Checklist (English, Revised 02/2025)

added.summary: For crime scene clean-up, include the homeowner's or renter's insurance determination, if applicable.
added.quote: Submit the homeowner's or renter's insurance determination, if applicable.
added.pinpoint: Application Checklist, Crime Scene Clean-Up, item 2
added.source_title: Crime Victim Services Compensation Application Checklist (English, Revised 02/2025)

added.summary: For funeral or burial costs, include itemized funeral home or cemetery bills and any paid receipts.
added.quote: Submit an itemized copy of the funeral home and/or cemetery bill(s), plus copies of any paid receipts.
added.pinpoint: Application Checklist, Funeral/Burial Benefits, item 1
added.source_title: Crime Victim Services Compensation Application Checklist (English, Revised 02/2025)

added.summary: If someone else paid toward the funeral and lets you be reimbursed, include their written statement authorizing it.
added.quote: If somebody other than you made a payment toward the funeral costs, and they allow you to be reimbursed for their payment, provide a written statement from that person authorizing you to be reimbursed for that payment.
added.pinpoint: Application Checklist, Funeral/Burial Benefits, item 2
added.source_title: Crime Victim Services Compensation Application Checklist (English, Revised 02/2025)

added.summary: For loss of support, include the Social Security Survivor's Benefit Statement for you and your dependents.
added.quote: If you are applying for loss of support, provide the Social Security Survivor's Benefit Statement for you and/or your dependents.
added.pinpoint: Application Checklist, Loss of Earnings or Support, item 4
added.source_title: Crime Victim Services Compensation Application Checklist (English, Revised 02/2025)

added.summary: For loss of support, include the court order for child support, if there is one.
added.quote: If you are applying for loss of support, provide a copy of the Court Order for Child Support, if applicable.
added.pinpoint: Application Checklist, Loss of Earnings or Support, item 5
added.source_title: Crime Victim Services Compensation Application Checklist (English, Revised 02/2025)

added.summary: For loss of support, include the victim's most recent federal and state tax returns and W-2 forms.
added.quote: If you are applying for loss of support, provide a copy of the victim's most recent Federal and State Income Tax Returns and W-2 forms.
added.pinpoint: Application Checklist, Loss of Earnings or Support, item 6
added.source_title: Crime Victim Services Compensation Application Checklist (English, Revised 02/2025)

added.summary: A survivor can fill out the Crime Victim Compensation application online through the Attorney General's portal.

added.summary: Fill out the paper application, attach itemized bills and other required documents, and mail it to the Crime Victim Compensation Division's post office box in Jackson.

added.summary: The printed application can also be faxed to the program using the fax number on the form.
added.quote: print the form found online and mail or fax it using the information on the form.

added.source_title: Mississippi Crime Victim Compensation brochure (2025)

added.summary: The application has to be filled out completely and signed.
added.quote: Application must be completed and signed.
added.pinpoint: Application (rev. 12.9.2025), page 1
added.source_title: Crime Victim Compensation Application (rev. 12.9.2025)

added.summary: Attach itemized bills and any other documentation for the expenses being claimed.
added.quote: attach any required documentation, including itemized bills
added.pinpoint: Application (rev. 12.9.2025), Instructions
added.source_title: Crime Victim Compensation Application (rev. 12.9.2025)

added.summary: For medical expenses, provide an itemized statement listing each service's date, type, diagnostic and treatment codes, and charge.
added.quote: The victim/claimant shall provide an itemized statement indicating date of service, type of service, diagnostic code, treatment code and charge for each service, product or treatment.
added.pinpoint: 3 Miss. Admin. Code Pt. 1, R. 301(2)(a)
added.source_title: Miss. Admin. Code Title 3, Part 1: Division of Victim Compensation rules

added.summary: Over-the-counter medical supplies need an itemized receipt that shows the item.

added.source_title: Miss. Admin. Code Title 3, Part 1: Division of Victim Compensation rules

added.summary: The insurance and other benefits section must be filled in, because the program pays only after every other source.
added.quote: By law, the Crime Victim Compensation Division is payer of last resort and must verify all sources available for payment of expenses. This section must be completed.

added.source_title: Crime Victim Compensation Application (rev. 12.9.2025)

added.summary: If claiming lost wages, provide a report of earnings and information on other benefit sources.

added.source_title: Miss. Admin. Code Title 3, Part 1: Division of Victim Compensation rules

added.summary: A self-employed applicant claiming lost wages attaches a copy of their latest federal income tax return.
added.quote: If you are self-employed, attach a copy of your latest federal income tax return.
added.pinpoint: Application (rev. 12.9.2025), Section D
added.source_title: Crime Victim Compensation Application (rev. 12.9.2025)

added.summary: If work was missed for more than a week, include a disability statement from the victim's doctor giving how long the disability lasted.
added.quote: If loss of work due to victim's physical injuries and/or psychological trauma is longer than one work week, the victim or claimant shall provide a disability statement from the victim's attending licensed medical doctor or doctor of osteopathy licensed to practice medicine
added.pinpoint: 3 Miss. Admin. Code Pt. 1, R. 303(4)(b)
added.source_title: Miss. Admin. Code Title 3, Part 1: Division of Victim Compensation rules

added.summary: For counseling costs, the counselor fills out the program's Mental Health Services and Expenses Report form.
added.quote: The mental health provider shall provide a completed Mental Health Services and Expenses Report form
added.pinpoint: 3 Miss. Admin. Code Pt. 1, R. 302(3)(b)
added.source_title: Miss. Admin. Code Title 3, Part 1: Division of Victim Compensation rules

added.summary: For medical or counseling travel, submit the program's travel reimbursement request form.
added.quote: The victim/claimant shall submit a travel reimbursement request form as prescribed by the Division.
added.pinpoint: 3 Miss. Admin. Code Pt. 1, R. 301(7)(h)
added.source_title: Miss. Admin. Code Title 3, Part 1: Division of Victim Compensation rules

added.summary: The program says an eligibility decision is usually made within 90 days of receiving the application.
added.quote: A decision about whether the victim or claimant is eligible is usually made within 90 days.

added.source_title: NC DPS Victim Compensation Program page and FAQ

added.summary: Funeral claims need a copy of the death certificate, the itemized funeral bill, and the law enforcement report.
added.quote: Submit a copy of the death certificate, itemized funeral bill and the law enforcement report.
added.pinpoint: NC DPS Victim Compensation Program FAQ, 'What paperwork do I need to submit with my application?' (Funeral expenses)
added.source_title: NC DPS Victim Compensation Program page and FAQ

added.summary: The program says the average processing time is three to six months from when it receives the application.
added.quote: From the time an application is received, the average processing time is between three to six months.
added.pinpoint: NC DPS Victim Compensation Program FAQ, 'What happens after I submit my application?'
added.source_title: NC DPS Victim Compensation Program page and FAQ

from.name: law-2026-10-03-52abf94

added.summary: Apply online through the ND DOCR Crime Victim's Compensation Application portal linked from the program page.
added.quote: Clicking the link below will take you to the online application for Crime Victim
added.pinpoint: Program page, Crime Victims Compensation Application and Forms
added.source_title: ND DOCR Crime Victims Compensation program page

added.summary: Allow 2 to 4 weeks for the program to process an application or a reimbursement request.
added.quote: Please allow 2-4 weeks for processing CVC application or claim reimbursement requests.
added.pinpoint: Program page, Claim Status
added.source_title: ND DOCR Crime Victims Compensation program page

added.summary: Submit a completed application on the program's form, signed by the claimant or a parent, guardian, or legal representative; an employer, provider, or insurer cannot apply for you.
added.quote: A claimant for benefits shall submit a completed application for compensation signed by the claimant or the claimant's parent, guardian, or legal representative on an application form prescribed by the division.
added.source_title: N.D. Admin. Code ch. 94-03-03 (application for compensation)

added.summary: If the crime was not reported to law enforcement in time, explain the reason for the late report in the application.
added.quote: There may be a justifiable reason for the late report. Please explain.
added.pinpoint: CVC Application Tips, Section 3 (Incident Information, continued)
added.source_title: ND DOCR CVC Application Tips (PDF)

added.summary: For medical costs, include a billing statement showing the provider's name, business address, phone number, and treatment plan.
added.quote: A request for compensation for medical services must include a billing statement containing the medical provider's name, business address, telephone number, treatment plan, and other information necessary for the division to determine the claim is for services directly related to the criminally injurious conduct.
added.source_title: N.D. Admin. Code ch. 94-03-03 (application for compensation)

added.summary: For dental costs, include a billing statement showing the dentist's name, business address, phone number, and treatment plan.
added.quote: A request for compensation for dental services must include a billing statement containing the dental provider's name, business address, telephone number, treatment plan, and other information necessary for the division to determine the claim is for services directly related to the criminally injurious conduct.
added.source_title: N.D. Admin. Code ch. 94-03-03 (application for compensation)

added.summary: For counseling, the provider's billing statement must list itemized transactions with the provider's name, business address, and phone number.
added.quote: A billing statement of itemized transactions containing the provider's name, business address, and telephone number.
added.pinpoint: CVC Mental Health Treatment Policy and Provider Verification Form (Rev. 6/2025), Verification Requirements
added.source_title: ND CVC Mental Health Treatment Policy and Provider Verification Form (Rev. 6/2025)

added.summary: For counseling, the provider returns the CVC Provider Verification Form with the billing invoice.
added.quote: The Provider Verification Form portion is to be returned with the billing invoice for reimbursement of services to the CVC program.
added.pinpoint: CVC Mental Health Treatment Policy and Provider Verification Form (Rev. 6/2025), introduction
added.source_title: ND CVC Mental Health Treatment Policy and Provider Verification Form (Rev. 6/2025)

added.summary: For lost wages, include written documentation from a medical or mental health provider and from your employer.
added.quote: A claim for reimbursement for work loss must include written documentation from a medical or mental health provider, the claimant's employer, and information the division may request that supports payment for work loss.
added.source_title: N.D. Admin. Code ch. 94-03-03 (application for compensation)

added.summary: For lost wages, the employer you worked for at the time of the crime completes the CVC Employer's Report.
added.quote: FORM MUST BE COMPLETED BY EMPLOYER YOU WERE WORKING FOR AT THE TIME OF THE CRIME INCIDENT.
added.pinpoint: Work Loss - Employer's Report, SFN 12437
added.source_title: ND CVC Work Loss - Employer's Report (SFN 12437, Rev. 06-2018)

added.summary: For lost wages, if you are self-employed, include a copy of your federal income tax return for the prior year.
added.quote: Self-employed victims shall provide a copy of federal income tax return for one year prior and other substantial verification of work loss or profits the division determines is necessary to support payment for work loss.
added.source_title: N.D. Admin. Code ch. 94-03-03 (application for compensation)

added.summary: For lost wages, a medical provider who treated your crime injuries completes the CVC Physician's Report.
added.quote: FORM MUST BE COMPLETED BY A MEDICAL PROVIDER WHO TREATED YOU FOR YOUR CRIME INJURIES.
added.pinpoint: Work Loss - Physician's Report, SFN 60497
added.source_title: ND CVC Work Loss - Physician's Report (SFN 60497, Rev. 06-2018)

added.summary: For travel and lodging, include your receipts.
added.quote: The claimant shall submit receipts for travel and lodging expenses to the division.
added.source_title: N.D. Admin. Code ch. 94-03-03 (application for compensation)

added.summary: For funeral and burial costs, include itemized receipts.
added.quote: The claimant shall submit itemized receipts for reimbursement under this section.
added.source_title: N.D. Admin. Code ch. 94-03-03 (application for compensation)

added.summary: For replacement services, include receipts showing the billed amount and the type of service.
added.quote: A claim for reimbursement for replacement services loss must include receipts for the billed amount, type of service provided, and other information necessary for the division to determine the claim is for services directly related to the criminally injurious conduct.
added.source_title: N.D. Admin. Code ch. 94-03-03 (application for compensation)

added.summary: For loss of support, include proof of the support the victim gave dependents before the crime, such as tax forms, a certified death certificate, or birth certificates.
added.quote: A claim for loss of support must include verification of the amount of support the victim provided to dependents prior to the criminally injurious conduct.
added.source_title: N.D. Admin. Code ch. 94-03-03 (application for compensation)

added.summary: Before the program pays, you or the provider must show what insurance or another collateral source paid, or that it did not cover the service.
added.quote: Before payment is made from the division, either the provider or the claimant shall provide documentation that: a. Verifies the amount paid by the collateral source; or b. Verifies the applicant or service was not covered by the collateral source.
added.pinpoint: N.D. Admin. Code 94-03-03-06 (collateral sources)
added.source_title: N.D. Admin. Code ch. 94-03-03 (application for compensation)

added.summary: The program may ask you to sign its Authorization to Disclose Protected Health Information form so it can get records it needs to decide the claim.
added.quote: The DOCR may, however, require that you authorize disclosure of your health information if needed to make a determination about your claim.
added.pinpoint: Authorization to Disclose Protected Health Information, SFN 61353, Privacy Statement
added.source_title: ND CVC Authorization to Disclose Protected Health Information (SFN 61353)

added.title: ND CVC Work Loss - Employer's Report (SFN 12437, Rev. 06-2018)
ND CVC Work Loss - Physician's Report (SFN 60497, Rev. 06-2018)
ND CVC Authorization to Disclose Protected Health Information (SFN 61353)

added.summary: Mail the completed, signed application and documentation to the Nebraska Crime Victim's Reparations Program, PO Box 94946, Lincoln, NE 68509-4946.
added.quote: Return the completed/signed application and documentation to the below address: Nebraska Crime Victim’s Reparations Program PO Box 94946 Lincoln, NE 68509-4946
added.pinpoint: CVR Claim Application (Oct 2023), cover page
added.source_title: CVR Claim Application (October 2023)

added.summary: Email the claim application and the supporting documentation requested to ncc.cvr@nebraska.gov.
added.quote: Submit, along with supporting documentation requested, by email or mailing to: CVR Claim → ncc.cvr@nebraska.gov
added.pinpoint: Crime Victim Reparations program page, Apply
added.source_title: Nebraska Crime Commission: Crime Victim Reparations program page

added.summary: The application's return-to block also lists the program's fax number, 402.471.2837.
added.pinpoint: CVR Claim Application (Oct 2023), cover page
added.source_title: CVR Claim Application (October 2023)

added.summary: Include itemized copies of all medical bills related to the incident.
added.quote: Submit itemized copies of all medical bills relating to the incident.
added.pinpoint: FAQ, What must I do to apply for compensation?
added.source_title: CVR Frequently Asked Questions (updated 4-5-2023)

added.summary: Attach copies of crime-related bills and any receipts for bills you already paid.
added.quote: Attach copies of crime related bills and any paid receipts.
added.pinpoint: CVR Claim Application (Oct 2023), Section 4: Expenses
added.source_title: CVR Claim Application (October 2023)

added.summary: Sign and date the Authorization to Release Information; no action is taken on the claim until it is signed.
added.quote: This authorization is an integral part of your application and must be signed and dated by the victim or claimant before any action will be taken on your claim.
added.pinpoint: CVR Claim Application (Oct 2023), Authorization to Release Information
added.source_title: CVR Claim Application (October 2023)

added.summary: Complete the citizenship attestation; if you attest as a qualified alien, you agree to provide a copy of your USCIS documentation.
added.quote: I am a qualified alien under the federal Immigration and Nationality Act and I agree to provide a copy of my USCIS documentation.
added.pinpoint: CVR Claim Application (Oct 2023), United States Citizenship Attestation
added.source_title: CVR Claim Application (October 2023)

added.summary: For lost wages, include pay stubs or an earning statement for the pay periods of work missed because of the incident.
added.quote: Copy of pay stubs or an earning statement for the pay period(s) for missed work as a result of the incident.
added.pinpoint: CVR Claim Application (Oct 2023), Section 6: Loss of Wage Information
added.source_title: CVR Claim Application (October 2023)

added.summary: For lost wages when self-employed, include your most recent federal tax returns with Schedule C and copies of estimates, bids, or contracts.
added.quote: If Self-Employed: submit the most recent federal tax returns including the schedule C form, Copies of Estimates, Bids, and/or Contracts.
added.pinpoint: CVR Claim Application (Oct 2023), Section 6: Loss of Wage Information
added.source_title: CVR Claim Application (October 2023)

added.summary: For lost wages, include a doctor's release back to work.
added.quote: A Doctor’s release back to work.
added.pinpoint: CVR Claim Application (Oct 2023), Section 6: Loss of Wage Information
added.source_title: CVR Claim Application (October 2023)

added.summary: For funeral or burial expenses, a copy of the death certificate is needed.
added.quote: Funeral or Burial Expenses (A copy of the death certificate will need to be provided.)
added.pinpoint: CVR Claim Application (Oct 2023), Section 4: Expenses
added.source_title: CVR Claim Application (October 2023)

added.summary: By statute, a hearing officer rules on an application within 180 days after receiving all required information; the clock does not start until the file is complete.
added.quote: A hearing officer shall consider and rule upon any application made under the Nebraska Crime Victim's Reparations Act within one hundred eighty days after receipt of all required information related to the crime.
added.pinpoint: Claims Process, quoting Neb. Rev. Stat. 81-1809(1)
added.source_title: CVR Claims Process

added.summary: The program says claims are typically fully processed within 6 to 9 months.
added.quote: CVR program applications take time, typically claims are fully processed within 6-9 months.
added.pinpoint: CVR pamphlet (English), back panel
added.source_title: Nebraska Crime Victim's Reparations Program pamphlet (English)

added.title: CVR Claims Process

added.summary: Mail the completed paper application to the Victims' Compensation Program at the Department of Justice in Concord. This is the return address printed on the application form.
added.quote: Please return completed application to: New Hampshire Victims' Compensation Program Department of Justice 33 Capitol Street Concord, N.H. 03301-6397
added.pinpoint: Application, page 7 (return address)
added.source_title: New Hampshire Victims' Compensation Program Application Form (rev. 02/11/2021)

added.summary: The program page lists a newer office address in Concord (Granite Place South). The form still prints the Capitol Street address, so a survivor may want to call the program to confirm which address to use.
added.quote: How To Contact Our Office New Hampshire Victims' Compensation Program Department of Justice 1 Granite Place South Concord, NH 03301
added.pinpoint: Program page, How To Contact Our Office
added.source_title: New Hampshire DOJ, Victims' Compensation Program page and FAQ

added.summary: For medical, dental, or counseling costs, list every provider and enclose copies of their bills if you have them.
added.quote: If applicable, list all providers that provided treatment, including hospital, doctors, dentists, mental health counselors, ambulance, radiology and prescriptions (drugs and eyeglasses). Attach additional sheets if necessary. If available, please enclose copies of bills.
added.pinpoint: Application, Section 6 (Medical/Counseling Information)
added.source_title: New Hampshire Victims' Compensation Program Application Form (rev. 02/11/2021)

added.summary: After the application arrives, the program may ask for photocopies of all crime-related counseling bills.
added.quote: Photocopies of all crime-related mental health counseling bills
added.source_title: N.H. Admin. Rules, Chapter Jus 600, Victims' Compensation

added.summary: To claim medical or hospital costs, sign a HIPAA-compliant medical release so the program can get itemized statements and records from your providers.
added.quote: If a claimant seeks compensation for medical expenses, the victim or victim's parent or guardian shall complete and submit a HIPAA- compliant hospital and/or medical release.
added.source_title: N.H. Admin. Rules, Chapter Jus 600, Victims' Compensation

added.summary: To claim lost wages, fill in the employment section and send copies of your pay stubs.
added.quote: If yes, complete the following section, and submit copies of your pay stubs.
added.pinpoint: Application, Section 8 (Employment Information)
added.source_title: New Hampshire Victims' Compensation Program Application Form (rev. 02/11/2021)

added.summary: If you were self-employed, send a copy of your tax return for the year before the crime instead of pay stubs.
added.quote: If you were self-employed at the time of the crime, please submit a copy of your tax return documentation for the year before the crime.
added.pinpoint: Application, Section 8 (Employment Information)
added.source_title: New Hampshire Victims' Compensation Program Application Form (rev. 02/11/2021)

added.summary: If you missed more than two weeks of work, include a doctor's statement saying how long you were unable to work.
added.quote: If you have missed more than two weeks of work, please provide a doctor's statement verifying length of time you were unable to work.
added.pinpoint: Application, Section 8 (Employment Information)
added.source_title: New Hampshire Victims' Compensation Program Application Form (rev. 02/11/2021)

added.summary: For lost wages, keep and send copies of written confirmations of crime-related appointments such as medical, counseling, and police meetings.
added.quote: Copies of all written confirmations of appointments with medical providers, mental health providers, police and other law-enforcement officials, and any other appointments necessitated as a direct result of the crime.
added.source_title: N.H. Admin. Rules, Chapter Jus 600, Victims' Compensation

added.summary: If the crime involved a motor vehicle, include your auto insurance policy declarations page.
added.quote: Did the crime involve motor vehicles? (If yes, please provide your automobile insurance policy declarations page.)
added.pinpoint: Application, Section 9 (Restitution and Civil Action)
added.source_title: New Hampshire Victims' Compensation Program Application Form (rev. 02/11/2021)

added.summary: If insurance, leave, benefits, restitution, or any other resource might cover part of the costs, explain it on a separate sheet and attach it.
added.quote: please explain in full on a separate piece of paper and attach it to this application.
added.pinpoint: Application, Section 12 (Statement of Facts and Authorization)
added.source_title: New Hampshire Victims' Compensation Program Application Form (rev. 02/11/2021)

added.summary: If you applied for Medicaid, Medicare, hospital free care, or public assistance and were turned down, attach copies of the denial documents.
added.quote: attach copies of the documents that show your ineligibility for public assistance.
added.pinpoint: Application, Section 12 (Statement of Facts and Authorization)
added.source_title: New Hampshire Victims' Compensation Program Application Form (rev. 02/11/2021)

added.summary: After the program receives the application, staff will contact the applicant by mail or email within 2 weeks. This is first contact, not a decision.
added.quote: Once the program receives your application, you will be contacted by mail or email within 2 weeks.
added.pinpoint: Program page FAQ, How Long Will It Take?
added.source_title: New Hampshire DOJ, Victims' Compensation Program page and FAQ

added.summary: Once an application is complete, the rules say no more than 60 days should pass before the commission can decide. The program page warns the whole process may take several months or longer while police reports are gathered.
added.quote: In no case shall placement on the agenda result in the passage of more than 60 days after the claimant submitted a completed application before a decision can be made by the commission.
added.source_title: N.H. Admin. Rules, Chapter Jus 600, Victims' Compensation
