added.summary: Applications can be filed online through the VCCO claims system.
added.quote: For applications and submission of documents, you may: File online @ www.njvictims.org
added.pinpoint: NJ VCCO Contact page, applications and submission of documents
added.source_title: NJ VCCO Contact page

added.summary: Paper applications go by mail to the VCCO office in Newark.
added.quote:
Mail all applications
to Newark office at:
VCCO
50 Park Place, 5th floor
Newark, NJ 07102
added.pinpoint: NJ VCCO Claim Application and Instructions (oag.rev.8.25.20), Instructions page II sidebar
added.source_title: NJ VCCO Application and Instructions (rev. 8/25/20)

added.summary: Applications and documents can be faxed to the VCCO.
added.pinpoint: NJ VCCO Contact page, applications and submission of documents
added.source_title: NJ VCCO Contact page

added.summary: Attach a copy of the police incident report if you have one; otherwise the VCCO requests it.
added.quote:
Attach a copy
of the incident report. If you don't have one, the
VCCO will request one from the police and/or
prosecutor.
added.pinpoint: NJ VCCO Claim Application and Instructions (oag.rev.8.25.20), Instructions, Section 4
added.source_title: NJ VCCO Application and Instructions (rev. 8/25/20)

added.summary: Include copies of itemized receipts with the application.
added.quote:
Include
copies of as much related information (i.e. copies of itemized receipts,
bills, insurance statements) as you have.
added.pinpoint: NJ VCCO Claim Application and Instructions (oag.rev.8.25.20), Instructions page II
added.source_title: NJ VCCO Application and Instructions (rev. 8/25/20)

added.summary: Send copies of any itemized medical or counseling bills you already have.
added.quote:
If you already
have itemized bills, please send copies with
your application.
added.pinpoint: NJ VCCO Claim Application and Instructions (oag.rev.8.25.20), Instructions, Section 7
added.source_title: NJ VCCO Application and Instructions (rev. 8/25/20)

added.summary: Include copies of insurance statements with the application.
added.quote:
Include
copies of as much related information (i.e. copies of itemized receipts,
bills, insurance statements) as you have.
added.pinpoint: NJ VCCO Claim Application and Instructions (oag.rev.8.25.20), Instructions page II
added.source_title: NJ VCCO Application and Instructions (rev. 8/25/20)

added.summary: For lost wages, supply pay stubs from before the crime and from your return to work.
added.quote:
If available, please supply your pay stubs from the week before the crime, the week you returned to work
and a letter from your doctor stating your period of disability.
added.pinpoint: NJ VCCO Claim Application and Instructions (oag.rev.8.25.20), Section 8 (Lost Wages/Support Information)
added.source_title: NJ VCCO Application and Instructions (rev. 8/25/20)

added.summary: For lost wages, supply a doctor's letter stating the period of disability.
added.quote:
If available, please supply your pay stubs from the week before the crime, the week you returned to work
and a letter from your doctor stating your period of disability.
added.pinpoint: NJ VCCO Claim Application and Instructions (oag.rev.8.25.20), Section 8 (Lost Wages/Support Information)
added.source_title: NJ VCCO Application and Instructions (rev. 8/25/20)

added.summary: Self-employed applicants claiming lost wages must supply income and business tax returns for the 2 years before the crime.
added.quote: If you are self-employed, you must supply copies of your income tax returns and business tax returns for the last 2 years before the crime.
added.pinpoint: NJ VCCO Claim Application and Instructions (oag.rev.8.25.20), Section 8 (Lost Wages/Support Information)
added.source_title: NJ VCCO Application and Instructions (rev. 8/25/20)

added.summary: The HIPAA release in the application must be completed, signed and dated before the claim can be processed.
added.quote:
This authorization is necessary to obtain information
from your health care providers under federal law.
It must be completed, signed and dated in order
for the VCCO to process your claim.
added.pinpoint: NJ VCCO Claim Application and Instructions (oag.rev.8.25.20), Instructions, Section 15
added.source_title: NJ VCCO Application and Instructions (rev. 8/25/20)

added.summary: The VCCO decides on an application within 90 days after it acknowledges receiving the completed application and all supporting information; this can be extended for good cause.
added.quote:
The Office will make its determination regarding the application within 90 days of acknowledgment by the
Office of receipt of the completed application and any and all necessary supplemental information
added.source_title: N.J.A.C. 13:75 (VCCO administrative code, OAG copy)

added.summary: The application instructions say claims take 3 months to process once all documentation is received.
added.quote:
the turn around time for processing a claim is 3 months of receipt of
all documentation.
added.pinpoint: NJ VCCO Claim Application and Instructions (oag.rev.8.25.20), Instructions page II
added.source_title: NJ VCCO Application and Instructions (rev. 8/25/20)

added.summary: You can file online through the CVRC application portal, where you sign in or create an account and submit the application.
added.quote: To begin Please choose one of the following options: Sign In OR Create an Account
added.pinpoint: CVRC online application portal, home page
added.source_title: CVRC online compensation application portal (home page)

added.summary: A paper application goes to the Crime Victims Reparation Commission office in Albuquerque; the rules count it as filed on the postmark date.
added.quote: Crime Victims Reparation Commission 6200 Uptown Blvd., Suite 210 Albuquerque, NM 87110
added.pinpoint: Compensation Application page, How do I apply?
added.source_title: CVRC Compensation Application and FAQ page

added.summary: A paper application can be faxed to the commission's office.
added.pinpoint: Compensation Application page, How do I apply?
added.source_title: CVRC Compensation Application and FAQ page

added.summary: The application asks for a copy of the police report if one is available.
added.quote: CRIME INFORMATION (Provide copy of police report if available)
added.pinpoint: Application, Section 4
added.source_title: NM Crime Victims Reparation Commission Application (English, reviewed 02/2025)

added.summary: The commission reviews the application with a complete offense report or a provider incident verification form, which its office requests.
added.quote: The application and related documentation received, including a complete offense report or provider incident verification form (which this office requests), will then be reviewed to determine if the victim and/or claimant are eligible for compensation.
added.pinpoint: Compensation Application page, What happens after I send my application?
added.source_title: CVRC Compensation Application and FAQ page

added.summary: Expenses must be documented with invoices, receipts or canceled checks that show who was paid, who paid, the amount, the date and the service.
added.quote: This documentation must provide the name of payee, the name of payer, the amount paid, date of services, and indicate what service was provided. This documentation may include invoices, receipts and canceled checks. Affidavits and letters shall not be considered proper documentation.
added.source_title: 10.40.2 NMAC (Crime Victims Reparation Commission, Compensation)

added.summary: For lost wages, the employer must give a statement of the work dates missed, hourly wage and average weekly hours.
added.quote: a statement from the employer providing: (a) the dates of work missed due to the incident; (b) hourly wage; (c) the average number of hours worked weekly; and (d) any type of compensation received, such as sick leave, annual leave, unemployment, etc.
added.source_title: 10.40.2 NMAC (Crime Victims Reparation Commission, Compensation)

added.summary: For lost wages, a doctor's statement or medical documentation must show the victim is unable to work.
added.quote: a copy of a doctor's statement certifying that the victim is unable to work; or a doctor's statement included in a medical document, or medical documentation showing the inability of the victim to work.
added.source_title: 10.40.2 NMAC (Crime Victims Reparation Commission, Compensation)

added.summary: Counselors must give commission staff a detailed patient evaluation describing the effect of the victimization.
added.quote: All counselors shall provide the commission staff with the following: (a) detailed patient evaluation describing the effect of the victimization
added.source_title: 10.40.2 NMAC (Crime Victims Reparation Commission, Compensation)

added.summary: If the victim is deceased, the application asks for a copy of the death certificate.
added.quote: DECEASED (Submit copy of death certificate)
added.pinpoint: Application, Section 1
added.source_title: NM Crime Victims Reparation Commission Application (English, reviewed 02/2025)

added.summary: If the victim is incapacitated, the application asks for a power of attorney.
added.quote: INCAPACITATED (Submit a power of attorney)
added.pinpoint: Application, Section 1
added.source_title: NM Crime Victims Reparation Commission Application (English, reviewed 02/2025)

added.summary: The signed Acknowledgement and Authorization page is required for the application to be processed.
added.quote: This authorization is part of your application and must be completed and signed in order to process this application.
added.pinpoint: Application, Acknowledgement and Authorization
added.source_title: NM Crime Victims Reparation Commission Application (English, reviewed 02/2025)

added.summary: An eligibility decision is usually made within 120 days.
added.quote: A decision about whether the victim/claimant is eligible is usually made within 120 days.
added.pinpoint: Compensation Application page, What happens after I send my application?
added.source_title: CVRC Compensation Application and FAQ page

added.title: CVRC online compensation application portal (home page)

added.summary: Attach the bills or estimates for the crime-related expenses you want paid.

added.source_title: Nevada VOCP Application for Victim of Crime Compensation (English, revised 7/30/2026)

added.summary: Attach receipts for crime-related expenses you already paid.
added.quote: Attach your bills, receipts, estimates, or other documents which support your request for payment.
added.pinpoint: Application, Section 4: Tell us about your Crime Related Expenses
added.source_title: Nevada VOCP Application for Victim of Crime Compensation (English, revised 7/30/2026)

added.summary: If the victim has life, medical, dental, or vision insurance, attach the insurance card.
added.quote: Does the Victim/ Applicant have Life, Medical, Dental, or Vision Insurance? Please attach Insurance card.

added.source_title: Nevada VOCP Application for Victim of Crime Compensation (English, revised 7/30/2026)

added.summary: Sign the authorization and release forms that come with the application; all of them are needed to process it.
added.quote: By checking the boxes and signing below, you are giving permission for certain information to be shared. Please read each section carefully. All authorizations are required to process your application.

added.summary: The program needs some document showing the crime occurred, such as a police report, an advocate statement, medical or counseling records, or court papers.

added.source_title: Nevada VOCP Application for Victim of Crime Compensation Instructions and form (2026)

added.summary: Unless the claim is denied at first review, the compensation officer must decide it within 60 days after receiving the application.
added.quote: the compensation officer shall conduct an investigation and, except as otherwise provided in subsection 6, render a decision within 60 days after receipt of the application or order.

added.summary: A paper application and documents can be mailed to the OVS office in Albany.

added.summary: The application and supporting documents can be emailed to the OVS intake address.

added.summary: A claim can be filed online through the OVS Compass Applicant Portal, as a guest or with a NY.gov account.

added.pinpoint: OVS Victim Compensation Claim Application (Feb. 2026), page 1, FAQ: Is there another way to apply?

added.summary: Include all bills and receipts for the expenses described in the application.
added.quote: All bills and receipts for expenses related to goods and services you described in this application.

added.source_title: OVS Victim Compensation Claim Application (English, fillable PDF)

added.summary: Include the bills for the crime-related goods and services claimed.
added.quote: All bills and receipts for expenses related to goods and services you described in this application.
added.pinpoint: OVS Victim Compensation Claim Application (Feb. 2026), page 2, Processing Your Claim
added.source_title: OVS Victim Compensation Claim Application (English, fillable PDF)

added.summary: Include one completed HIPAA authorization for each medical and mental health provider seen for crime-related care.
added.quote: One completed HIPAA form for each medical and mental health provider you saw for services related to this crime.
added.pinpoint: OVS Victim Compensation Claim Application (Feb. 2026), page 2, Processing Your Claim
added.source_title: OVS Victim Compensation Claim Application (English, fillable PDF)

added.summary: Include any letters from insurance companies or government agencies that denied or authorized payment for the claimed expenses.
added.quote: Letters from any insurance or government agencies denying or authorizing payments related to goods and services you described in this application.
added.pinpoint: OVS Victim Compensation Claim Application (Feb. 2026), page 2, Processing Your Claim
added.source_title: OVS Victim Compensation Claim Application (English, fillable PDF)

added.summary: Only one third-party document confirming the crime is needed, and a Crime Verification Form from a victim service provider or medical or mental health professional works.

added.summary: A police or other criminal justice agency report can be submitted as the crime verification document, but it is a choice.

added.source_title: OVS Victim Compensation Claim Application (English, fillable PDF)

added.summary: If a forensic rape exam was done, the survivor can choose to use the exam report in the application.
added.quote: If an FRE was performed, do you want to use the report as part of your application?

added.source_title: OVS Victim Compensation Claim Application (English, fillable PDF)

added.summary: If the victim has Workers' Compensation or disability insurance coverage, OVS needs that provider's decision letter.
added.quote: If the victim has coverage through either Worker's Compensation or a Disability Insurance provider, OVS will need the decision letter from either Worker's Compensation or the Disability Insurance provider to help determine eligibility for compensation.
added.pinpoint: OVS Victim Compensation Claim Application (Feb. 2026), page 16, Workers Compensation/Disability
added.source_title: OVS Victim Compensation Claim Application (English, fillable PDF)

added.summary: The completed paper application can be faxed to either of the Attorney General's fax numbers.

added.summary: New applications can be emailed, but only as a PDF or Word attachment; photos or screenshots of the pages are rejected.

added.pinpoint: AG Apply for Victims Compensation, Two options for filing a claim
added.source_title: Ohio Attorney General, Apply for Victims Compensation page

added.summary: If claiming lost wages, include copies of the 6 paychecks from before the crime.
added.quote: Complete if filing for loss of earnings. Provide copies of 6 paychecks prior to crime.
added.pinpoint: Application, Section 7: Employment Information

added.summary: Send a front and back copy of each insurance or benefit plan card listed on the application.

added.summary: The release in the application must be signed and dated, or the application will not be processed.

added.summary: Apply online through the OCVC online application portal.
added.quote: Use our online application to apply for compensation benefits.
added.pinpoint: VCP Online Access home page, How to Apply
added.source_title: OCVC VCP Online Access claim portal

added.summary: Mail the printed and signed claim form to the Crime Victims Compensation Board at 421 N.W. 13th Street, Suite 290, Oklahoma City.
added.quote: Please Return to: 421 N.W. 13TH STREET, SUITE 290 • OKLAHOMA CITY, OKLAHOMA 73103
added.pinpoint: Official Claim Form (Revised June 2019), page 1 header
added.source_title: OCVC Official Claim Form (2019)

added.summary: Fax the printed and signed claim form to 405/264-5097.
added.pinpoint: Official Claim Form (Revised June 2019), page 1 header
added.source_title: OCVC Official Claim Form (2019)

added.summary: The claim form says it can be emailed once printed and signed; the program email is victimsservices@dac.state.ok.us.
added.quote: Website: www.okvictimscomp.com E-mail: victimsservices@dac.state.ok.us
added.pinpoint: Official Claim Form (Revised June 2019), instructions header
added.source_title: OCVC Official Claim Form (2019)

added.summary: Fill out every section of the paper form and sign all three signature areas on page four.
added.quote: Please thoroughly complete ALL sections and sign all three areas of page four.
added.pinpoint: Official Claim Form (Revised June 2019), Instructions
added.source_title: OCVC Official Claim Form (2019)

added.summary: List the injuries from the crime and attach all itemized medical statements.
added.quote: List the injuries suffered as a result of the crime and attach all itemized medical statements.
added.pinpoint: Official Claim Form (Revised June 2019), Instructions, Section I
added.source_title: OCVC Official Claim Form (2019)

added.summary: Send all the bills you have received with the application; bills that arrive later can be added.
added.quote: Please submit all the bills that you have received. If more come in, they can always be added later.
added.pinpoint: FAQ, Do I need to submit all bills with the application?
added.source_title: OCVC Frequently Asked Questions

added.summary: Out-of-pocket medical, dental, and counseling costs are reimbursed at 100% only with documentation of payment.
added.quote: Medical, dental, and counseling expenses that the victim is out-of-pocket will be reimbursed at 100%, provided there is documentation of payment and no collateral sources exist.
added.pinpoint: Application Process, Payments
added.source_title: DAC Victims Compensation Program page (application process)

added.summary: The DA's Victim-Witness Coordinator requests the police report while documenting the claim.
added.quote: A police report is requested, along with any other forms and reports that may be needed to determine out-of-pocket expenses.
added.pinpoint: Application Process, Documentation
added.source_title: DAC Victims Compensation Program page (application process)

added.summary: Lost income must be verified by both your employer and your attending physician.
added.quote: Work loss must be verified by the employer and the attending physician.
added.pinpoint: Official Claim Form (Revised June 2019), Types of Expenses Covered, Income Loss / Economic Loss
added.source_title: OCVC Official Claim Form (2019)

added.summary: For lost wages, a physician or mental health professional and your employer must verify the disability time.
added.quote: provided the crime prevented the person from working and the disability can be verified by a physician or mental health professional and by the victim’s employer.
added.pinpoint: Official Claim Form (Revised June 2019), Instructions, Section G
added.source_title: OCVC Official Claim Form (2019)

added.summary: If you are self-employed, tax returns for the last 3 years are required for lost wages.
added.quote: IF SELF-EMPLOYED, TAX RETURNS FOR THE LAST THREE YEARS WILL BE REQUIRED.
added.pinpoint: Official Claim Form (Revised June 2019), Section G heading
added.source_title: OCVC Official Claim Form (2019)

added.summary: For mileage to medical or counseling appointments, include documentation from the provider verifying the dates of service.
added.quote: Documentation from the provider verifying the dates of services is required.
added.pinpoint: Official Claim Form (Revised June 2019), Types of Expenses Covered, Travel
added.source_title: OCVC Official Claim Form (2019)

added.summary: To ask for future costs, include an itemized list of the expenses you expect and an explanation.
added.quote: To submit a request for future economic loss, include an itemized list of the expenses you expect to incur, along with an explanation regarding the expense.
added.pinpoint: Official Claim Form (Revised June 2019), Types of Expenses Covered, Future Economic Loss
added.source_title: OCVC Official Claim Form (2019)

added.summary: For future dental work or surgery, ask the attending physician for a written estimate of the work and the cost.
added.quote: For future dental work or surgery necessary to repair damage from the criminal incident, ask the attending physician to write an accurate estimate which clearly states the work to be performed and the cost.
added.pinpoint: Official Claim Form (Revised June 2019), Types of Expenses Covered, Future Economic Loss
added.source_title: OCVC Official Claim Form (2019)

added.summary: For traditional American Indian healing or burial services, receipts must note each item's purpose.
added.quote: In order for reimbursement of these expenses, receipts must be provided with the item’s purpose clearly noted on the receipt.
added.pinpoint: Eligible Expenses, Traditional American Indian Services
added.source_title: OCVC Fund Eligibility page

added.summary: If you paid the forensic exam bill yourself, the program needs your Social Security number to reimburse you.
added.quote: If the victim/guardian paid the bill out of their own pocket, we will need a Social Security number in order to reimburse them.
added.pinpoint: Sexual Assault Examination Fund page
added.source_title: DAC Sexual Assault Examination Fund page

added.summary: Processing can take anywhere from 4 to 12 months depending on where the crime occurred.
added.quote: Depending on the area in which the crime occurred, the processing time could vary anywhere from 4-12 months
added.pinpoint: FAQ, How Long is the Process?
added.source_title: OCVC Frequently Asked Questions

added.summary: Once the Victim-Witness Coordinator sends all documentation, claims are generally docketed for decision within 30 days.
added.quote: Claims are generally placed on a docket for decision within 30 days of receipt of all documentation from the Victim-Witness Coordinator.
added.pinpoint: Application Process
added.source_title: DAC Victims Compensation Program page (application process)

added.summary: Payments are generally made within 3 weeks of approval.
added.quote: PAYMENTS are generally made within three weeks of approval.
added.pinpoint: Application Process, Payments
added.source_title: DAC Victims Compensation Program page (application process)

added.summary: Sexual Assault Examination Fund payments are usually made within 30 days of receiving the application.
added.quote: Payment is usually made within 30 days of the receipt of the application by the Compensation Program.
added.pinpoint: Sexual Assault Examination Fund page
added.source_title: DAC Sexual Assault Examination Fund page

added.title: OCVC Frequently Asked Questions
DAC Victims Compensation Program page (application process)
OCVC VCP Online Access claim portal

doj.state.or.us/cvcportal.

added.summary: Mail the signed paper application to the DOJ Crime Victims' Compensation Program in Salem.
added.quote:
You can mail a paper application to:
Oregon Department of Justice
Crime Victims’ Compensation Program
1162 Court Street NE
Salem, OR 97301–4096
added.pinpoint: CVC Application (2026), page i, How do I apply?
added.source_title: Oregon Crime Victims' Compensation Application (English, 2026)

added.summary: You can also apply in person through a county District Attorney's victim assistance program or a community-based victim services agency.

added.source_title: Oregon DOJ: Crime Victims' Compensation brochure (2024)

added.summary: Sign the release in the application so CVC can verify your information; unsigned applications are returned.

added.summary: For lost earnings, provide employer documentation of employment and time lost and your last paystub before the crime.

added.summary: If you are self-employed and claim lost earnings, submit the previous year's tax records.

added.pinpoint: CVC FAQ, loss of earnings benefit
added.source_title: Oregon DOJ: Crime Victims' Compensation FAQ

added.summary: If you missed more than 2 weeks of work, a work release from your doctor is required.
added.quote: A work release from a doctor is required beyond 2 weeks of missed work.
added.pinpoint: CVC Application (2026), page i, Answers to Commonly Asked Questions
added.source_title: Oregon Crime Victims' Compensation Application (English, 2026)

added.summary: Payment requests must be itemized billing statements listing the services, the provider's name, and the date of service.

added.source_title: Oregon DOJ: Applying for Crime Victims' Compensation

added.summary: If CVC pays for a car rental or bus, train, or air fare instead of mileage, it needs a valid receipt.
added.quote: the Department may, at its discretion, reimburse reasonable and necessary round-trip car rental or bus, train, or air fare, upon submission of a valid receipt.
added.source_title: OAR Chapter 137 Division 76 (Crime Victims' Compensation)

added.summary: CVC confirms receipt by mail or email and issues a claim number within 2 business days.

We will notify you by mail or email when we receive your application. You will receive a

We will contact you again in 60 to 90 days to tell you if we have accepted your
application.

added.source_title: Oregon Crime Victims' Compensation Application (English, 2026)

added.summary: The Secretary of State's Address Confidentiality Program gives survivors of sexual offenses, domestic violence, and stalking a substitute address and free mail forwarding so the person they fear cannot find them through public records. Eligible applicants include victims of a sexual offense such as rape or sexual assault. Enrollment is only through an in-person meeting with a registered Application Assistant at a victim services agency.

rule.summary: By statute, the cost of a sexual assault forensic or medical exam is paid from the state crime victims compensation account rather than by the law enforcement agency.
rule.quote: the cost of forensic and/or medical examinations of alleged victims of sexual assault shall be paid for from the crime victims compensation account
rule.source_title: Idaho Code 19-5303 (Cost of medical exams)

rule.summary: The commission pays for evidence-gathering sexual assault exams after any federal or federally financed payer (such as Medicaid or Medicare); for victims under 18 it pays after any liable third party.
rule.quote: Payment for the costs of forensic and medical examinations of alleged victims of sexual assault performed for the purposes of gathering evidence for possible prosecution, after collections from any federal or federally financed third party who has liability, shall be made by the commission; provided however that payment for the costs of forensic and medical examinations of alleged victims under eighteen (18) years of age shall be made by the commission after collections from any third party who has liability.
rule.source_title: Idaho Code 72-1019 (Compensation benefits)

rule.summary: A medical provider that the program has paid may not try to collect more from the victim for the same services, except when the program cannot pay the full allowable amount.
rule.quote: Except as provided in subsection (3) herein, a medical provider who has received payment from the commission for medical services provided to a victim or claimant under this chapter may not attempt to collect any further payment from the victim or the claimant for those same services.
rule.source_title: Idaho Code 72-1026 (Payments to medical providers)

rule.summary: Compensation to a victim, and to the victim's dependents if the victim dies, for crimes by the same offender within a 6 month period may not exceed $25,000 in total. The statute's wording is built around death cases; the program applies $25,000 as its maximum for all claims.
rule.quote: Compensation payable to a victim and all of the victim's dependents in cases of the victim's death, because of injuries suffered due to an act or acts of criminally injurious conduct involving the same offender and occurring within a six (6) month period, may not exceed twenty-five thousand dollars ($25,000) in the aggregate.
rule.source_title: Idaho Code 72-1019 (Compensation benefits)

rule.summary: Mental health treatment for the victim is capped at $2,500 unless the commission finds extenuating circumstances, in which case it can go up to the overall maximum.
rule.quote: payments for mental health treatment received as a result of the victim's injury may not exceed two thousand five hundred dollars ($2,500) unless the industrial commission finds extenuating circumstances.
rule.source_title: Idaho Code 72-1019 (Compensation benefits)

rule.summary: Family members of a sexual assault victim can get mental health treatment reimbursed, up to $500 per person or $1,500 per family, if the victim was also awarded benefits.
rule.quote: Total payments made under paragraph (a) of this subsection may not exceed five hundred dollars ($500) for each person or one thousand five hundred dollars ($1,500) for a family.
rule.source_title: Idaho Code 72-1019 (Compensation benefits)

rule.summary: A victim with total wage loss gets 66 2/3 percent of their wages, up to $175 per week.
rule.quote: The weekly benefit amount is sixty-six and two-thirds percent (66 2/3%) of the wages received at the time of the criminally injurious conduct, subject to a maximum of one hundred seventy-five dollars ($175).
rule.source_title: Idaho Code 72-1019 (Compensation benefits)

rule.summary: A victim who was employable but not employed at the time of the injury may get up to $150 per week, at the commission's discretion.
rule.quote: who was employable but was not employed at the time of such injury, may in the discretion of the commission be awarded weekly compensation benefits in an amount determined by the commission not to exceed one hundred fifty dollars ($150) per week.
rule.source_title: Idaho Code 72-1019 (Compensation benefits)

rule.summary: Weekly benefits for a victim who was employable but not employed may not exceed $20,000 in total.
rule.quote: Compensation payable to a victim or a victim's dependents under this subsection may not exceed twenty thousand dollars ($20,000), and the limitations of subsection (5) of this section apply to compensation under this subsection.
rule.source_title: Idaho Code 72-1019 (Compensation benefits)

rule.summary: Reasonable funeral, burial or cremation costs, plus transporting the victim's body, are paid up to $5,000 after other collateral sources have paid.
rule.quote: Reasonable funeral and burial or cremation expenses of the victim, together with actual expenses of transportation of the victim's body, shall be paid in an amount not exceeding five thousand dollars ($5,000) if all other collateral sources have properly paid such expenses but have not covered all such expenses.
rule.source_title: Idaho Code 72-1019 (Compensation benefits)

rule.summary: The commission may pay reasonable doctor, hospital, and medicine costs for crime injuries.
rule.quote: The commission may order payment of reasonable expenses actually incurred by the claimant for reasonable services by a physician or surgeon, reasonable hospital services and medicines, mental health counseling and care, and such other treatment as may be approved by the commission for the injuries suffered due to criminally injurious conduct.
rule.source_title: Idaho Code 72-1019 (Compensation benefits)

rule.summary: Mental health counseling and care for crime injuries can be paid.
rule.quote: The commission may order payment of reasonable expenses actually incurred by the claimant for reasonable services by a physician or surgeon, reasonable hospital services and medicines, mental health counseling and care, and such other treatment as may be approved by the commission for the injuries suffered due to criminally injurious conduct.
rule.source_title: Idaho Code 72-1019 (Compensation benefits)

rule.summary: The claimant or a close family member can be reimbursed for necessary travel to get covered benefits, under the commission's rules.
rule.quote: A claimant or a spouse, parent, child or sibling of a claimant or victim may be reimbursed for his or her expenses for necessary travel incurred in connection with obtaining benefits covered pursuant to this chapter and in accordance with rules of the commission.
rule.source_title: Idaho Code 72-1019 (Compensation benefits)

rule.summary: Property damage is not paid, so replacing personal property such as a phone is not covered. Pain and suffering is not paid either.
rule.quote: Compensation benefits are not payable for pain and suffering or property damage.
rule.source_title: Idaho Code 72-1019 (Compensation benefits)

rule.summary: Pain and suffering is not compensated.
rule.quote: Compensation benefits are not payable for pain and suffering or property damage.
rule.source_title: Idaho Code 72-1019 (Compensation benefits)

rule.summary: The claim must be filed within 1 year after the crime; the commission can extend this for good cause.
rule.quote: Compensation may not be awarded unless the claim is filed with the commission within one (1) year after the day the criminally injurious conduct occurred causing the injury or death upon which the claim is based. The time for filing a claim may be extended by the commission for good cause shown.
rule.source_title: Idaho Code 72-1016 (Limitations on awards)

rule.summary: The crime must be reported to law enforcement within 72 hours, unless the commission finds good cause for the delay.
rule.quote: Compensation may not be awarded unless the criminally injurious conduct resulting in injury or death was reported to a law enforcement officer within seventy-two (72) hours after its occurrence or the commission finds there was good cause for the failure to report within that time.
rule.source_title: Idaho Code 72-1016 (Limitations on awards)

rule.summary: To get benefits, the claimant must fully cooperate with law enforcement and prosecutors; the commission may deny or reduce an award if they do not.
rule.quote: In order to be entitled to benefits under this chapter, a claimant must fully cooperate with all law enforcement agencies and prosecuting attorneys in the apprehension and prosecution of the offender causing the criminally injurious conduct.
rule.source_title: Idaho Code 72-1016 (Limitations on awards)

rule.summary: Except for the sexual assault exam rules in 72-1019(2), compensation is reduced or denied to the extent it can be recovered from insurance or other collateral sources.
rule.quote: Subject to the limitations on payments for the costs of forensic and medical examinations of alleged victims of sexual assault described in section 72-1019 (2), Idaho Code, compensation otherwise payable to a claimant shall be reduced or denied to the extent the compensation benefits payable are or can be recouped from collateral sources.
rule.source_title: Idaho Code 72-1016 (Limitations on awards)

rule.summary: An award may be reduced or denied in proportion to how much the commission finds the victim contributed to the injury.
rule.quote: Compensation may be denied or reduced if the victim contributed to the infliction of death or injury with respect to which the claim is made.
rule.source_title: Idaho Code 72-1016 (Limitations on awards)

rule.summary: Compensation is cut by 50 percent if the claimant was committing a felony or certain impaired-driving or boating violations when injured.
rule.quote: Compensation otherwise payable to a claimant shall be reduced by fifty percent (50%) if at the time the injury was incurred the claimant was engaged in a felony or was in violation of section 18-8004 or 67-7034 , Idaho Code
rule.source_title: Idaho Code 72-1016 (Limitations on awards)

rule.summary: The commission may deny or reduce an award if the claimant or victim did not fully cooperate with law enforcement or prosecutors.
rule.quote: The commission, upon finding that the claimant or victim has not fully cooperated with appropriate law enforcement agencies or prosecuting attorneys, may deny or reconsider and reduce an award of compensation.
rule.source_title: Idaho Code 72-1016 (Limitations on awards)

rule.summary: If the claimant would face financial hardship and a final award looks likely, the commission may pay a tentative award, deducted from the final award later.
rule.quote: If the commission determines that the claimant will suffer financial hardship unless a tentative award is made and it appears likely that a final award will be made, an amount may be paid to the claimant, to be deducted from the final award
rule.source_title: Idaho Code 72-1017 (Tentative award of compensation)

rule.summary: Covered injury includes physical harm and, for a victim, pregnancy, sexually transmitted disease, mental or nervous shock, or extreme mental distress.
rule.quote: means actual bodily harm or disfigurement and, with respect to a victim, includes pregnancy, venereal disease, mental or nervous shock, or extreme mental distress
rule.source_title: Idaho Code 72-1003 (Definitions)

rule.summary: Crimes committed in Idaho qualify. An Idaho resident hurt in another state qualifies only if that state has no compensation program the victim is eligible for.
rule.quote: Occurs or is attempted in this state or occurs outside the state of Idaho against a resident of the state of Idaho and which occurred in a state which does not have a crime victims compensation program for which the victim is eligible
rule.source_title: Idaho Code 72-1003 (Definitions)

rule.summary: The information and records the Industrial Commission keeps for crime victim compensation claims are confidential and exempt from public disclosure, with limited exceptions (the claimant, a court in camera review, public officials doing their duties, and treating or advising health care providers).
rule.quote: The information and records the commission maintains in its possession in the administration of this chapter shall be kept confidential and are exempt from public disclosure under chapter 1, title 74 , Idaho Code
rule.source_title: Idaho Code 72-1007 (Public inspection and disclosure of commission records)

added.summary: The paper application can be mailed to the VCCB office in Anchorage.

added.summary: The paper application can be faxed to the VCCB.
added.quote: You may fill out and fax in the application. fax: (907) 465-2379
added.pinpoint: VCCB Application page, How to Apply, Fax
added.source_title: Alaska VCCB, Application and Forms page

added.summary: The application can be emailed to the VCCB; the application's contact block gives the email address and its instructions say it can be submitted by email.
added.quote: Email: VCCB@alaska.gov
added.pinpoint: Application (05/2026), contact block on page 1 and on the Claim Application and Instructions page
added.source_title: Alaska VCCB Application for Crime Victim Compensation (05/2026)

added.summary: An application can also be filed online through the VCCB's secure web portal, reached from the VCCB website.
added.quote: Please visit https://vccb.alaska.gov to access the secure web application portal to file an application online.
added.pinpoint: Claim Application and Instructions, Is there another way to apply?
added.source_title: Alaska VCCB Application for Crime Victim Compensation (05/2026)

added.summary: The signed Release of Information on the last page of the application must be included however the application is sent.
added.quote: Whether applying online, by email, fax or through a printed application, please ensure the Release of Information on the final page is signed and included.
added.pinpoint: VCCB Application page, How to Apply
added.source_title: Alaska VCCB, Application and Forms page

added.summary: Include a copy of the police report if you have it; you do not need to wait for it before applying.
added.quote: Please include any documentation you have available such as a copy of the police report, bills, receipts, or other crime-related information.
added.pinpoint: Claim Application and Instructions, Do I need to include any other documentation with the application?
added.source_title: Alaska VCCB Application for Crime Victim Compensation (05/2026)

added.summary: Submit invoices or statements for claimed services, or a page listing each provider and dates of service so the VCCB can request the records.
added.quote: Billing Records: Submit invoices, statements, or receipts for all medical, dental, counseling, or other claimed services.
added.pinpoint: Application (05/2026), Section 5: Crime-Related Expenses, Billing Records
added.source_title: Alaska VCCB Application for Crime Victim Compensation (05/2026)

added.summary: If you paid for services yourself, save and send the receipts as verification.
added.quote: please save your receipts to send in as verification.
added.pinpoint: VCCB Application page, Additional Forms
added.source_title: Alaska VCCB, Application and Forms page

added.summary: Copies of insurance information strengthen the application.
added.quote: To strengthen your application, include copies of any supporting documents, such as bills or insurance information.
added.pinpoint: VCCB Application page, How to Apply
added.source_title: Alaska VCCB, Application and Forms page

added.summary: By statute the applicant submits reports from the physicians who treated or examined the victim, if reasonably available.
added.quote: the applicant shall, before a hearing on an application under this chapter, submit reports, if reasonably available, from all physicians or surgeons who have treated or examined the victim in relation to the injury for which compensation is claimed
added.source_title: AS 18.67.010 to 18.67.180, Violent Crimes Compensation Board (Alaska Statutes, print view)

added.summary: For lost wages, the VCCB contacts the employer for wage and date information without sharing case details.
added.quote: Your employer will be contacted for wage and date information, however no details of your case will be shared
added.pinpoint: VCCB Application page, Additional Forms, Loss of Income
added.source_title: Alaska VCCB, Application and Forms page

added.summary: A treatment plan is required for counseling beyond the initial award.
added.quote: there are session rate limits and treatment plans are required for services beyond the initial award
added.pinpoint: VCCB Application page, Additional Forms, Counseling
added.source_title: Alaska VCCB, Application and Forms page

added.summary: Relocation requests need the Request for Relocation Assistance form completed before expenses are covered.
added.quote: This Request for Relocation Assistance must be completed prior to any expenses being covered.
added.pinpoint: VCCB Application page, Additional Forms, Relocation
added.source_title: Alaska VCCB, Application and Forms page

added.summary: Rental assistance requests need the Request for Rental Assistance form and documentation such as a lease copy.
added.quote: Request for Rental Assistance must be filled out along with documentation, such as a copy of your lease
added.pinpoint: VCCB Application page, Additional Forms, Rental Assistance
added.source_title: Alaska VCCB, Application and Forms page

added.summary: Alaska's new Address Confidentiality Program, run by the Department of Administration, gives an enrolled person a post office box to use as a substitute mailing address and forwards their mail, and state and municipal agencies must accept that address. A victim of a crime involving sexual assault, domestic violence, or stalking can enroll if a court has issued a protective order for them or they meet other standards the department sets. The department must still adopt regulations setting out how to enroll.
added.quote: (2) designate a post office box as a substitute mailing address for an 02 individual enrolled in the program; 03 (3) forward the mail of an individual enrolled in the program from the 04 post office box designated under (2) of this subsection to the individual's residential 05 street address, post office box, school address, or work address as specified on the 06 individual's application for enrollment in the program; 07 (4) maintain the confidentiality of the address of an individual enrolled 08 in the program; and 09 (5) adopt regulations establishing a procedure for a qualified individual 10 under (c) of this section to enroll in or withdraw from the program. 11 (c) The following individuals may enroll in the program: 12 (1) a victim of a crime involving domestic violence, stalking, or sexual 13 assault if 14 (A) a court has issued a protective order on behalf of the 15 victim; or 16 (B) the victim meets other standards set by the department;
added.pinpoint: AS 44.21.022(b)(2) to (c)(1), enacted by sec. 75 of Chapter 9 SLA 26 (HB 239), effective July 1, 2026 under sec. 94; agencies must accept the address under AS 44.21.022(e)
added.source_title: Enrolled HB 239 (Chapter 9 SLA 26), sec. 75 enacting AS 44.21.022, Address confidentiality program (Alaska Legislature bill text)

added.summary: By statute, a compensation application and personally identifying information about the applicant are confidential records that the Violent Crimes Compensation Board may not release.
added.quote: An application for compensation and personally identifying information relating to an applicant for compensation are confidential records and may not be released by the board.
added.source_title: AS 18.67.010 to 18.67.180, Violent Crimes Compensation Board (Alaska Statutes, print view)

rule.summary: Lost wage payments cover only leave without pay, not days already covered by paid leave.
rule.quote: Compensation is limited to leave without pay.
rule.pinpoint: VCCB Application, Section 7: Lost Wage Information
rule.source_title: Alaska VCCB Application for Crime Victim Compensation (05/2026)

rule.summary: Property loss or damage is generally not covered; essential items taken as evidence (and phones) are limited exceptions.
rule.quote: Note: VCCB does not generally cover property loss or damage, these are limited exceptions.
rule.pinpoint: VCCB Application and Forms, Property Replacement
rule.source_title: Alaska VCCB, Application and Forms page

added.title: Enrolled HB 239 (Chapter 9 SLA 26), sec. 75 enacting AS 44.21.022, Address confidentiality program (Alaska Legislature bill text)

added.summary: Mail the completed application to the Alabama Crime Victims Compensation Commission, P.O. Box 231267, Montgomery, Alabama 36123-1267.
added.quote: The completed application can be returned by: FAX: (334)290-4455 Email: info@acvcc.alabama.gov Mail: Alabama Crime Victims Compensation Commission P.O. Box 231267 Montgomery, Alabama 36123-1267
added.pinpoint: Compensation page, How Do I File A Claim?
added.source_title: ACVCC: Compensation

added.summary: Email the completed application to info@acvcc.alabama.gov.
added.quote: Please download the completed application and email it to info@acvcc.alabama.gov or fax it to 334-290-4455.
added.pinpoint: Application, Claim Authorization page, submission box
added.source_title: ACVCC application for compensation (MAR 2026)

added.summary: Fax the completed application to 334-290-4455.
added.quote: Please download the completed application and email it to info@acvcc.alabama.gov or fax it to 334-290-4455.
added.pinpoint: Application, Claim Authorization page, submission box
added.source_title: ACVCC application for compensation (MAR 2026)

added.summary: The application must be signed; a fax or electronic signature is accepted, but the Commission may ask for an original notarized signature.
added.quote: The claimant must submit an application that has been signed by either facsimile signature or electronic signature.
added.pinpoint: Ala. Admin. Code r. 262-X-4-.02(10)
added.source_title: Ala. Admin. Code r. 262-X-4-.02

added.summary: Include proof of U.S. citizenship or that you are an alien eligible for public benefits.
added.quote: You must submit proof of US citizenship or that you are an alien eligible for public benefits.
added.pinpoint: Application, Section 1 note
added.source_title: ACVCC application for compensation (MAR 2026)

added.summary: Include a copy of the police report if one is available.
added.quote: Complete this section and, if one is available, provide a copy of the Police Report.
added.pinpoint: Application, Section 5 (Crime Information)
added.source_title: ACVCC application for compensation (MAR 2026)

added.summary: For each type of compensation you request, include the related bills or receipts.
added.quote: Provide any corresponding and directly related bills/receipts.
added.pinpoint: Application, Section 6 (Compensation Request)
added.source_title: ACVCC application for compensation (MAR 2026)

added.summary: If you are asking for medical expenses, the victim or a representative must sign and date the health information authorization in the application.
added.quote: Either the patient (victim) or their representative must sign and date this authorization if consideration of medical expenses is being requested.
added.pinpoint: Application, Patient Authorization for Use and Disclosure of Protected Health Information
added.source_title: ACVCC application for compensation (MAR 2026)

added.summary: If you file more than one year after the incident, explain the good cause in writing.
added.quote: The claim must be filed within one (1) year of the incident, or good cause must be submitted in writing.
added.pinpoint: Application Form page, Additional Requirements
added.source_title: ACVCC: Application Form page

added.summary: If the crime was not reported to law enforcement within 72 hours, explain the good cause in writing.
added.quote: The crime must be reported to the proper law enforcement agency within 72 hours of the incident, or good cause must be submitted in writing.
added.pinpoint: Application Form page, Additional Requirements
added.source_title: ACVCC: Application Form page

added.summary: If someone other than the victim signs as claimant, include documentation that they are legally authorized to act for the victim.
added.quote: The claimant (if other than victim) must be the person legally authorized to act on the behalf of the victim. Documentation of this authority must be provided.
added.pinpoint: Application, Claim Authorization page, signature note
added.source_title: ACVCC application for compensation (MAR 2026)

added.summary: If the victim is 19 or older but incapacitated, include proof of guardianship or conservatorship.
added.quote: If the victim is 19 or older, but is incapacitated, you will have to provide proof of guardianship/conservatorship over the victim.
added.pinpoint: Application, Section 3 (Claimant Information)
added.source_title: ACVCC application for compensation (MAR 2026)

added.summary: For lost wages, include written documentation from your employer or a W-2.
added.quote: Lost wages shall be verified by obtaining written documentation from the employer or by submission of a W-2 tax document.
added.pinpoint: Ala. Admin. Code r. 262-X-4-.04(8)
added.source_title: Ala. Admin. Code r. 262-X-4-.04

added.summary: For lost wages, if you are self-employed, include a tax transcript from the IRS.
added.quote: A tax transcript from the IRS is required if the person seeking reimbursement of his/her lost wages is self-employed.
added.pinpoint: Ala. Admin. Code r. 262-X-4-.04(8)
added.source_title: Ala. Admin. Code r. 262-X-4-.04

added.summary: A sexual assault victim can claim up to two weeks of lost wages without a doctor's excuse; beyond two weeks, include a doctor's excuse.
added.quote: A victim of sexual assault may be granted compensation for maximum of two weeks of lost wages without a doctor's excuse. A doctor's excuse must be provided for lost wages in excess of two weeks to be considered for reimbursement.
added.pinpoint: Ala. Admin. Code r. 262-X-4-.04(28)
added.source_title: Ala. Admin. Code r. 262-X-4-.04

added.summary: For counseling, the Commission needs a letter from the clinician certifying that therapy is necessary because of the victimization.
added.quote: ACVCC must receive a letter from the clinician certifying that the victim is engaged in necessary therapy due to his/her victimization.
added.pinpoint: Ala. Admin. Code r. 262-X-4-.07(2)(a)
added.source_title: Ala. Admin. Code r. 262-X-4-.07

added.summary: For ongoing counseling, the clinician must send quarterly updates certifying the treatment is still necessary.
added.quote: Quarterly updates from the clinician certifying that the treatment is necessary and the result of victimization must be submitted in order for payment to be considered.
added.pinpoint: Ala. Admin. Code r. 262-X-4-.07(2)(b)
added.source_title: Ala. Admin. Code r. 262-X-4-.07

added.summary: For counseling, the clinician must provide an itemized bill for the treatment sessions.
added.quote: The clinician must provide an itemized bill for treatment sessions.
added.pinpoint: Ala. Admin. Code r. 262-X-4-.07(2)(c)
added.source_title: Ala. Admin. Code r. 262-X-4-.07

added.summary: For moving expenses, include written estimates or receipts.
added.quote: Written estimates and/or receipts are required for payment of moving expenses.
added.pinpoint: Ala. Admin. Code r. 262-X-4-.04(14)(a)
added.source_title: Ala. Admin. Code r. 262-X-4-.04

added.summary: For temporary relocation, include a copy of the hotel bill, credit card receipt, or another verifiable document.
added.quote: A copy of the hotel bill, credit card receipt, or other verifiable document is required for verification.
added.pinpoint: Ala. Admin. Code r. 262-X-4-.04(14)(b)
added.source_title: Ala. Admin. Code r. 262-X-4-.04

added.summary: The Commission may not disclose the names and addresses of victims or claimants who applied for compensation, or the facts of the crime against them.
added.quote: The commission may not disclose the names and addresses of victims or claimants who have applied for compensation pursuant to this article or the facts or circumstances of the criminally injurious conduct perpetrated against them.
added.pinpoint: Ala. Code 15-23-4(k)
added.source_title: Ala. Code 15-23-4 (Justia)

rule.summary: The Commission does not reimburse or replace property, so a lost or damaged phone or other personal item is not covered. The only items listed under this rule are security windows and locks and damaged prescription eyeglasses.
rule.quote: The Commission does not provide property reimbursement or replacement.
rule.source_title: Ala. Admin. Code r. 262-X-4-.04

added.title: Ala. Admin. Code r. 262-X-2-.05 (Records)
Ala. Code 15-23-4 (Justia)

added.summary: For lost wages, attach your most recent pay stub, or if self-employed, your tax returns from the last three years.
added.quote: Attach a copy of your most recent pay stub from your employer. If you are self-employed, you must furnish copies of your tax returns from the last three (3) years so lost wages can be most accurately determined.
added.pinpoint: Application, Section D, Request for Lost Wages
added.source_title: Arkansas CVRB, Application for Crime Victim Compensation (10-6-2023)

added.summary: For lost wages, give the name and address of the physician who can verify your time off, or attach a recent disability statement.
added.quote: You must also provide the complete name and address of the physician who can verify your disability period, or you may attach a copy of a recent disability statement.
added.pinpoint: Application, Section D, Request for Lost Wages
added.source_title: Arkansas CVRB, Application for Crime Victim Compensation (10-6-2023)

added.summary: For funeral or burial expenses, include a copy of the funeral bill and the death certificate.

added.source_title: Arkansas CVRB, Application for Crime Victim Compensation (10-6-2023)

added.summary: For loss of support after a victim's death, include the victim's last three years of tax returns, Social Security benefit verification, and proof of guardianship for a minor dependent.
added.quote: NOTE: You must attach copies of the deceased victim's last three (3) years' tax returns. You must also provide verification regarding the denial or receipt of any benefits from the Social Security Administration. You must be the legal guardian of a minor dependent to request loss of support on their behalf and must provide verification of guardianship.

added.summary: For crime scene cleanup, attach receipts or other supporting documentation.

added.source_title: Arkansas CVRB, Application for Crime Victim Compensation (10-6-2023)

added.summary: Arkansas's Address Confidentiality Program, run by the DFA Office of Driver Services, is free and puts a post office box on the driver's license or ID card instead of the home address. It is limited to domestic violence victims and their dependents, so most sexual assault survivors do not qualify unless the abuser was a family or household member or dating partner.
added.quote: The Address Confidentiality Program is a free program administered by the Office of Driver Services. Participants in tis program will be issued a driver’s license or identification card that displays a post office box in lieu of a residential address.
added.pinpoint: DFA Address Confidentiality Program page, Program Description
added.source_title: Arkansas DFA Office of Driver Services, Address Confidentiality Program page

added.summary: Medical treatment documents a claimant submits with a reparations application are confidential by statute, and so are law enforcement investigative reports if another law makes them confidential. The statute does not make the whole claim file or the applicant's identity confidential.
added.quote: When submitted to the Crime Victims Reparations Board as part of an application, the following information shall be confidential: (1) Documents submitted by a claimant which relate to medical treatment; and (2) Law enforcement investigative reports, if confidential under any other law.
added.source_title: Arkansas DPS, CVRB Statutes compilation PDF (current through 2023 Regular Session)

rule.summary: If the victim is a minor, the claim may be filed within 5 years after the victim turns 18.
rule.quote: If the victim is a minor, the claim is filed within five (5) years after the date the victim reaches eighteen (18) years of age

added.summary: The Secretary of State's Address Confidentiality Program gives survivors of sexual offenses, domestic violence, and stalking a substitute address and free mail forwarding so the person they fear cannot find them through public records. Eligible applicants include victims of a sexual offense such as rape or sexual assault. Enrollment is only through an in-person meeting with a registered Application Assistant at a victim services agency.
added.quote: The Arizona Address Confidentiality Program (ACP) is a program that helps victims of domestic violence, sexual offenses, and/or stalking from being located by the person they are seeking safety from through public records. The program provides a substitute address and confidential mail forwarding services to individuals and families across Arizona.

added.summary: Mail the claim form to VCAP at 900 N. King Street, 4th Floor, Wilmington, DE 19801.

added.source_title: VCAP brochure (English)

added.source_title: VCAP brochure (English)

added.summary: The claim must be filed in writing on VCAP's own claim form and signed by the claimant.

added.source_title: 11 Del. C. ch. 90, Compensation for Innocent Victims of Crime (sections 9001 to 9025)

added.summary: The official claim form includes subrogation, authorization, and consent agreements that must be part of the filing.
added.quote: claims must be filed in the office of VCAP on official forms which include subrogation, authorization, and consent agreements.

added.source_title: 1 Del. Admin. Code 301, Victims' Compensation Assistance Program Rules and Regulations

added.summary: Every loss must be backed by documentation before VCAP awards compensation.

added.source_title: Delaware DOJ, Victims' Compensation Assistance Program page and FAQs

added.summary: If VCAP asks for more documentation while investigating, it must be sent within 45 days of the request.
added.quote: If VCAP, in its investigation of a claim, requires further documentation from the claimant, such documentation must be submitted to VCAP no later than 45 days of the date of VCAP's request.
added.pinpoint: 1 Del. Admin. Code 301-11.2
added.source_title: 1 Del. Admin. Code 301, Victims' Compensation Assistance Program Rules and Regulations

added.summary: Survivors claiming temporary housing, rent, security deposit, furniture, or moving costs must send documentation within 45 days of VCAP's request.
added.quote: A victim who seeks compensation for temporary housing, rent, security deposit, furniture and/or moving expenses must submit documentation within 45 days of VCAP's request therefor, unless an extension is granted by the Agency.
added.pinpoint: 1 Del. Admin. Code 301-11.3
added.source_title: 1 Del. Admin. Code 301, Victims' Compensation Assistance Program Rules and Regulations

added.summary: If the injury happened on the job, the survivor must file a workers' compensation claim and send proof of it before applying to VCAP.
added.quote: If the victim seeks compensation for an injury sustained while in the course and scope of employment, the victim must submit a claim for worker's compensation, and provide documentation thereof, before making application to VCAP for compensation.
added.pinpoint: 1 Del. Admin. Code 301-11.4
added.source_title: 1 Del. Admin. Code 301, Victims' Compensation Assistance Program Rules and Regulations

added.summary: To ask for an emergency award, the claimant must request it in writing with the claim form and show just cause.

added.pinpoint: 1 Del. Admin. Code 301-23.0
added.source_title: 1 Del. Admin. Code 301, Victims' Compensation Assistance Program Rules and Regulations

added.summary: A decision on a claim can take up to 60 days, and longer in rare cases.

added.source_title: VCAP brochure (English)

added.summary: Delaware's Address Confidentiality Program, run by the Department of Justice, gives certified participants a substitute address and forwards their mail. Victims of sexual assault can apply if they have filed for a protection from abuse order or are named as a victim in a criminal or delinquency case, and they state that they fear future violence from the perpetrator.
added.quote: All of the following persons are eligible to apply to become program participants: (1) A victim of domestic violence, sexual assault, human trafficking, kidnapping, or stalking who has filed for a protection from abuse order or who is or was named as a victim in any criminal or delinquency proceeding
added.pinpoint: 11 Del. C. § 9613(1); substitute address under § 9612(a)
added.source_title: 11 Del. C. ch. 96, subch. II, Address Confidentiality Act (sections 9611 to 9619)

added.summary: Under Delaware's Freedom of Information Act, the investigative files the Victims' Compensation Assistance Program compiles or maintains are not public records.
added.quote: (14) Investigative files compiled or maintained by the Victims’ Compensation Assistance Program
added.pinpoint: 29 Del. C. § 10002(o)(14) (records not deemed public)
added.source_title: 29 Del. C. ch. 100, Freedom of Information Act

rule.summary: Pecuniary loss does not include property damage, so damaged personal property (for example a phone) is generally not paid. The cost to replace items seized as evidence is the exception.
rule.quote: “Pecuniary loss” means any expenses actually and necessarily incurred as a result of personal injury or death resulting from a crime, but does not include property damage.
rule.source_title: 11 Del. C. ch. 90, Compensation for Innocent Victims of Crime (sections 9001 to 9025)

Survivors of sexual assault qualify only when it was domestic or dating violence; there is no general sexual assault eligibility.

If you require information regarding the Address Confidentiality Program, please contact the switchboard at (850) 414-3300. Once you call, please request to be connected to the Address Confidentiality Program, and you will be transferred to the appropriate personnel who can assist you further.

added.summary: Any part of a public record held by an agency that regularly receives information about crime victims, such as the Bureau of Victim Compensation, that reveals a victim's name, phone, address, or assets, or anything that could be used to locate or harass the victim, is exempt from Florida's public records law.
added.quote: Any portion of a public record which reveals the identity, including the name or personal identification number, home or employment telephone number, home or employment address, or personal assets, of a victim, or any other information that could be used to locate, intimidate, harass, or abuse the victim, which identifies that person as the victim of a crime, and which is a public record that is generated or received by any agency that regularly generates or receives information from or concerning the victims of crime is exempt from s. 119.07 (1) and s. 24(a), Art. I of the State Constitution.
added.source_title: Fla. Stat. 119.071 (General exemptions from inspection or copying of public records)

rule.summary: A victim who was under 18 at the time of a crime on or after October 1, 2019 has 3 years after turning 18 to file; good cause can extend this and kit testing or DNA matching delays can waive it.

rule.summary: Compensation funds are not awarded to pay attorney's fees for a claimant who hires a lawyer for a Board hearing.

rule.summary: A victim who was a minor at the time of the crime has until three years after their eighteenth birthday to file.
