added.pinpoint: FAQ, What happens after my application is received?
added.source_title: Idaho CVCP: Frequently Asked Questions

added.summary: Idaho's Address Confidentiality Program, run by the Secretary of State, gives survivors of sexual assault and other listed crimes a substitute mailing address and mail forwarding so their new address stays confidential; state and local agencies must accept the substitute address.
added.quote: If you move to a new location to escape domestic violence, sexual assault, stalking, malicious harassment or human trafficking, the Address Confidentiality Program (ACP) helps keep your new address confidential using a mail-forwarding service and substitute address.
added.pinpoint: Address Confidentiality Program page, introduction; Idaho Code 19-5701 and 19-5703
added.source_title: Idaho Secretary of State, Address Confidentiality Program page

added.summary: The information and records the Industrial Commission keeps for crime victim compensation claims are confidential and exempt from public disclosure, with limited exceptions (the claimant, a court in camera review, public officials doing their duties, and treating or advising health care providers).
added.quote: The information and records the commission maintains in its possession in the administration of this chapter shall be kept confidential and are exempt from public disclosure under chapter 1, title 74 , Idaho Code
added.pinpoint: Idaho Code 72-1007
added.source_title: Idaho Code 72-1007 (Public inspection and disclosure of commission records)

rule.summary: By statute, the cost of a sexual assault forensic or medical exam is paid from the state crime victims compensation account rather than by the law enforcement agency.
rule.quote: the cost of forensic and/or medical examinations of alleged victims of sexual assault shall be paid for from the crime victims compensation account
rule.source_title: Idaho Code 19-5303 (Cost of medical exams)

rule.summary: The commission pays for evidence-gathering sexual assault exams after any federal or federally financed payer (such as Medicaid or Medicare); for victims under 18 it pays after any liable third party.
rule.quote: Payment for the costs of forensic and medical examinations of alleged victims of sexual assault performed for the purposes of gathering evidence for possible prosecution, after collections from any federal or federally financed third party who has liability, shall be made by the commission; provided however that payment for the costs of forensic and medical examinations of alleged victims under eighteen (18) years of age shall be made by the commission after collections from any third party who has liability.
rule.source_title: Idaho Code 72-1019 (Compensation benefits)

rule.summary: A medical provider that the program has paid may not try to collect more from the victim for the same services, except when the program cannot pay the full allowable amount.
rule.quote: Except as provided in subsection (3) herein, a medical provider who has received payment from the commission for medical services provided to a victim or claimant under this chapter may not attempt to collect any further payment from the victim or the claimant for those same services.
rule.source_title: Idaho Code 72-1026 (Payments to medical providers)

rule.summary: Compensation to a victim, and to the victim's dependents if the victim dies, for crimes by the same offender within a 6 month period may not exceed $25,000 in total. The statute's wording is built around death cases; the program applies $25,000 as its maximum for all claims.
rule.quote: Compensation payable to a victim and all of the victim's dependents in cases of the victim's death, because of injuries suffered due to an act or acts of criminally injurious conduct involving the same offender and occurring within a six (6) month period, may not exceed twenty-five thousand dollars ($25,000) in the aggregate.
rule.source_title: Idaho Code 72-1019 (Compensation benefits)

rule.summary: Mental health treatment for the victim is capped at $2,500 unless the commission finds extenuating circumstances, in which case it can go up to the overall maximum.
rule.quote: payments for mental health treatment received as a result of the victim's injury may not exceed two thousand five hundred dollars ($2,500) unless the industrial commission finds extenuating circumstances.
rule.source_title: Idaho Code 72-1019 (Compensation benefits)

rule.summary: Family members of a sexual assault victim can get mental health treatment reimbursed, up to $500 per person or $1,500 per family, if the victim was also awarded benefits.
rule.quote: Total payments made under paragraph (a) of this subsection may not exceed five hundred dollars ($500) for each person or one thousand five hundred dollars ($1,500) for a family.
rule.source_title: Idaho Code 72-1019 (Compensation benefits)

rule.summary: A victim with total wage loss gets 66 2/3 percent of their wages, up to $175 per week.
rule.quote: The weekly benefit amount is sixty-six and two-thirds percent (66 2/3%) of the wages received at the time of the criminally injurious conduct, subject to a maximum of one hundred seventy-five dollars ($175).
rule.source_title: Idaho Code 72-1019 (Compensation benefits)

rule.summary: A victim who was employable but not employed at the time of the injury may get up to $150 per week, at the commission's discretion.
rule.quote: who was employable but was not employed at the time of such injury, may in the discretion of the commission be awarded weekly compensation benefits in an amount determined by the commission not to exceed one hundred fifty dollars ($150) per week.
rule.source_title: Idaho Code 72-1019 (Compensation benefits)

rule.summary: Weekly benefits for a victim who was employable but not employed may not exceed $20,000 in total.
rule.quote: Compensation payable to a victim or a victim's dependents under this subsection may not exceed twenty thousand dollars ($20,000), and the limitations of subsection (5) of this section apply to compensation under this subsection.
rule.source_title: Idaho Code 72-1019 (Compensation benefits)

rule.summary: Reasonable funeral, burial or cremation costs, plus transporting the victim's body, are paid up to $5,000 after other collateral sources have paid.
rule.quote: Reasonable funeral and burial or cremation expenses of the victim, together with actual expenses of transportation of the victim's body, shall be paid in an amount not exceeding five thousand dollars ($5,000) if all other collateral sources have properly paid such expenses but have not covered all such expenses.
rule.source_title: Idaho Code 72-1019 (Compensation benefits)

rule.summary: The commission may pay reasonable doctor, hospital, and medicine costs for crime injuries.
rule.quote: The commission may order payment of reasonable expenses actually incurred by the claimant for reasonable services by a physician or surgeon, reasonable hospital services and medicines, mental health counseling and care, and such other treatment as may be approved by the commission for the injuries suffered due to criminally injurious conduct.
rule.source_title: Idaho Code 72-1019 (Compensation benefits)

rule.summary: Mental health counseling and care for crime injuries can be paid.
rule.quote: The commission may order payment of reasonable expenses actually incurred by the claimant for reasonable services by a physician or surgeon, reasonable hospital services and medicines, mental health counseling and care, and such other treatment as may be approved by the commission for the injuries suffered due to criminally injurious conduct.
rule.source_title: Idaho Code 72-1019 (Compensation benefits)

rule.summary: The claimant or a close family member can be reimbursed for necessary travel to get covered benefits, under the commission's rules.
rule.quote: A claimant or a spouse, parent, child or sibling of a claimant or victim may be reimbursed for his or her expenses for necessary travel incurred in connection with obtaining benefits covered pursuant to this chapter and in accordance with rules of the commission.
rule.source_title: Idaho Code 72-1019 (Compensation benefits)

rule.summary: Property damage is not paid, so replacing personal property such as a phone is not covered. Pain and suffering is not paid either.
rule.quote: Compensation benefits are not payable for pain and suffering or property damage.
rule.source_title: Idaho Code 72-1019 (Compensation benefits)

rule.summary: Pain and suffering is not compensated.
rule.quote: Compensation benefits are not payable for pain and suffering or property damage.
rule.source_title: Idaho Code 72-1019 (Compensation benefits)

rule.summary: The program will not pay counseling cancellation or missed-appointment fees, or sessions that included the offender.
rule.quote: CVCP will not reimburse for cancellation or missed appointment fees nor will they consider payments for sessions that included the offender.
rule.source_title: Idaho CVCP: Frequently Asked Questions

rule.summary: Mileage is not paid for the first 15 miles of a round trip, or for round trips of 15 miles or less; one round trip per day.
rule.quote: Reimbursement is limited to one (1) round trip per day. The claimant shall not be reimbursed for the first fifteen (15) miles of any round trip, nor for traveling any round trip of fifteen (15) miles or less.
rule.source_title: IDAPA 17.10.01, Administrative Rules Under the Crime Victims Compensation Act

rule.summary: The program's FAQ lists crime-scene cleanup among costs it does not cover and points victims to court-ordered restitution from the offender instead. The same FAQ sentence also lists wage loss, which the statute does cover, so this page is not fully reliable.
rule.quote: A victim may request the criminal court to order the offender to pay restitution for expenses that are not covered by the program, such as property damage, wage loss, expenses to attend criminal court, or costs for crime-scene cleanup.
rule.source_title: Idaho CVCP: Frequently Asked Questions

rule.summary: The claim must be filed within 1 year after the crime; the commission can extend this for good cause.
rule.quote: Compensation may not be awarded unless the claim is filed with the commission within one (1) year after the day the criminally injurious conduct occurred causing the injury or death upon which the claim is based. The time for filing a claim may be extended by the commission for good cause shown.
rule.source_title: Idaho Code 72-1016 (Limitations on awards)

rule.summary: The crime must be reported to law enforcement within 72 hours, unless the commission finds good cause for the delay.
rule.quote: Compensation may not be awarded unless the criminally injurious conduct resulting in injury or death was reported to a law enforcement officer within seventy-two (72) hours after its occurrence or the commission finds there was good cause for the failure to report within that time.
rule.source_title: Idaho Code 72-1016 (Limitations on awards)

rule.summary: To get benefits, the claimant must fully cooperate with law enforcement and prosecutors; the commission may deny or reduce an award if they do not.
rule.quote: In order to be entitled to benefits under this chapter, a claimant must fully cooperate with all law enforcement agencies and prosecuting attorneys in the apprehension and prosecution of the offender causing the criminally injurious conduct.
rule.source_title: Idaho Code 72-1016 (Limitations on awards)

rule.summary: Except for the sexual assault exam rules in 72-1019(2), compensation is reduced or denied to the extent it can be recovered from insurance or other collateral sources.
rule.quote: Subject to the limitations on payments for the costs of forensic and medical examinations of alleged victims of sexual assault described in section 72-1019 (2), Idaho Code, compensation otherwise payable to a claimant shall be reduced or denied to the extent the compensation benefits payable are or can be recouped from collateral sources.
rule.source_title: Idaho Code 72-1016 (Limitations on awards)

rule.summary: An award may be reduced or denied in proportion to how much the commission finds the victim contributed to the injury.
rule.quote: Compensation may be denied or reduced if the victim contributed to the infliction of death or injury with respect to which the claim is made.
rule.source_title: Idaho Code 72-1016 (Limitations on awards)

rule.summary: Compensation is cut by 50 percent if the claimant was committing a felony or certain impaired-driving or boating violations when injured.
rule.quote: Compensation otherwise payable to a claimant shall be reduced by fifty percent (50%) if at the time the injury was incurred the claimant was engaged in a felony or was in violation of section 18-8004 or 67-7034 , Idaho Code
rule.source_title: Idaho Code 72-1016 (Limitations on awards)

rule.summary: The commission may deny or reduce an award if the claimant or victim did not fully cooperate with law enforcement or prosecutors.
rule.quote: The commission, upon finding that the claimant or victim has not fully cooperated with appropriate law enforcement agencies or prosecuting attorneys, may deny or reconsider and reduce an award of compensation.
rule.source_title: Idaho Code 72-1016 (Limitations on awards)

rule.summary: If the claimant would face financial hardship and a final award looks likely, the commission may pay a tentative award, deducted from the final award later.
rule.quote: If the commission determines that the claimant will suffer financial hardship unless a tentative award is made and it appears likely that a final award will be made, an amount may be paid to the claimant, to be deducted from the final award
rule.source_title: Idaho Code 72-1017 (Tentative award of compensation)

rule.summary: Covered injury includes physical harm and, for a victim, pregnancy, sexually transmitted disease, mental or nervous shock, or extreme mental distress.

added.summary: Apply online through the Attorney General's web form. The AG calls online submission the preferred method.

added.pinpoint: FAQ by Sexual Assault Victims (Rev. 01/25), closing paragraph

added.summary: Fill out the fillable PDF application electronically and email it to the Attorney General's office.

added.pinpoint: AG Crime Victim Compensation page, Crime Victim Compensation Application section
added.source_title: Illinois Attorney General: Crime Victim Compensation

added.summary: Mail the completed paper application to the Attorney General's Crime Victim Compensation Bureau in Chicago.
added.quote:
Mail your completed application
to:
Office of the Illinois Attorney General
Crime Victim Compensation Bureau
115 South LaSalle Street
Chicago, IL 60603
added.pinpoint: Application (Rev. 12/2024), Application Instructions, page 1
added.source_title: Illinois Attorney General: Crime Victims Compensation Application (English, Rev. 12/2024)

added.summary: Send copies of supporting documents you have, such as the police report, with the application. If you do not have them yet, keep collecting them for when the office contacts you.
added.quote:
If available, please send copies of all the documents you have with the completed
application (e.g., police report, plenary order of protection, civil no-contact order, hospital, or
doctor bills).
added.pinpoint: Application (Rev. 12/2024), Application Instructions, Documents
added.source_title: Illinois Attorney General: Crime Victims Compensation Application (English, Rev. 12/2024)

added.summary: If you have a plenary order of protection or civil no-contact order, send a copy with the application.
added.quote:
If available, please send copies of all the documents you have with the completed
application (e.g., police report, plenary order of protection, civil no-contact order, hospital, or
doctor bills).
added.pinpoint: Application (Rev. 12/2024), Application Instructions, Documents
added.source_title: Illinois Attorney General: Crime Victims Compensation Application (English, Rev. 12/2024)

added.summary: For medical, dental, or counseling expenses, send copies of itemized bills, and submit those bills to insurance or other payment sources too.
added.quote:
Please submit copies of itemized bills. All bills must be submitted to other sources of recovery available to
the victim.
added.pinpoint: Application (Rev. 12/2024), Section 4, Medical Information & Benefits
added.source_title: Illinois Attorney General: Crime Victims Compensation Application (English, Rev. 12/2024)

added.summary: Keep receipts, bills, and other proof of payment for every expense you want reimbursed.
added.quote: Keep receipts, bills, and any other proof of payment for all items you are seeking to receive compensation for.
added.pinpoint: Compensation guide (Rev. 11/24), What proof of my expenses should I keep?
added.source_title: Illinois Attorney General: Crime Victims Compensation Program guide (Rev. 11/24)

added.summary: If you are the legal guardian of a minor or incapacitated adult victim, include documentation showing guardianship.
added.quote: If the answer is YES, please provide documentation to show guardianship.
added.pinpoint: Application (Rev. 12/2024), Section 1
added.source_title: Illinois Attorney General: Crime Victims Compensation Application (English, Rev. 12/2024)

added.summary: When eligibility depends on where you live, you may be asked for proof of residence such as a lease, utility bill, pay stub, tax form, or notarized statement.
added.quote:
A person may be required to provide verification or proof of residence including, but not limited to,
a lease agreement, utility bill, license registration, document showing the mailing address, pay stub, tax form, or notarized statement.
added.pinpoint: Compensation guide (Rev. 11/24), definition of Dwelling
added.source_title: Illinois Attorney General: Crime Victims Compensation Program guide (Rev. 11/24)

added.summary: If the crime involved a law enforcement officer's use of force and you filed a complaint, lawsuit, or got a settlement, provide documentation of it.
added.quote: If yes, please explain and provide documentation for all complaints, proceedings or settlements
added.pinpoint: Application (Rev. 12/2024), Section 2, Use of Force Claims
added.source_title: Illinois Attorney General: Crime Victims Compensation Application (English, Rev. 12/2024)

added.summary: The Attorney General's Address Confidentiality Program gives survivors of sexual assault, domestic violence, human trafficking, and stalking a substitute address to use with State and local government agencies instead of their home, school, or work address.
added.quote: The Address Confidentiality Program (ACP) provides a substitute address for victims of domestic violence, sexual assault, human trafficking, and stalking to use instead of their home, school, or work addresses when interacting with State and local government agencies.
added.pinpoint: Illinois AG ACP page, opening paragraph; statutory basis 750 ILCS 61/11 and 61/15
added.source_title: Illinois Attorney General: Illinois Address Confidentiality Program (ACP)

added.summary: Records the Attorney General's office gets to process a compensation application, including the application, documents, and photographs, are exempt from disclosure under the Freedom of Information Act.
added.quote: Any records obtained by the Attorney General's office to process the application, including but not limited to applications, documents, and photographs, shall be exempt from disclosure by the Attorney General's office under the Freedom of Information Act.
added.source_title: Crime Victims Compensation Act, 740 ILCS 45 (full act, ILGA)

rule.summary: The program's sexual assault FAQ says stolen, damaged, or lost property cannot be paid, except locks, doors, and windows.
rule.quote: Stolen, damaged or lost property (except locks, doors and windows)
rule.pinpoint: Crime Victims Compensation FAQ by Sexual Assault Victims, What types of expenses cannot be paid
rule.source_title: Illinois Attorney General: Crime Victims Compensation FAQ by Sexual Assault Victims (Rev. 01/25)

rule.summary: The program's sexual assault FAQ says counseling by an unlicensed person working under a licensed provider cannot be paid.
rule.quote: Services by an unlicensed person working with a licensed person cannot be paid.
rule.pinpoint: Crime Victims Compensation FAQ by Sexual Assault Victims, What types of expenses may the Crime Victims Compensation Program pay?
rule.source_title: Illinois Attorney General: Crime Victims Compensation FAQ by Sexual Assault Victims (Rev. 01/25)

rule.summary: A victim who was under 18 or under a legal disability can apply within 3 years after turning 18 or after the disability ends, and a posttraumatic stress disorder diagnosis counts as a legal disability.
rule.quote: he or she may present the application required by this subsection within 3 years after he or she attains the age of 18 years or the disability is removed, as the case may be. Legal disability includes a diagnosis of posttraumatic stress disorder.
rule.source_title: Crime Victims Compensation Act, 740 ILCS 45 (full act, ILGA)

added.summary: Indiana's Address Confidentiality Program, run by the Attorney General's Office, is free and lets survivors of sexual assault and other listed crimes keep a confidential address: first-class mail goes to a secure substitute address and is forwarded, and the substitute address is used for state and local government services.
added.quote: The ACP is a free program that allows victims of domestic violence, sexual assault stalking, human trafficking, harassment, intimidation, or invasion of privacy to maintain a confidential address through the Attorney General's Office.
added.pinpoint: Attorney General, Address Confidentiality Program page, opening paragraphs
added.source_title: Indiana Attorney General, Address Confidentiality Program

added.summary: Indiana law makes a compensation claimant's personal information and medical records confidential, along with records from the division's claim investigation that are not publicly available.
added.quote: The following are confidential: (1) A claimant's: (A) personal information (as defined in IC 9-14-6-6 ); and (B) medical records. (2) Records obtained during an investigation under section 26 of this chapter that are not publicly available.
added.source_title: IC 5-2-6.1-11.5 (confidentiality) via Justia, 2025 Indiana Code

rule.summary: The program lists moving, relocation, and daily living expenses as not reimbursable.
rule.quote: Moving, relocation or daily living expenses.
rule.source_title: ICJI Victim Compensation Division (program page)

rule.summary: The program lists rent, utilities, food, travel, and lodging as not reimbursable (ambulance services are covered as medical).
rule.quote: Rent, utilities, food, travel, or lodging.

rule.summary: Paid leave must be used first, and the program will not reimburse time covered by paid vacation, sick, or personal leave.
rule.quote: The division may not reimburse the claimant for the use of paid or otherwise compensated vacation leave, sick leave, personal leave, or other compensatory time.

added.pinpoint: 802 KAR 3:030 Section 8(2)(a)

added.source_title: CVCB Documents to include (claim checklist)

added.source_title: Crime Victim Compensation Form (revised July 2024)

added.summary: A survivor seeking the lump sum for a sexual assault claim filed more than ten years after the crime must send proof of the crime date, that the kit was collected and when, that it went untested for a long time, and anecdotal proof of damages.
added.quote: (1) For purposes of KRS 49.370(7), a claimant seeking an award under this provision shall submit: (a) Proof that the crime occurred more than ten (10) years prior to the date of filing of the claim; (b) Proof that the sexual assault kit was collected; (c) Proof of the collection date of the biological material; (d) Proof that the biological material went untested for an extended period; and (e) Anecdotal proof of the damages incurred as a result of the crime.
added.pinpoint: 802 KAR 3:010 Section 8(1)

added.source_title: CVCB Documents to include (claim checklist)

added.summary: For claims filed after July 1, 2026, the investigator must finish the investigative report within 90 days after the claim is assigned; this is the investigation step, not the Board's final decision.

added.pinpoint: 802 KAR 3:010 Section 6(3)
added.source_title: 802 KAR 3:010 Crime victims compensation

added.summary: Kentucky's Safe at Home Program, run by the Secretary of State, protects victims of sexual assault, rape, other sexual crimes, domestic violence, human trafficking, and stalking by letting them use a designated address instead of their real one. It also covers their minor children and anyone living with them, and it is free for Kentucky residents who are U.S. citizens.
added.quote: The Safe at Home Program shall be operated with the intent to protect victims of: (a) Domestic violence; (b) Human trafficking; (c) Stalking; (d) Sexual assault; (e) Rape; and (f) Other sexual crimes as defined by KRS 17.500. The Safe at Home Program shall authorize the use of designated addresses for victims, their minor children, and all other individuals residing with the victim.
added.source_title: KRS 14.302 (Safe at Home Program established, designated addresses)

added.summary: Under the Crime Victims Compensation Board's regulation, a claimant's or victim's personally identifiable information must stay secure and confidential, and information that could show whether someone filed a claim may not be disclosed to unauthorized people.
added.quote: A claimant or victim's personally identifiable information shall remain secure and confidential. (4) Information that may be used to determine whether an individual filed a claim with the Board shall not be disclosed to unauthorized individuals.
added.source_title: 802 KAR 3:010 Crime victims compensation

rule.summary: Counseling compensation may be denied for missed or cancelled appointments and for non-therapeutic court or investigative work by the provider.

added.summary: The application must be signed, and it includes release forms that let staff collect and verify information.
added.quote: The application must be signed and sent to the Victims' Compensation Board. Release forms are included with the application to allow staff to compile and verify information.

added.source_title: Maine AG: Victims' Compensation Program Law and History

added.summary: A claim must include documentation of every expense claimed, including medical reports and records.
added.quote: Claims must include documentation of all eligible expenses and losses for which the claimant seeks compensation, including but not limited to medical reports, records and bills, funeral bills and employment records when lost wages are sought.
added.source_title: 5 M.R.S. 3360-D (Claims)

added.summary: A claim must include the bills for the expenses claimed, such as medical bills.
added.quote: Claims must include documentation of all eligible expenses and losses for which the claimant seeks compensation, including but not limited to medical reports, records and bills, funeral bills and employment records when lost wages are sought.
added.source_title: 5 M.R.S. 3360-D (Claims)

added.summary: A survivor claiming lost wages must include employment records.
added.quote: Claims must include documentation of all eligible expenses and losses for which the claimant seeks compensation, including but not limited to medical reports, records and bills, funeral bills and employment records when lost wages are sought.
added.source_title: 5 M.R.S. 3360-D (Claims)

added.summary: A claim must include records about insurance, workers' compensation, and state or federal assistance programs.
added.quote: Claims must include records related to insurance, workers' compensation, federal and state entitlement and assistance programs.
added.source_title: 5 M.R.S. 3360-D (Claims)

added.summary: The claim must give the date and circumstances of the crime and name the law enforcement agency it was reported to.
added.quote: Claims must specify the date, the nature and circumstances of the crime and the law enforcement agency to which the crime was reported.
added.source_title: 5 M.R.S. 3360-D (Claims)

added.summary: For counseling costs, the counselor must send a completed treatment plan; the case cannot go to the Board without it.
added.quote: Your case cannot go before the Board without the completed treatment plan.
added.pinpoint: AG Mental Health Counseling Guidelines
added.source_title: Maine AG: Mental Health Counseling Guidelines

added.summary: The Secretary of State runs an Address Confidentiality Program that gives victims of sexual assault, domestic violence, stalking or human trafficking a designated substitute address, which state and local agencies and courts must use instead of the real one. A survivor applies with the help of a registered application assistant, usually at a victim services program.
added.quote: The Address Confidentiality Program is established to protect victims of domestic violence, sexual assault, stalking or human trafficking; minor victims of kidnapping; and reproductive or gender-affirming health care services practitioners by authorizing the use of designated addresses for such victims and practitioners.
added.source_title: 5 M.R.S. 90-B (Address Confidentiality Program)

added.summary: Everything the Attorney General's office holds about a compensation application or award is confidential and stays confidential with the Board. The Attorney General may still share it, at its discretion, with law enforcement, courts and Corrections for restitution, a claimant in a hearing or appeal, or others to carry out the program.
added.quote: All records and information obtained by or in the possession of the Department of the Attorney General concerning an application for or an award of compensation under this chapter are confidential and may not be disclosed.
added.source_title: 5 M.R.S. 3360-D (Claims)

rule.summary: Property losses are not covered, except replacement of eyeglasses, dentures and other prosthetic devices and some crime scene cleanup costs.
rule.quote: No property losses are covered other than replacement costs of eyeglasses, dentures and other prosthetic devices and some costs of crime scene cleanup.
rule.pinpoint: Maine AG Program Law and History, What Is an Eligible Expense?
rule.source_title: Maine AG: Victims' Compensation Program Law and History

added.summary: Michigan's Address Confidentiality Program, run by the Department of Attorney General, gives victims of sexual assault, domestic violence, stalking, and human trafficking a designated substitute address to use instead of their real one on public records, plus free mail forwarding. added.quote: The Program (ACP) was created to conceal the addresses of victims of stalking, domestic violence, sexual assault, human trafficking, and of individuals at risk of being threatened or physically harmed from being located by their perpetrators through public records. ACP provides victims with a designated (substitute) address that can be used instead of their real address.

added.summary: A claimant's file and testimony before the Crime Victim Services Commission are exempt from disclosure under Michigan's Freedom of Information Act, and records the commission obtains that other laws keep confidential stay confidential.

added.summary: The Missouri Secretary of State runs an Address Confidentiality Program that gives victims of rape, sexual assault, and other listed crimes who fear for their safety a designated substitute address in place of their real address. added.quote: There is created in the office of the secretary of state a program to be known as the "Address Confidentiality Program" to protect victims of domestic violence, rape, sexual assault, human trafficking, stalking, or other crimes who fear for their safety, as well as the safety of individuals residing in the same household as the victim, by authorizing the use of designated addresses for such victims, their minor children, and individuals residing with them.

added.summary: CVC claim information and hearings are open to the public by default in Missouri. A claim for rape, sodomy, or sexual abuse is closed and confidential only when DPS decides that is in the best interest of the victim or dependents; claims involving a minor, or where the assailant has not been tried and disclosure would hurt the case, are also closed, and DPS may close any record in the interest of justice.
added.quote: A claim in which the offense allegedly perpetrated against the victim is rape, sodomy or sexual abuse and it is determined by the department to be in the best interest of the victim or of the victim's dependents that the information be kept confidential or that the public be excluded from the hearing;

added.source_title: Mississippi Attorney General: Bureau of Victim Assistance (Victim Compensation and Sexual Assault Examinations)

added.summary: Fill out the paper application, attach itemized bills and other required documents, and mail it to the Crime Victim Compensation Division's post office box in Jackson.
added.quote: Fill out the form completely (please print), attach any required documentation, including itemized bills, and mail to the above address.
added.pinpoint: Application (rev. 12.9.2025), Instructions
added.source_title: Crime Victim Compensation Application (rev. 12.9.2025)

added.summary: The printed application can also be faxed to the program using the fax number on the form.
added.quote: print the form found online and mail or fax it using the information on the form.
added.pinpoint: Victim Compensation brochure (2025), How to Apply
added.source_title: Mississippi Crime Victim Compensation brochure (2025)

added.summary: The application has to be filled out completely and signed.
added.quote: Application must be completed and signed.
added.pinpoint: Application (rev. 12.9.2025), page 1
added.source_title: Crime Victim Compensation Application (rev. 12.9.2025)

added.summary: Attach itemized bills and any other documentation for the expenses being claimed.

added.pinpoint: Application (rev. 12.9.2025), Instructions
added.source_title: Crime Victim Compensation Application (rev. 12.9.2025)

added.summary: For medical expenses, provide an itemized statement listing each service's date, type, diagnostic and treatment codes, and charge.
added.quote: The victim/claimant shall provide an itemized statement indicating date of service, type of service, diagnostic code, treatment code and charge for each service, product or treatment.
added.pinpoint: 3 Miss. Admin. Code Pt. 1, R. 301(2)(a)
added.source_title: Miss. Admin. Code Title 3, Part 1: Division of Victim Compensation rules

added.summary: Over-the-counter medical supplies need an itemized receipt that shows the item.

added.source_title: Miss. Admin. Code Title 3, Part 1: Division of Victim Compensation rules

added.summary: The insurance and other benefits section must be filled in, because the program pays only after every other source.
added.quote: By law, the Crime Victim Compensation Division is payer of last resort and must verify all sources available for payment of expenses. This section must be completed.
added.pinpoint: Application (rev. 12.9.2025), Section F
added.source_title: Crime Victim Compensation Application (rev. 12.9.2025)

added.summary: If claiming lost wages, provide a report of earnings and information on other benefit sources.
added.quote: The victim and/or claimant shall provide report of earnings and collateral source information.
added.pinpoint: 3 Miss. Admin. Code Pt. 1, R. 303(4)(a)
added.source_title: Miss. Admin. Code Title 3, Part 1: Division of Victim Compensation rules

added.summary: A self-employed applicant claiming lost wages attaches a copy of their latest federal income tax return.
added.quote: If you are self-employed, attach a copy of your latest federal income tax return.
added.pinpoint: Application (rev. 12.9.2025), Section D
added.source_title: Crime Victim Compensation Application (rev. 12.9.2025)

added.summary: If work was missed for more than a week, include a disability statement from the victim's doctor giving how long the disability lasted.

added.source_title: Miss. Admin. Code Title 3, Part 1: Division of Victim Compensation rules

added.summary: For counseling costs, the counselor fills out the program's Mental Health Services and Expenses Report form.
added.quote: The mental health provider shall provide a completed Mental Health Services and Expenses Report form
added.pinpoint: 3 Miss. Admin. Code Pt. 1, R. 302(3)(b)
added.source_title: Miss. Admin. Code Title 3, Part 1: Division of Victim Compensation rules

added.summary: For medical or counseling travel, submit the program's travel reimbursement request form.
added.quote: The victim/claimant shall submit a travel reimbursement request form as prescribed by the Division.
added.pinpoint: 3 Miss. Admin. Code Pt. 1, R. 301(7)(h)
added.source_title: Miss. Admin. Code Title 3, Part 1: Division of Victim Compensation rules

added.summary: The program says an eligibility decision is usually made within 90 days of receiving the application.
added.quote: A decision about whether the victim or claimant is eligible is usually made within 90 days.
added.pinpoint: Victim Compensation FAQ, What Happens After I Mail in my Application?
added.source_title: Mississippi Attorney General: Victim Compensation Frequently Asked Questions

added.summary: The Attorney General's Address Confidentiality Program gives Mississippi residents who are victims of domestic violence, sexual assault, or stalking a substitute address and mail forwarding to use with state and local agencies, so the person they fear cannot find them. Applicants send the program application to the Attorney General's Victim Compensation Division; the assault does not have to have happened in Mississippi.
added.quote: The Address Confidentiality Program helps victims keep their location confidential by providing them with a substitute address and a mail forwarding service for use when interacting with state and local agencies.
added.pinpoint: Miss. Admin. Code Title 3, Part 1, Chapter 07, Rules 700 and 703; statutory basis Miss. Code Ann. 99-47-1
added.source_title: Miss. Admin. Code Title 3, Part 1: Division of Victim Compensation rules

added.summary: By statute, the compensation division's records, files and communications are confidential and privileged and cannot be released under the Mississippi Public Records Act of 1983, and no one may disclose information about applicants or recipients without the claimant's written consent except to run the program.
added.quote: The records, papers, files and communications of the division, director, staff and agents must be regarded as confidential information and privileged and not subject to disclosure under any condition including the Mississippi Public Records Act of 1983.
added.pinpoint: Miss. Code Ann. 99-41-31
added.source_title: Miss. Code Ann. 99-41-31 (2025): Disclosure of records as to claims; confidentiality of records

rule.summary: Damaged or stolen property is not reimbursed. Medical items such as eyeglasses, hearing aids, dentures or prosthetics destroyed in the crime are handled separately as a medical expense.
rule.quote: Ineligible expenses include, but are not limited to, damaged or stolen property, pain and suffering, expenses not directly related to the crime injuries, attorney’s fees
rule.source_title: Miss. Admin. Code Title 3, Part 1: Division of Victim Compensation rules

rule.summary: Attorney's fees are not reimbursed.
rule.quote: Ineligible expenses include, but are not limited to, damaged or stolen property, pain and suffering, expenses not directly related to the crime injuries, attorney’s fees
rule.source_title: Miss. Admin. Code Title 3, Part 1: Division of Victim Compensation rules

added.title: Miss. Code Ann. 99-41-31 (2025): Disclosure of records as to claims; confidentiality of records

added.pinpoint: CVC FAQ, Should I send in copies of medical bills along with the application?
added.source_title: Montana DOJ: CVC Frequently Asked Questions

added.summary: If insurance processed the bills, include a copy of the explanation of benefits.
added.quote: If applicable, submit a copy of your insurance explanation of benefits.
added.pinpoint: CVC FAQ, Should I send in copies of medical bills along with the application?
added.source_title: Montana DOJ: CVC Frequently Asked Questions

added.summary: Wage loss claims need extra paperwork and verification.
added.quote: Additional paperwork and verification are required to approve wage loss.
added.pinpoint: Eligible Benefits, Wage Loss
added.source_title: Montana DOJ Office of Victim Services: Crime Victim Compensation

added.summary: The claimant must sign and date the claim form or it will not be considered.
added.quote: Claimant must sign and date here before the claim will be considered for benefits.
added.pinpoint: Claim Form, Section G signature block
added.source_title: Montana Crime Victim Compensation Claim Form (12-25)

added.summary: The program aims to decide eligibility within 60 days; it can take longer if requested information is slow to arrive.
added.quote: The goal of the CVC program is to determine eligibility on a claim within 60 days.
added.pinpoint: CVC FAQ, How long will it take to receive a decision on compensation benefits?
added.source_title: Montana DOJ: CVC Frequently Asked Questions

added.summary: Montana's Address Confidentiality Program, run by the DOJ Office of Victim Services, gives Montana residents who are victims of sexual assault, partner or family member assault, stalking, or human trafficking a substitute address and free confidential first-class mail forwarding. Survivors apply online or by mailing, emailing, or faxing the application with supporting documents, and a crime victim advocate can help.
added.quote: Be a victim of partner or family member assault, sexual assault, stalking, human trafficking, or eligible to apply for an order of protection.
added.pinpoint: Address Confidentiality Program page, eligibility list
added.source_title: Montana DOJ Office of Victim Services: Address Confidentiality Program

added.summary: The compensation office's records are generally open to public inspection, but personal, medical, or similar information is exempt from disclosure when releasing it would be an unreasonable invasion of privacy, and confidential criminal justice information stays protected under the Montana Criminal Justice Information Act.
added.quote: the following public records of the office are exempt from disclosure: (a)	information of a personal nature, such as personal, medical, or similar information, if the public disclosure of the information would constitute an unreasonable invasion of privacy
added.source_title: MCA 53-9-107: Public inspection and disclosure of office's records

rule.summary: The program does not pay for stolen, damaged, or destroyed property (for example a phone). It may still pay for items such as eyeglasses, hearing aids, crutches, braces, and prosthetic devices.
rule.quote: No, the CVC program cannot pay for stolen, damaged, or destroyed property.  CVC may pay for items such as eyeglasses, hearing aids, crutches, braces, and prosthetic devices.
rule.source_title: Montana DOJ: CVC Frequently Asked Questions

rule.summary: Lost wages are paid only for physical injury; missed work due to mental impairment is not covered.
rule.quote: CVC does not cover missed work due to mental impairment.
rule.pinpoint: Montana DOJ, Crime Victim Compensation page, Wage Loss
rule.source_title: Montana DOJ Office of Victim Services: Crime Victim Compensation

rule.summary: For sexual offenses against minors, the deadline is 1 year after the report to police or child welfare, or 1 year after the victim turns 18, whichever is later.
rule.quote: Compensation in cases involving sexual offenses against minors may not be awarded unless the claim is filed with the office within 1 year after the day the criminally injurious conduct was reported to a law enforcement agency or an agency of the state responsible for provision of child welfare services, or within 1 year after the day the victim reaches 18 years of age, whichever occurs last.
rule.source_title: MCA 53-9-125, Limitations on awards

MCA 53-9-107: Public inspection and disclosure of office's records

added.summary: A paper application can be mailed to the Office of Victim Compensation Services, 4232 Mail Service Center, Raleigh, NC 27699-4232.
added.quote: If you prefer to apply by mail, you may download and print a paper form . Mail your application to: Office of Victim Compensation Services 4232 Mail Service Center Raleigh, NC 27699-4232
added.pinpoint: NC DPS Victim Compensation Program page, How to Apply
added.source_title: NC DPS Victim Compensation Program page and FAQ

added.summary: Survivors can start an application online through ncdps.gov/4victims, which leads to the program's online portal.
added.quote: To learn more about the program and start an application, visit ncdps.gov/4victims.
added.pinpoint: NC DPS Rape Victim Assistance Program FAQ, 'Is financial help available for medical expenses beyond the cost of the forensic exam?'
added.source_title: NC DPS Rape Victim Assistance Program page and FAQ

added.summary: The application must be completed, signed, and dated.
added.quote: Complete, sign, and date the application.
added.pinpoint: NC DPS Victim Compensation Program FAQ, 'How can applicants avoid delays?'
added.source_title: NC DPS Victim Compensation Program page and FAQ

added.summary: Include a copy of the law enforcement report or warrant that names the victim.
added.quote: Include a copy of the law enforcement report or warrant that lists the victim’s name.
added.pinpoint: NC DPS Victim Compensation Program FAQ, 'How can applicants avoid delays?'
added.source_title: NC DPS Victim Compensation Program page and FAQ

added.summary: Medical and counseling expenses need itemized bills from the providers.
added.quote: Submit itemized bills from certified providers of medical or counseling services.
added.pinpoint: NC DPS Victim Compensation Program FAQ, 'What paperwork do I need to submit with my application?' (Medical and counseling services)
added.source_title: NC DPS Victim Compensation Program page and FAQ

added.summary: Include proof of any payments already made toward the itemized bills, by the victim, third parties, or insurance.
added.quote: Provide proof of payment made towards any of the itemized bills by the victim, third parties, or insurance companies.
added.pinpoint: NC DPS Victim Compensation Program FAQ, 'How can applicants avoid delays?'
added.source_title: NC DPS Victim Compensation Program page and FAQ

added.summary: For lost wages, an employed survivor sends a physician's letter on letterhead, an employer letter confirming the absence, and the last paystub before the crime.
added.quote: If you have an employer, you should submit a signed physician’s letter on the provider’s letterhead that details the dates and reasons you were advised to be out of work, an official employer letter on company letterhead that confirms your approved absence and your last paystub before the incident.
added.pinpoint: NC DPS Victim Compensation Program FAQ, 'What paperwork do I need to submit with my application?' (Lost wages)
added.source_title: NC DPS Victim Compensation Program page and FAQ

added.summary: For lost wages, a self-employed survivor sends a physician's letter on letterhead and a signed federal tax return from the year before the crime.
added.quote: If you are self-employed or are an independent contractor, you’ll need a signed physician’s letter on the provider’s letterhead and a copy of your signed federal tax return from the year before the crime.
added.pinpoint: NC DPS Victim Compensation Program FAQ, 'What paperwork do I need to submit with my application?' (Lost wages)
added.source_title: NC DPS Victim Compensation Program page and FAQ

added.summary: For dental care, a survivor may send a proposed treatment plan on the dentist's letterhead.
added.quote: You may submit a proposed treatment plan on your dentist’s letterhead.
added.pinpoint: NC DPS Victim Compensation Program FAQ, 'What paperwork do I need to submit with my application?' (Dental services)
added.source_title: NC DPS Victim Compensation Program page and FAQ

added.summary: Funeral claims need a copy of the death certificate, the itemized funeral bill, and the law enforcement report.
added.quote: Submit a copy of the death certificate, itemized funeral bill and the law enforcement report.
added.pinpoint: NC DPS Victim Compensation Program FAQ, 'What paperwork do I need to submit with my application?' (Funeral expenses)
added.source_title: NC DPS Victim Compensation Program page and FAQ

added.summary: The program says the average processing time is three to six months from when it receives the application.
added.quote: From the time an application is received, the average processing time is between three to six months.
added.pinpoint: NC DPS Victim Compensation Program FAQ, 'What happens after I submit my application?'
added.source_title: NC DPS Victim Compensation Program page and FAQ

added.summary: North Carolina's Address Confidentiality Program, run by the Attorney General, gives relocated victims of domestic violence, sexual offense, or stalking a substitute address so assailants cannot find them through public records.
added.quote: A program in the Office of the Attorney General to protect the confidentiality of the address of a relocated victim of domestic violence, sexual offense, or stalking to prevent the victim's assailants or potential assailants from finding the victim through public records.
added.pinpoint: N.C. Gen. Stat. 15C-2(2)
added.source_title: N.C. Gen. Stat. 15C-2 (Address Confidentiality Program definitions)

added.summary: To enroll, the survivor files an application with the Attorney General with help from a designated application assistant (an advocate at a victim services agency or nonprofit).
added.quote: An individual who wants to participate in the Address Confidentiality Program shall file an application with the Attorney General with the assistance of an application assistant.
added.pinpoint: N.C. Gen. Stat. 15C-4(a)
added.source_title: N.C. Gen. Stat. 15C-4 (Filing and certification of applications; authorization card)

added.summary: Victims' and claimants' personal information and all information about how claims were decided (except the total amount awarded) are held confidential by the Commission and Director; medical and law enforcement records are also confidential.
added.quote: All personal information, as that term is defined in 18 U.S.C. § 2725(3), of victims and claimants and all information concerning the disposition of claims for compensation, except for the total amount awarded a victim or claimant, shall be held confidential by the Commission and Director.
added.pinpoint: N.C. Gen. Stat. 15B-8.1(b)
added.source_title: N.C. Gen. Stat. 15B-8.1 (Privilege and records of the Commission)

rule.summary: Travel is listed as not accepted.
rule.quote: X Travel
rule.pinpoint: NC DPS Victim Compensation Program page, Not Accepted
rule.source_title: NC DPS Victim Compensation Program page and FAQ

rule.summary: Court fees and expenses are not accepted.
rule.quote: X Court fees and expenses
rule.pinpoint: NC DPS Victim Compensation Program page, Not Accepted
rule.source_title: NC DPS Victim Compensation Program page and FAQ

N.C. Gen. Stat. 15B-8.1 (Privilege and records of the Commission)
N.C. Gen. Stat. 15C-2 (Address Confidentiality Program definitions)

added.summary: Apply online through the ND DOCR Crime Victim's Compensation Application portal linked from the program page.
added.quote: Clicking the link below will take you to the online application for Crime Victim
added.pinpoint: Program page, Crime Victims Compensation Application and Forms
added.source_title: ND DOCR Crime Victims Compensation program page

added.summary: Allow 2 to 4 weeks for the program to process an application or a reimbursement request.
added.quote: Please allow 2-4 weeks for processing CVC application or claim reimbursement requests.
added.pinpoint: Program page, Claim Status
added.source_title: ND DOCR Crime Victims Compensation program page

added.summary: Submit a completed application on the program's form, signed by the claimant or a parent, guardian, or legal representative; an employer, provider, or insurer cannot apply for you.
added.quote: A claimant for benefits shall submit a completed application for compensation signed by the claimant or the claimant's parent, guardian, or legal representative on an application form prescribed by the division.
added.source_title: N.D. Admin. Code ch. 94-03-03 (application for compensation)

added.summary: If the crime was not reported to law enforcement in time, explain the reason for the late report in the application.
added.quote: There may be a justifiable reason for the late report. Please explain.
added.pinpoint: CVC Application Tips, Section 3 (Incident Information, continued)
added.source_title: ND DOCR CVC Application Tips (PDF)

added.summary: For medical costs, include a billing statement showing the provider's name, business address, phone number, and treatment plan.
added.quote: A request for compensation for medical services must include a billing statement containing the medical provider's name, business address, telephone number, treatment plan, and other information necessary for the division to determine the claim is for services directly related to the criminally injurious conduct.
added.source_title: N.D. Admin. Code ch. 94-03-03 (application for compensation)

added.summary: For dental costs, include a billing statement showing the dentist's name, business address, phone number, and treatment plan.
added.quote: A request for compensation for dental services must include a billing statement containing the dental provider's name, business address, telephone number, treatment plan, and other information necessary for the division to determine the claim is for services directly related to the criminally injurious conduct.
added.source_title: N.D. Admin. Code ch. 94-03-03 (application for compensation)

added.summary: For counseling, the provider's billing statement must list itemized transactions with the provider's name, business address, and phone number.
added.quote: A billing statement of itemized transactions containing the provider's name, business address, and telephone number.
added.pinpoint: CVC Mental Health Treatment Policy and Provider Verification Form (Rev. 6/2025), Verification Requirements
added.source_title: ND CVC Mental Health Treatment Policy and Provider Verification Form (Rev. 6/2025)

added.summary: For counseling, the provider returns the CVC Provider Verification Form with the billing invoice.
added.quote: The Provider Verification Form portion is to be returned with the billing invoice for reimbursement of services to the CVC program.
added.pinpoint: CVC Mental Health Treatment Policy and Provider Verification Form (Rev. 6/2025), introduction
added.source_title: ND CVC Mental Health Treatment Policy and Provider Verification Form (Rev. 6/2025)

added.summary: For lost wages, include written documentation from a medical or mental health provider and from your employer.
added.quote: A claim for reimbursement for work loss must include written documentation from a medical or mental health provider, the claimant's employer, and information the division may request that supports payment for work loss.
added.source_title: N.D. Admin. Code ch. 94-03-03 (application for compensation)

added.summary: For lost wages, the employer you worked for at the time of the crime completes the CVC Employer's Report.
added.quote: FORM MUST BE COMPLETED BY EMPLOYER YOU WERE WORKING FOR AT THE TIME OF THE CRIME INCIDENT.
added.pinpoint: Work Loss - Employer's Report, SFN 12437
added.source_title: ND CVC Work Loss - Employer's Report (SFN 12437, Rev. 06-2018)

added.summary: For lost wages, if you are self-employed, include a copy of your federal income tax return for the prior year.
added.quote: Self-employed victims shall provide a copy of federal income tax return for one year prior and other substantial verification of work loss or profits the division determines is necessary to support payment for work loss.
added.source_title: N.D. Admin. Code ch. 94-03-03 (application for compensation)

added.summary: For lost wages, a medical provider who treated your crime injuries completes the CVC Physician's Report.
added.quote: FORM MUST BE COMPLETED BY A MEDICAL PROVIDER WHO TREATED YOU FOR YOUR CRIME INJURIES.
added.pinpoint: Work Loss - Physician's Report, SFN 60497
added.source_title: ND CVC Work Loss - Physician's Report (SFN 60497, Rev. 06-2018)

added.summary: For travel and lodging, include your receipts.
added.quote: The claimant shall submit receipts for travel and lodging expenses to the division.
added.source_title: N.D. Admin. Code ch. 94-03-03 (application for compensation)

added.summary: For funeral and burial costs, include itemized receipts.
added.quote: The claimant shall submit itemized receipts for reimbursement under this section.
added.source_title: N.D. Admin. Code ch. 94-03-03 (application for compensation)

added.summary: For replacement services, include receipts showing the billed amount and the type of service.
added.quote: A claim for reimbursement for replacement services loss must include receipts for the billed amount, type of service provided, and other information necessary for the division to determine the claim is for services directly related to the criminally injurious conduct.
added.source_title: N.D. Admin. Code ch. 94-03-03 (application for compensation)

added.summary: For loss of support, include proof of the support the victim gave dependents before the crime, such as tax forms, a certified death certificate, or birth certificates.
added.quote: A claim for loss of support must include verification of the amount of support the victim provided to dependents prior to the criminally injurious conduct.
added.source_title: N.D. Admin. Code ch. 94-03-03 (application for compensation)

added.summary: Before the program pays, you or the provider must show what insurance or another collateral source paid, or that it did not cover the service.
added.quote: Before payment is made from the division, either the provider or the claimant shall provide documentation that: a. Verifies the amount paid by the collateral source; or b. Verifies the applicant or service was not covered by the collateral source.
added.pinpoint: N.D. Admin. Code 94-03-03-06 (collateral sources)
added.source_title: N.D. Admin. Code ch. 94-03-03 (application for compensation)

added.summary: The program may ask you to sign its Authorization to Disclose Protected Health Information form so it can get records it needs to decide the claim.
added.quote: The DOCR may, however, require that you authorize disclosure of your health information if needed to make a determination about your claim.
added.pinpoint: Authorization to Disclose Protected Health Information, SFN 61353, Privacy Statement
added.source_title: ND CVC Authorization to Disclose Protected Health Information (SFN 61353)

added.summary: Division records about an application for or award of crime victims compensation are confidential and not open to public disclosure; law enforcement may inspect them for official duties, and a claimant's representative may see the file only with the claimant's signed authorization.
added.quote: All other records of the division concerning the application for or award of compensation under this chapter are confidential and are not open to public disclosure.
added.source_title: N.D.C.C. ch. 54-23.4 (Crime Victims Compensation)

rule.summary: Claims for property loss or damage are not covered.
rule.quote: Claims for property loss or damage.
rule.source_title: N.D. Admin. Code ch. 94-03-03 (application for compensation)

ND CVC Work Loss - Physician's Report (SFN 60497, Rev. 06-2018)

added.summary: Mail the completed, signed application and documentation to the Nebraska Crime Victim's Reparations Program, PO Box 94946, Lincoln, NE 68509-4946.
added.quote: Return the completed/signed application and documentation to the below address: Nebraska Crime Victim’s Reparations Program PO Box 94946 Lincoln, NE 68509-4946
added.pinpoint: CVR Claim Application (Oct 2023), cover page
added.source_title: CVR Claim Application (October 2023)

added.summary: Email the claim application and the supporting documentation requested to ncc.cvr@nebraska.gov.
added.quote: Submit, along with supporting documentation requested, by email or mailing to: CVR Claim → ncc.cvr@nebraska.gov
added.pinpoint: Crime Victim Reparations program page, Apply
added.source_title: Nebraska Crime Commission: Crime Victim Reparations program page

added.summary: The application's return-to block also lists the program's fax number, 402.471.2837.
added.pinpoint: CVR Claim Application (Oct 2023), cover page
added.source_title: CVR Claim Application (October 2023)

added.summary: Include itemized copies of all medical bills related to the incident.
added.quote: Submit itemized copies of all medical bills relating to the incident.
added.pinpoint: FAQ, What must I do to apply for compensation?
added.source_title: CVR Frequently Asked Questions (updated 4-5-2023)

added.summary: Attach copies of crime-related bills and any receipts for bills you already paid.
added.quote: Attach copies of crime related bills and any paid receipts.
added.pinpoint: CVR Claim Application (Oct 2023), Section 4: Expenses
added.source_title: CVR Claim Application (October 2023)

added.summary: Sign and date the Authorization to Release Information; no action is taken on the claim until it is signed.
added.quote: This authorization is an integral part of your application and must be signed and dated by the victim or claimant before any action will be taken on your claim.
added.pinpoint: CVR Claim Application (Oct 2023), Authorization to Release Information
added.source_title: CVR Claim Application (October 2023)

added.summary: Complete the citizenship attestation; if you attest as a qualified alien, you agree to provide a copy of your USCIS documentation.
added.quote: I am a qualified alien under the federal Immigration and Nationality Act and I agree to provide a copy of my USCIS documentation.
added.pinpoint: CVR Claim Application (Oct 2023), United States Citizenship Attestation
added.source_title: CVR Claim Application (October 2023)

added.summary: For lost wages, include pay stubs or an earning statement for the pay periods of work missed because of the incident.
added.quote: Copy of pay stubs or an earning statement for the pay period(s) for missed work as a result of the incident.
added.pinpoint: CVR Claim Application (Oct 2023), Section 6: Loss of Wage Information
added.source_title: CVR Claim Application (October 2023)

added.summary: For lost wages when self-employed, include your most recent federal tax returns with Schedule C and copies of estimates, bids, or contracts.
added.quote: If Self-Employed: submit the most recent federal tax returns including the schedule C form, Copies of Estimates, Bids, and/or Contracts.
added.pinpoint: CVR Claim Application (Oct 2023), Section 6: Loss of Wage Information
added.source_title: CVR Claim Application (October 2023)

added.summary: For lost wages, include a doctor's release back to work.
added.quote: A Doctor’s release back to work.
added.pinpoint: CVR Claim Application (Oct 2023), Section 6: Loss of Wage Information
added.source_title: CVR Claim Application (October 2023)

added.summary: For funeral or burial expenses, a copy of the death certificate is needed.
added.quote: Funeral or Burial Expenses (A copy of the death certificate will need to be provided.)
added.pinpoint: CVR Claim Application (Oct 2023), Section 4: Expenses
added.source_title: CVR Claim Application (October 2023)

added.summary: By statute, a hearing officer rules on an application within 180 days after receiving all required information; the clock does not start until the file is complete.
added.quote: A hearing officer shall consider and rule upon any application made under the Nebraska Crime Victim's Reparations Act within one hundred eighty days after receipt of all required information related to the crime.
added.pinpoint: Claims Process, quoting Neb. Rev. Stat. 81-1809(1)
added.source_title: CVR Claims Process

added.summary: The program says claims are typically fully processed within 6 to 9 months.
added.quote: CVR program applications take time, typically claims are fully processed within 6-9 months.
added.pinpoint: CVR pamphlet (English), back panel
added.source_title: Nebraska Crime Victim's Reparations Program pamphlet (English)

added.summary: Nebraska's Address Confidentiality Program, run by the Secretary of State, gives eligible victims of abuse, sexual assault or stalking a substitute address for state and local agencies and forwards their mail; you apply in person at a designated victim assistance center, not at the Secretary of State's office.
added.quote: To be eligible for ACP, an individual must be (1) a victim of abuse, sexual assault or stalking who fears for his or her safety
added.pinpoint: Program eligibility
added.source_title: Nebraska Secretary of State: Address Confidentiality Program page

added.summary: By statute, the name of a sexual assault victim in the reparations committee's records when applying for compensation may not be made public. The statute protects the name; it does not say the whole claim file is confidential.
added.quote: The name of any victim of a sexual assault appearing in information or records of the Crime Victim's Reparations Committee when the victim is applying for compensation under the Nebraska Crime Victim's Reparations Act shall not be made public.
added.pinpoint: Neb. Rev. Stat. 81-1842
added.source_title: Neb. Rev. Stat. 81-1842 (sexual assault victim; records; confidential)

rule.summary: Lost or damaged property is not covered.
rule.quote: The program does not cover property crime, property loss, property damage or pain and suffering.
rule.pinpoint: NCC Crime Victim Reparations page, Limitations
rule.source_title: Nebraska Crime Commission: Crime Victim Reparations program page

added.summary: Mail the completed paper application to the Victims' Compensation Program at the Department of Justice in Concord. This is the return address printed on the application form.
added.quote: Please return completed application to: New Hampshire Victims' Compensation Program Department of Justice 33 Capitol Street Concord, N.H. 03301-6397
added.pinpoint: Application, page 7 (return address)
added.source_title: New Hampshire Victims' Compensation Program Application Form (rev. 02/11/2021)

added.summary: The program page lists a newer office address in Concord (Granite Place South). The form still prints the Capitol Street address, so a survivor may want to call the program to confirm which address to use.
added.quote: How To Contact Our Office New Hampshire Victims' Compensation Program Department of Justice 1 Granite Place South Concord, NH 03301
added.pinpoint: Program page, How To Contact Our Office
added.source_title: New Hampshire DOJ, Victims' Compensation Program page and FAQ

added.summary: For medical, dental, or counseling costs, list every provider and enclose copies of their bills if you have them.
added.quote: If applicable, list all providers that provided treatment, including hospital, doctors, dentists, mental health counselors, ambulance, radiology and prescriptions (drugs and eyeglasses). Attach additional sheets if necessary. If available, please enclose copies of bills.
added.pinpoint: Application, Section 6 (Medical/Counseling Information)
added.source_title: New Hampshire Victims' Compensation Program Application Form (rev. 02/11/2021)

added.summary: After the application arrives, the program may ask for photocopies of all crime-related counseling bills.
added.quote: Photocopies of all crime-related mental health counseling bills
added.source_title: N.H. Admin. Rules, Chapter Jus 600, Victims' Compensation

added.summary: To claim medical or hospital costs, sign a HIPAA-compliant medical release so the program can get itemized statements and records from your providers.
added.quote: If a claimant seeks compensation for medical expenses, the victim or victim's parent or guardian shall complete and submit a HIPAA- compliant hospital and/or medical release.
added.source_title: N.H. Admin. Rules, Chapter Jus 600, Victims' Compensation

added.summary: To claim lost wages, fill in the employment section and send copies of your pay stubs.
added.quote: If yes, complete the following section, and submit copies of your pay stubs.
added.pinpoint: Application, Section 8 (Employment Information)
added.source_title: New Hampshire Victims' Compensation Program Application Form (rev. 02/11/2021)

added.summary: If you were self-employed, send a copy of your tax return for the year before the crime instead of pay stubs.
added.quote: If you were self-employed at the time of the crime, please submit a copy of your tax return documentation for the year before the crime.
added.pinpoint: Application, Section 8 (Employment Information)
added.source_title: New Hampshire Victims' Compensation Program Application Form (rev. 02/11/2021)

added.summary: If you missed more than two weeks of work, include a doctor's statement saying how long you were unable to work.
added.quote: If you have missed more than two weeks of work, please provide a doctor's statement verifying length of time you were unable to work.
added.pinpoint: Application, Section 8 (Employment Information)
added.source_title: New Hampshire Victims' Compensation Program Application Form (rev. 02/11/2021)

added.summary: For lost wages, keep and send copies of written confirmations of crime-related appointments such as medical, counseling, and police meetings.
added.quote: Copies of all written confirmations of appointments with medical providers, mental health providers, police and other law-enforcement officials, and any other appointments necessitated as a direct result of the crime.
added.source_title: N.H. Admin. Rules, Chapter Jus 600, Victims' Compensation

added.summary: If the crime involved a motor vehicle, include your auto insurance policy declarations page.
added.quote: Did the crime involve motor vehicles? (If yes, please provide your automobile insurance policy declarations page.)
added.pinpoint: Application, Section 9 (Restitution and Civil Action)
added.source_title: New Hampshire Victims' Compensation Program Application Form (rev. 02/11/2021)

added.summary: If insurance, leave, benefits, restitution, or any other resource might cover part of the costs, explain it on a separate sheet and attach it.
added.quote: please explain in full on a separate piece of paper and attach it to this application.
added.pinpoint: Application, Section 12 (Statement of Facts and Authorization)
added.source_title: New Hampshire Victims' Compensation Program Application Form (rev. 02/11/2021)

added.summary: If you applied for Medicaid, Medicare, hospital free care, or public assistance and were turned down, attach copies of the denial documents.
added.quote: attach copies of the documents that show your ineligibility for public assistance.
added.pinpoint: Application, Section 12 (Statement of Facts and Authorization)
added.source_title: New Hampshire Victims' Compensation Program Application Form (rev. 02/11/2021)

added.summary: After the program receives the application, staff will contact the applicant by mail or email within 2 weeks. This is first contact, not a decision.

added.summary: Once an application is complete, the rules say no more than 60 days should pass before the commission can decide. The program page warns the whole process may take several months or longer while police reports are gathered.
added.quote: In no case shall placement on the agenda result in the passage of more than 60 days after the claimant submitted a completed application before a decision can be made by the commission.
added.source_title: N.H. Admin. Rules, Chapter Jus 600, Victims' Compensation

added.summary: New Hampshire's Address Confidentiality Program, run by the Attorney General, gives survivors of sexual assault, domestic violence, or stalking a substitute address to use on state and local records, with first class mail forwarded to their real address. Survivors apply through a crisis center advocate, and no police report or restraining order is needed.
added.quote: Any adult person, a parent or guardian acting on behalf of a minor or guardian acting on behalf of an incapacitated person, may apply to the program if they are a victim of domestic violence, sexual assault or stalking and meet the eligibility guidelines.
added.pinpoint: DOJ ACP page, FAQ: What are the eligibility guidelines?
added.source_title: New Hampshire DOJ, Address Confidentiality Program page and FAQ

added.summary: Everything the compensation program receives or keeps about a claim is confidential and may not be released to anyone unless the claimant authorizes it or another law allows it.
added.quote: All information received, obtained, or maintained by the program in connection with any claim for victims' compensation shall be maintained as confidential material, and shall not be released or disclosed to any person or entity whatsoever, except as authorized by the claimant or as otherwise provided by law.
added.source_title: N.H. Admin. Rules, Chapter Jus 600, Victims' Compensation

added.pinpoint: Compensation Application page, How do I apply?
added.source_title: CVRC Compensation Application and FAQ page

added.summary: The commission reviews the application with a complete offense report or a provider incident verification form, which its office requests.

added.source_title: 10.40.2 NMAC (Crime Victims Reparation Commission, Compensation)

added.summary: Include the bills for the crime-related goods and services claimed.

added.pinpoint: AG Apply for Victims Compensation, Two options for filing a claim
added.source_title: Ohio Attorney General, Apply for Victims Compensation page

added.summary: If claiming lost wages, include copies of the 6 paychecks from before the crime.
added.quote: Complete if filing for loss of earnings. Provide copies of 6 paychecks prior to crime.
added.pinpoint: Application, Section 7: Employment Information
added.source_title: Ohio Attorney General, Application for Crime Victim Compensation (with program overview)

added.summary: Send a front and back copy of each insurance or benefit plan card listed on the application.
added.quote: Please send front and back copy of card
added.pinpoint: Application, Section 6: Insurance and Benefit Information
added.source_title: Ohio Attorney General, Application for Crime Victim Compensation (with program overview)

added.summary: The release in the application must be signed and dated, or the application will not be processed.
added.quote: This release must be signed and dated for the application to be processed.
added.pinpoint: Application, Section 12: Subrogation, Authorization, and Signature
added.source_title: Ohio Attorney General, Application for Crime Victim Compensation (with program overview)

added.summary: For funeral expense claims, include a copy of the death certificate if you have one.
added.quote: If you have a copy of the death certificate, please include a copy with your application.
added.pinpoint: Application, Section 8: Funeral Expenses
added.source_title: Ohio Attorney General, Application for Crime Victim Compensation (with program overview)

added.summary: The Attorney General must issue a written decision within 120 days after receiving the application, but may extend that limit with written reasons.
added.quote: The attorney general shall make a written finding of fact and decision in accordance with sections 2743.51 to 2743.72 of the Revised Code within one hundred twenty days after receiving the claim application.
added.source_title: ORC 2743.59 (investigating claim; decision deadline)

added.summary: Ohio's Safe at Home program, run by the Secretary of State, gives survivors of rape, sexual battery, domestic violence, stalking, or human trafficking a substitute address to use on government records instead of their real one. You apply with a certified Application Assistant at a survivor services organization.
added.quote: The applicant fears for the safety of the applicant, a member of the applicant's household, or the minor, incompetent, or ward on whose behalf the application is made because the applicant, household member, minor, incompetent, or ward is a victim of domestic violence, menacing by stalking, human trafficking, trafficking in persons, rape, or sexual battery.
added.source_title: ORC 111.42 (address confidentiality program; application to secretary of state)

added.summary: Records the Attorney General or Court of Claims gets for a compensation claim (such as medical or counseling records) that were confidential or exempt from public records law in the hands of whoever created them stay confidential once the program has them. This does not make the whole claim file confidential, and the records can still be used in hearings and written decisions on the claim.
added.quote: any record or report that the court of claims or the  attorney general has obtained prior to, or obtains on or after,  June 30, 1998, under the provisions of sections 2743.51 to 2743.72 of the Revised Code and that is confidential or otherwise exempt  from public disclosure under section 149.43 of the Revised Code  while in the possession of the creator of the record or report  shall remain confidential or exempt from public disclosure under  section 149.43 of the Revised Code while in the possession of the  court of claims or the attorney general.
added.source_title: ORC 2743.62 (privilege; confidentiality of records obtained for reparations claims)
