added.summary: Apply online through the OCVC online application portal.
added.quote: Use our online application to apply for compensation benefits.
added.pinpoint: VCP Online Access home page, How to Apply
added.source_title: OCVC VCP Online Access claim portal

added.summary: Mail the printed and signed claim form to the Crime Victims Compensation Board at 421 N.W. 13th Street, Suite 290, Oklahoma City.
added.quote: Please Return to: 421 N.W. 13TH STREET, SUITE 290 • OKLAHOMA CITY, OKLAHOMA 73103
added.pinpoint: Official Claim Form (Revised June 2019), page 1 header
added.source_title: OCVC Official Claim Form (2019)

added.summary: Fax the printed and signed claim form to 405/264-5097.
added.pinpoint: Official Claim Form (Revised June 2019), page 1 header
added.source_title: OCVC Official Claim Form (2019)

added.summary: The claim form says it can be emailed once printed and signed; the program email is victimsservices@dac.state.ok.us.
added.quote: Website: www.okvictimscomp.com E-mail: victimsservices@dac.state.ok.us
added.pinpoint: Official Claim Form (Revised June 2019), instructions header
added.source_title: OCVC Official Claim Form (2019)

added.summary: Fill out every section of the paper form and sign all three signature areas on page four.
added.quote: Please thoroughly complete ALL sections and sign all three areas of page four.
added.pinpoint: Official Claim Form (Revised June 2019), Instructions
added.source_title: OCVC Official Claim Form (2019)

added.summary: List the injuries from the crime and attach all itemized medical statements.
added.quote: List the injuries suffered as a result of the crime and attach all itemized medical statements.
added.pinpoint: Official Claim Form (Revised June 2019), Instructions, Section I
added.source_title: OCVC Official Claim Form (2019)

added.summary: Send all the bills you have received with the application; bills that arrive later can be added.
added.quote: Please submit all the bills that you have received. If more come in, they can always be added later.
added.pinpoint: FAQ, Do I need to submit all bills with the application?
added.source_title: OCVC Frequently Asked Questions

added.summary: Out-of-pocket medical, dental, and counseling costs are reimbursed at 100% only with documentation of payment.
added.quote: Medical, dental, and counseling expenses that the victim is out-of-pocket will be reimbursed at 100%, provided there is documentation of payment and no collateral sources exist.
added.pinpoint: Application Process, Payments
added.source_title: DAC Victims Compensation Program page (application process)

added.summary: The DA's Victim-Witness Coordinator requests the police report while documenting the claim.
added.quote: A police report is requested, along with any other forms and reports that may be needed to determine out-of-pocket expenses.
added.pinpoint: Application Process, Documentation
added.source_title: DAC Victims Compensation Program page (application process)

added.summary: Lost income must be verified by both your employer and your attending physician.
added.quote: Work loss must be verified by the employer and the attending physician.
added.pinpoint: Official Claim Form (Revised June 2019), Types of Expenses Covered, Income Loss / Economic Loss
added.source_title: OCVC Official Claim Form (2019)

added.summary: For lost wages, a physician or mental health professional and your employer must verify the disability time.
added.quote: provided the crime prevented the person from working and the disability can be verified by a physician or mental health professional and by the victim’s employer.
added.pinpoint: Official Claim Form (Revised June 2019), Instructions, Section G
added.source_title: OCVC Official Claim Form (2019)

added.summary: If you are self-employed, tax returns for the last 3 years are required for lost wages.
added.quote: IF SELF-EMPLOYED, TAX RETURNS FOR THE LAST THREE YEARS WILL BE REQUIRED.
added.pinpoint: Official Claim Form (Revised June 2019), Section G heading
added.source_title: OCVC Official Claim Form (2019)

added.summary: For mileage to medical or counseling appointments, include documentation from the provider verifying the dates of service.
added.quote: Documentation from the provider verifying the dates of services is required.
added.pinpoint: Official Claim Form (Revised June 2019), Types of Expenses Covered, Travel
added.source_title: OCVC Official Claim Form (2019)

added.summary: To ask for future costs, include an itemized list of the expenses you expect and an explanation.
added.quote: To submit a request for future economic loss, include an itemized list of the expenses you expect to incur, along with an explanation regarding the expense.
added.pinpoint: Official Claim Form (Revised June 2019), Types of Expenses Covered, Future Economic Loss
added.source_title: OCVC Official Claim Form (2019)

added.summary: For future dental work or surgery, ask the attending physician for a written estimate of the work and the cost.
added.quote: For future dental work or surgery necessary to repair damage from the criminal incident, ask the attending physician to write an accurate estimate which clearly states the work to be performed and the cost.
added.pinpoint: Official Claim Form (Revised June 2019), Types of Expenses Covered, Future Economic Loss
added.source_title: OCVC Official Claim Form (2019)

added.summary: For traditional American Indian healing or burial services, receipts must note each item's purpose.
added.quote: In order for reimbursement of these expenses, receipts must be provided with the item’s purpose clearly noted on the receipt.
added.pinpoint: Eligible Expenses, Traditional American Indian Services
added.source_title: OCVC Fund Eligibility page

added.summary: If you paid the forensic exam bill yourself, the program needs your Social Security number to reimburse you.
added.quote: If the victim/guardian paid the bill out of their own pocket, we will need a Social Security number in order to reimburse them.
added.pinpoint: Sexual Assault Examination Fund page
added.source_title: DAC Sexual Assault Examination Fund page

added.summary: Processing can take anywhere from 4 to 12 months depending on where the crime occurred.
added.quote: Depending on the area in which the crime occurred, the processing time could vary anywhere from 4-12 months
added.pinpoint: FAQ, How Long is the Process?
added.source_title: OCVC Frequently Asked Questions

added.summary: Once the Victim-Witness Coordinator sends all documentation, claims are generally docketed for decision within 30 days.
added.quote: Claims are generally placed on a docket for decision within 30 days of receipt of all documentation from the Victim-Witness Coordinator.
added.pinpoint: Application Process
added.source_title: DAC Victims Compensation Program page (application process)

added.summary: Payments are generally made within 3 weeks of approval.
added.quote: PAYMENTS are generally made within three weeks of approval.
added.pinpoint: Application Process, Payments
added.source_title: DAC Victims Compensation Program page (application process)

added.summary: Sexual Assault Examination Fund payments are usually made within 30 days of receiving the application.
added.quote: Payment is usually made within 30 days of the receipt of the application by the Compensation Program.
added.pinpoint: Sexual Assault Examination Fund page
added.source_title: DAC Sexual Assault Examination Fund page

added.summary: Oklahoma's Address Confidentiality Program, run by the Office of the Attorney General, gives victims of domestic violence, sexual assault, stalking, human trafficking, and child abduction who have moved somewhere unknown to their abuser a substitute address to use with state and local agencies, plus free mail forwarding. Applicants apply in person through a designated victim assistance program with an ACP-trained application assistant.
added.quote: The ACP aids in protecting the physical address of victims of domestic violence, sexual assault, stalking, human trafficking, and child abduction from disclosure. ACP contributes to the safety of victims by denying abusers the opportunity to use public records to violate the rights of others. Victims who have moved to a new location unknown to their abuser are provided with a substitute address when interacting with state and local agencies.
added.pinpoint: OAG ACP page, program description
added.source_title: Oklahoma Attorney General Address Confidentiality Program (ACP) page

added.summary: All records and information given to the Crime Victims Compensation Board to process a claim are confidential and generally cannot be obtained through discovery in a civil or criminal case, with narrow exceptions for an appeal of a Board decision or a strict showing to a court.
added.quote: All records and information given to the Board to process a claim on behalf of a crime victim shall be confidential.
added.source_title: 21 O.S. 142.9 Limits of compensation, provider payment, debt collection

added.title: OCVC Frequently Asked Questions
DAC Victims Compensation Program page (application process)
OCVC VCP Online Access claim portal
Oklahoma Attorney General Address Confidentiality Program (ACP) page

added.summary: Apply online through the CVC Portal, which also lets you upload documents and check claim status.
added.quote:
You can apply electronically through the Crime Victims’ Compensation Portal at
doj.state.or.us/cvcportal.
added.pinpoint: CVC Application (2026), page i, How do I apply?
added.source_title: Oregon Crime Victims' Compensation Application (English, 2026)

added.summary: Email the completed, signed application to the program.
added.quote: You can also submit your application by email: cvssd@doj.oregon.gov
added.pinpoint: CVC Application (2026), page i, How do I apply?
added.source_title: Oregon Crime Victims' Compensation Application (English, 2026)

added.summary: Mail the signed paper application to the DOJ Crime Victims' Compensation Program in Salem.
added.quote:
You can mail a paper application to:
Oregon Department of Justice
Crime Victims’ Compensation Program
1162 Court Street NE
Salem, OR 97301–4096
added.pinpoint: CVC Application (2026), page i, How do I apply?
added.source_title: Oregon Crime Victims' Compensation Application (English, 2026)

added.summary: You can also apply in person through a county District Attorney's victim assistance program or a community-based victim services agency.
added.quote: Apply at your local District Attorney’s Office Victim Assistance Program or local community-based victim services agency.
added.pinpoint: CVC brochure (2024), How Do I Submit an Application?
added.source_title: Oregon DOJ: Crime Victims' Compensation brochure (2024)

added.summary: Sign the release in the application so CVC can verify your information; unsigned applications are returned.
added.quote: You must sign this form to allow CVC to verify the information in your application. We will return any unsigned applications.
added.pinpoint: CVC Application (2026), page 4, Required Release to Process Your Application
added.source_title: Oregon Crime Victims' Compensation Application (English, 2026)

added.summary: For lost earnings, provide employer documentation of employment and time lost and your last paystub before the crime.
added.quote: The following information must be provided to CVC: Documentation from your employer to verify employment and time loss. Your paystub just prior to the crime.
added.pinpoint: CVC FAQ, loss of earnings benefit
added.source_title: Oregon DOJ: Crime Victims' Compensation FAQ

added.summary: If you are self-employed and claim lost earnings, submit the previous year's tax records.
added.quote: If you are self-employed, please submit the previous year tax records.
added.pinpoint: CVC FAQ, loss of earnings benefit
added.source_title: Oregon DOJ: Crime Victims' Compensation FAQ

added.summary: If you missed more than 2 weeks of work, a work release from your doctor is required.
added.quote: A work release from a doctor is required beyond 2 weeks of missed work.
added.pinpoint: CVC Application (2026), page i, Answers to Commonly Asked Questions
added.source_title: Oregon Crime Victims' Compensation Application (English, 2026)

added.summary: Payment requests must be itemized billing statements listing the services, the provider's name, and the date of service.
added.quote: Requests for payment of crime related expenses shall be submitted in the form of an itemized billing statement detailing the services provided, the provider’s name, the date of service
added.source_title: OAR Chapter 137 Division 76 (Crime Victims' Compensation)

added.summary: Insurance EOBs, chart notes, and bills can be combined into one upload in the CVC Portal.
added.quote: EOB’s, chart notes, and bills can all be combined to one document and select bill as the category.
added.pinpoint: Applying for CVC, Crime Victims Portal FAQs, How do I upload documents?
added.source_title: Oregon DOJ: Applying for Crime Victims' Compensation

added.summary: If CVC pays for a car rental or bus, train, or air fare instead of mileage, it needs a valid receipt.
added.quote: the Department may, at its discretion, reimburse reasonable and necessary round-trip car rental or bus, train, or air fare, upon submission of a valid receipt.
added.source_title: OAR Chapter 137 Division 76 (Crime Victims' Compensation)

added.summary: CVC confirms receipt by mail or email and issues a claim number within 2 business days.
added.quote:
We will notify you by mail or email when we receive your application. You will receive a
claim number within 2 business days.
added.pinpoint: CVC Application (2026), page i, What happens next?
added.source_title: Oregon Crime Victims' Compensation Application (English, 2026)

added.summary: CVC says it will contact you in 60 to 90 days to tell you whether the application was accepted.
added.quote:
We will contact you again in 60 to 90 days to tell you if we have accepted your
application.
added.pinpoint: CVC Application (2026), page i, What happens next?
added.source_title: Oregon Crime Victims' Compensation Application (English, 2026)

added.summary: Oregon DOJ's Address Confidentiality Program is a free mail forwarding service that gives survivors of sexual assault, domestic violence, stalking, human trafficking, and bias crimes a substitute address to use instead of their real one.
added.quote: It helps survivors of domestic violence, sexual assault, stalking, human trafficking, bias crimes or bias incidents shield their physical address. Health care providers who provide physical and behavioral reproductive and gender-affirming health care also can participate in ACP. Program participants are provided with a substitute address to use instead of their real address.
added.pinpoint: Oregon DOJ ACP page, 'Protecting Addresses for Victims'; program established by ORS 192.822
added.source_title: Oregon DOJ: Address Confidentiality Program (ACP)

added.summary: Information an applicant gives the DOJ is open to the public by default, but the department may keep it confidential when the crime is rape, sodomy, sexual abuse, trafficking, or domestic violence and the victim's interests require it. The statute does not make the whole claim file confidential.
added.quote:
All information submitted to the Department of Justice by an applicant and
all hearings of the Workers’ Compensation Board under ORS 147.005 to 147.367
shall be open to the public unless the department or board determines that the
information shall be kept confidential or that a closed hearing shall be held
because: (a) The alleged
assailant has not been brought to trial and disclosure of the information or a
public hearing would adversely affect either the apprehension or the trial of
the alleged assailant; (b) The offense
allegedly perpetrated against the victim is rape, sodomy, sexual abuse,
trafficking in persons or a crime involving domestic violence as defined in ORS
135.230, and the interests of the victim or of the victim’s dependents require
that the information be kept confidential or that the public be excluded from
the hearing;
added.source_title: ORS Chapter 147 (Crime Victims; compensation and SAVE Fund)

added.title: Oregon DOJ: Address Confidentiality Program (ACP)
ORS Chapter 192 (Records; Address Confidentiality Program, ORS 192.820 to 192.868)
Oregon DOJ: Address Confidentiality Program FAQ

added.summary: Mail the completed claim form to VCAP's mailing address, PO Box 1167, Harrisburg, PA 17108-1167.
added.quote: Mailing Address PO Box 1167 Harrisburg, PA 17108-1167
added.pinpoint: Claim form (July 2024), back page contact block; PA.gov apply page step 4: 'Mail or email your claim'
added.source_title: VCAP Claim Form (long form, July 2024)

added.summary: File the claim online through the DAVE portal (the Crime Victims App also files online).
added.quote: File online at https://www.dave.pa.gov
added.pinpoint: Claim form (July 2024), back page footer
added.source_title: VCAP Claim Form (long form, July 2024)

added.summary: Email the completed claim form to VCAP at ra-davesupport@pa.gov.
added.quote: Email ra-davesupport@pa.gov
added.pinpoint: Claim form (July 2024), back page contact block; PA.gov apply page step 4: 'Mail or email your claim'
added.source_title: VCAP Claim Form (long form, July 2024)

added.summary: Include itemized medical bills related to the crime, in the victim's name.
added.quote: Provide all itemized medical bills related to the crime. Medical bills must be in the name of the victim.
added.pinpoint: Claim form (July 2024), Section 4: Medical Expenses
added.source_title: VCAP Claim Form (long form, July 2024)

added.summary: Include itemized counseling bills related to the crime.
added.quote: Provide all itemized counseling bills related to the crime.
added.pinpoint: Claim form (July 2024), Section 5: Counseling Expenses
added.source_title: VCAP Claim Form (long form, July 2024)

added.summary: Include copies of cancelled checks or receipts for any bills the victim or claimant already paid.
added.quote: Provide copies of cancelled checks and/or receipts for any bills paid by the victim/claimant.
added.pinpoint: Claim form (July 2024), Sections 4 and 5
added.source_title: VCAP Claim Form (long form, July 2024)

added.summary: If insured, submit bills to insurance first and include the insurance statements showing payments or rejections.
added.quote: Provide insurance statements of all payments and/or rejections for corresponding bills.
added.pinpoint: Claim form (July 2024), Sections 4 and 5
added.source_title: VCAP Claim Form (long form, July 2024)

added.summary: For lost wages, include two pay stubs from right before the crime, W-2 statements, or the most recent tax return with all schedules.
added.quote: Provide two pay stubs immediately prior to the crime incident, W-2 statements, or most recently filed IRS tax returns including all schedules.
added.pinpoint: Claim form (July 2024), Section 7: Loss of Earnings
added.source_title: VCAP Claim Form (long form, July 2024)

added.summary: For lost wages from crime injuries, a doctor, psychologist, or other listed provider must certify the disability.
added.quote: If filing for loss of earnings due to crime-related injuries a physician verification certifying disability is needed.
added.pinpoint: Claim form (July 2024), Section 7: Loss of Earnings
added.source_title: VCAP Claim Form (long form, July 2024)

added.summary: For lost wages, include proof of any sick, vacation, personal, or disability pay or other benefits received.
added.quote: Provide documentation of any reimbursements received, such as sick, vacation, personal, or disability pay
added.pinpoint: Claim form (July 2024), Section 7: Loss of Earnings
added.source_title: VCAP Claim Form (long form, July 2024)

added.summary: For relocation, include a letter from a human service agency, law enforcement, or a medical provider saying the move is needed for safety and health.
added.quote: Please provide a verification letter explaining that the immediate need for relocation is necessary to protect the safety and health of the victim and individuals residing in the same household
added.pinpoint: Claim form (July 2024), Section 10: Relocation
added.source_title: VCAP Claim Form (long form, July 2024)

added.summary: Sign the Acknowledgement and Reimbursement Agreement and Authorization to Obtain Information (and the HIPAA release for medical or counseling expenses) before the claim can be processed.
added.quote: The Acknowledgement and Reimbursement Agreement and Authorization to Obtain Information must be signed before a claim can be verified and processed for payment.
added.pinpoint: Claim form (July 2024), Acknowledgement & Reimbursement Agreements section
added.source_title: VCAP Claim Form (long form, July 2024)

added.summary: The program says most claims are processed in 12 weeks or less, though each claim differs.
added.quote: Most organizations process claims in 12 weeks or less.
added.pinpoint: PA.gov apply page, FAQ: How long does it take the Program to make a decision?
added.source_title: PA.gov: Apply for Victims' Compensation (VCAP)

added.summary: Once approved, payments owed to the victim or claimant of $5,000 or less are released within 2 business days.
added.quote: Payments owed to the victim/claimant that total $5,000.00 or less are released within 2 business days of being approved.
added.pinpoint: VCAP Claim Process flyer (11/2023)
added.source_title: VCAP flyer: Claim Process (11/2023)

added.summary: Pennsylvania's Address Confidentiality Program, run by the Office of Victim Advocate, gives survivors of sexual assault, domestic violence, stalking, human trafficking, or child abduction an alternate mailing address to keep their address out of public records.
added.quote: The ACP can provide you with an alternate mailing address to keep your address out of public records if you are a victim of domestic violence, sexual assault, stalking, human trafficking, or child abduction.
added.pinpoint: OVA Address Confidentiality Program page; statute: 23 Pa.C.S. 6703(a), 6704(2)
added.source_title: PA Office of Victim Advocate: Address Confidentiality Program (ACP)

added.summary: Everything VCAP obtains or produces while processing a claim is confidential and privileged, is not subject to subpoena or discovery, and may be used only to process the claim; disclosure needs the victim's written consent except as the law provides.
added.quote:
All reports, records or other information
obtained or produced by the Office of Victims' Services during
the processing or investigation of a claim shall be confidential
and privileged, shall not be subject to subpoena or discovery,
shall be used for no purpose other than the processing of a
claim
added.source_title: Crime Victims Act (1998 Act 111), Chapter 7: Compensation (18 P.S. 11.701 to 11.710)

added.title: VCAP flyer: Claim Process (11/2023)
PA Office of Victim Advocate: Address Confidentiality Program (ACP)
23 Pa.C.S. Chapter 67: Domestic and Sexual Violence Victim Address Confidentiality Act

added.summary: Utah's Safe at Home Program gives survivors of sexual assault, domestic violence, stalking, human trafficking, and abuse who fear for their safety a legal substitute address and free mail forwarding, and state and local government agencies must accept that substitute address. Survivors apply through a certified program assistant, not directly.

added.summary: Mail the completed application to the Virginia Victims Fund at P.O. Box 26927, Richmond, VA 23261.
added.quote: Submit application to P.O. Box 26927, Richmond, VA 23261 or (fax) 804-823-6905.
added.pinpoint: VVF Claim Form (English, 08/12/2025), instructions p. 2 (Returning the Application)
added.source_title: Virginia Victims Fund claim form (English, 08/12/2025)

added.summary: The application can be faxed to the Virginia Victims Fund at 804-823-6905.
added.quote: Submit application to P.O. Box 26927, Richmond, VA 23261 or (fax) 804-823-6905.
added.pinpoint: VVF Claim Form (English, 08/12/2025), instructions p. 2 (Returning the Application)
added.source_title: Virginia Victims Fund claim form (English, 08/12/2025)

added.summary: Claims can be filed in person at the office of the Virginia Workers' Compensation Commission, which runs the Fund; the contact page says in-person help is by appointment only.
added.quote: Claims shall be filed in the office of the Commission in person, by mail, or by electronic means in accordance with standards approved by the Commission.
added.source_title: Va. Code § 19.2-368.5 (Filing of claims)

added.summary: There is no public online application: trained Victim/Witness advocates can file the claim electronically through WebFile on the survivor's behalf.

added.pinpoint: VVF Policies (Sept 2025), Where a Claim Must Be Filed, p. 12
added.source_title: Policies of the Virginia Victims Fund (revised September 2025)

added.summary: Attach all receipts, records and documents that support the expenses requested, and keep sending them for ongoing expenses.
added.quote: Applicants should attach all receipts, records and documents supporting requested expenses and continue doing so for ongoing expenses.
added.pinpoint: VVF Claim Form (English, 08/12/2025), instructions p. 2 (Returning the Application)
added.source_title: Virginia Victims Fund claim form (English, 08/12/2025)

added.summary: Attach copies of detailed, itemized billing statements from the medical providers who treated crime-related injuries.
added.quote: Attach a list of additional providers and attach copies of detailed, itemized billing statements.
added.pinpoint: VVF Claim Form (English, 08/12/2025), Section I (Medical Providers), application p. 3
added.source_title: Virginia Victims Fund claim form (English, 08/12/2025)

added.summary: Include bills, receipts, invoices and insurance documentation with the application.
added.quote: Please include any bills, receipts, invoices, and insurance documentation with the application.
added.pinpoint: VVF Claim Form page, Helpful Tips
added.source_title: Virginia Victims Fund: VVF Claim Form page (form instructions)

added.summary: Once the application is deemed eligible, the survivor must provide proof of physical or emotional injury, such as health records.
added.quote: Eligible claimants must submit proof of physical and/or emotional injuries. Proof includes health records detailing a physical and/or emotional injury.
added.pinpoint: VVF Claim Form (English, 08/12/2025), instructions p. 1 (Physical/Emotional Injuries)
added.source_title: Virginia Victims Fund claim form (English, 08/12/2025)

added.summary: Include a written explanation of the victim's physical, mental, emotional and family situation with the application; the form asks for this under the reporting factors for newer crimes.
added.quote: The victim's physical, mental, emotional and family situation (Claimants must include a written explanation of these factors with their application,)
added.pinpoint: VVF Claim Form (English, 08/12/2025), instructions p. 1 (The Crime)
added.source_title: Virginia Victims Fund claim form (English, 08/12/2025)

added.summary: If there is a permanent protective order between the victim and offender, attach it.
added.quote: Is there a permanent protective order for the victim and offender? ☐ Yes ☐ No (Attach if yes.)
added.pinpoint: VVF Claim Form (English, 08/12/2025), Section E (Reporting Information), application p. 2
added.source_title: Virginia Victims Fund claim form (English, 08/12/2025)

added.summary: If the victim had no health insurance and was treated at a hospital, apply for the hospital's charity care and send a copy of the decision; VVF will not decide on health expenses without it.
added.quote: VVF will not make a decision on reimbursing health expenses without a copy of the charity care decision.
added.pinpoint: VVF Claim Form (English, 08/12/2025), Section J (Insurance and Collateral Resources), application p. 3
added.source_title: Virginia Victims Fund claim form (English, 08/12/2025)

added.summary: For prescriptions, provide copies of receipts that show the medication, the prescribing doctor, the date filled and the amount charged.
added.quote: The applicant must provide copies of receipts for prescriptions.
added.pinpoint: VVF Claim Form (English, 08/12/2025), instructions p. 1 (Prescriptions)
added.source_title: Virginia Victims Fund claim form (English, 08/12/2025)

added.summary: Lost wages are paid only when a medical provider verifies the victim could not work because of the crime-related injury.
added.quote: Replacement of lost wages for the victim, who could not work because of the crime-related injury, as verified by a medical provider.
added.pinpoint: VVF Claim Form (English, 08/12/2025), instructions p. 1 (Loss of Wages)
added.source_title: Virginia Victims Fund claim form (English, 08/12/2025)

added.summary: To be reimbursed for clothing or bedding taken as evidence, send a copy of the evidence receipt from law enforcement and the receipt for the replacement items.
added.quote: In order to reimburse this expense, the Fund must have a copy of the evidence receipt provided to the victim by a law-enforcement agency.
added.pinpoint: VVF Policies (Sept 2025), p. 15
added.source_title: Policies of the Virginia Victims Fund (revised September 2025)

added.summary: Moving expenses need dated, signed contracts and a written justification.
added.quote: (Dated/signed contracts required.)
added.pinpoint: VVF Claim Form (English, 08/12/2025), instructions p. 1 (Moving Expenses)
added.source_title: Virginia Victims Fund claim form (English, 08/12/2025)

added.summary: The application is not accepted unless the applicant signs it.
added.quote: Applications are not accepted unless this form is signed by the applicant.
added.pinpoint: VVF Claim Form (English, 08/12/2025), Applicant Responsibilities & Authorizations, application p. 4
added.source_title: Virginia Victims Fund claim form (English, 08/12/2025)

added.summary: Virginia's Address Confidentiality Program, run by the Office of the Attorney General, lets victims of sexual violence, domestic violence, stalking or child abduction use a designated address, and the office forwards their first-class mail to the actual address.
added.quote: to protect victims of domestic violence, stalking, child abduction, or sexual violence by authorizing the use of designated addresses for such victims
added.source_title: Va. Code § 2.2-515.2 (Address Confidentiality Program)

added.summary: All Virginia Victims Fund applications and related documents, including medical records, are confidential; except where law requires otherwise, VVF discloses a victim's information only with written permission.
added.quote: All Virginia Victims Fund (VVF) applications and related documents, including medical information and records, are highly confidential. Except as otherwise required by Virginia or federal law, VVF may only disclose a victim or applicant’s information with their written permission.
added.pinpoint: VVF Confidentiality page, Your Claim is Confidential
added.source_title: Virginia Victims Fund: Confidentiality page

rule.summary: The program cannot award attorneys' fees.
rule.quote: The Commission lacks authority to award attorneys’ fees.
rule.pinpoint: VVF Policies, Criteria for an Award (E)
rule.source_title: Policies of the Virginia Victims Fund (revised September 2025)

rule.summary: For sexual abuse of a minor, the claim may be filed up to 10 years after the victim's eighteenth birthday; where the conduct was a felony, there is no time bar.
rule.quote: in cases involving claims of sexual abuse of a minor, the claim shall be filed within 10 years after the minor's eighteenth birthday, except for in cases involving claims of sexual abuse of a minor where the conduct constitutes a felony, the passage of time shall not be a barrier to when the victim can file a claim.
rule.source_title: Va. Code § 19.2-368.5 (Filing of claims)

eligible for reimbursement of more than two weeks lost wages, a victim must

we will

added.summary: Mail the completed paper application to the Wisconsin Crime Victim Compensation Program's PO box in Madison.
added.quote: You may mail or fax your completed paper application. Mail to: Wisconsin Crime Victim Compensation Program PO Box 7951 Madison, WI 53707-7951
added.pinpoint: Wisconsin DOJ Crime Victim Compensation Application page, Submit Your Completed Paper Application
added.source_title: Wisconsin DOJ: Crime Victim Compensation Application

added.summary: The completed paper application can be faxed to the program instead of mailed.
added.pinpoint: Wisconsin DOJ Crime Victim Compensation Application page, Submit Your Completed Paper Application
added.source_title: Wisconsin DOJ: Crime Victim Compensation Application

added.summary: Applying online is the program's recommended option; you create an account with a personal email, then apply, check status, and upload bills and receipts.
added.quote: Option 1: Apply Online (Recommended) To apply, you must create an account with a personal email to log in and apply.
added.pinpoint: Wisconsin DOJ Crime Victim Compensation Application page, Option 1 (Apply Online link)
added.source_title: Wisconsin DOJ: Crime Victim Compensation Application

added.summary: Enclose copies of itemized crime-related medical bills, and send more as they arrive; the program only accepts itemized bills.
added.quote: Enclose itemized copies of crime-related medical bills. Send copies of other itemized crime-related medical bills as they are received. This Program requires that the bills be itemized.
added.pinpoint: Crime Victim Compensation Application, DJ-CVC-1 (Rev. 10/2024), Application Information, What To Do
added.source_title: Crime Victim Compensation Application, DJ-CVC-1 (Rev. 10/2024), English

added.summary: If insurance or another source covered expenses, attach copies of the itemized bills and the explanations of benefits.
added.quote: Please attach copies of any crime-related itemized bills and explanations of benefits.
added.pinpoint: Crime Victim Compensation Application, DJ-CVC-1 (Rev. 10/2024), Section 6: Insurance and Benefit Information
added.source_title: Crime Victim Compensation Application, DJ-CVC-1 (Rev. 10/2024), English

added.summary: If the crime was reported late or the application is filed late, include a short written explanation of the delay.
added.quote: If the crime was not reported within 5 days or the application was not filed within 1 year, include a brief but detailed written reason for the delay.
added.pinpoint: Crime Victim Compensation Application, DJ-CVC-1 (Rev. 10/2024), Eligibility Requirements
added.source_title: Crime Victim Compensation Application, DJ-CVC-1 (Rev. 10/2024), English

added.summary: Lost wage claims must be backed by an employer verification form, pay stubs, or tax returns; cash pay without documentation is not covered.
added.quote: all lost wage claims must be documented through an employer verification form, paycheck stubs or income tax returns.
added.pinpoint: Wisconsin DOJ Crime Victim Compensation FAQs, Compensation
added.source_title: Wisconsin DOJ: Crime Victim Compensation FAQs

added.summary: Up to two weeks of lost wages need no doctor's note; longer wage loss must be certified as a disability by a physician.
added.quote: The Program may cover up to two weeks of lost wages without a physician certifying the absence. Wage loss beyond two weeks must be documented as a disability by a physician.
added.pinpoint: Wisconsin DOJ Crime Victim Compensation FAQs, Compensation
added.source_title: Wisconsin DOJ: Crime Victim Compensation FAQs

added.summary: For counseling to be paid, the therapist fills out the program's authorization form with a diagnosis, treatment plan, and expected length of treatment.
added.quote: The Program requires that your therapist complete an authorization form, which gives a diagnosis, treatment plan and estimated length of treatment.
added.pinpoint: Wisconsin DOJ Crime Victim Compensation FAQs, Medical Treatment/Counseling
added.source_title: Wisconsin DOJ: Crime Victim Compensation FAQs

added.summary: To be paid back for costs you already paid yourself, send canceled checks or itemized bills or receipts showing the payments.
added.quote: We may send reimbursement checks to applicants if they have paid costs out of pocket already and have documented their payments. They should send in canceled checks or itemized bills/receipts showing their payments.
added.pinpoint: Wisconsin DOJ Crime Victim Compensation FAQs, Medical Treatment/Counseling
added.source_title: Wisconsin DOJ: Crime Victim Compensation FAQs

added.summary: A victim listed on the state child support lien docket must provide a copy of an alternative payment agreement approved by the county child support agency.
added.quote: If the victim is listed on the Wisconsin Child Support Lien Docket, the victim must provide a copy of his/her alternative payment agreement that has been approved by the county child support agency
added.pinpoint: Wisconsin DOJ Crime Victim Compensation FAQs, Applying and Eligibility
added.source_title: Wisconsin DOJ: Crime Victim Compensation FAQs

added.summary: The program says intake can take 90 to 120 days or longer because of the volume of applications.
added.quote: Due to the high volume of applications received, the intake process can take anywhere from 90-120 days or longer.
added.pinpoint: Wisconsin DOJ Crime Victim Compensation Program page, How will my claim be processed?
added.source_title: Wisconsin DOJ: Crime Victim Compensation Program

added.summary: Safe at Home, run by the Wisconsin Department of Justice, gives Wisconsin residents who are victims of sexual abuse and other listed abuse a legal substitute address to use in place of their actual address, with free mail forwarding. Applicants first make a safety plan with a designated Application Assistant.
added.quote: Safe at Home is an address confidentiality program that provides victims of domestic abuse, child abuse, sexual abuse, stalking, trafficking, or those who simply fear for their physical safety with a legal substitute address
added.pinpoint: Wisconsin DOJ, Safe at Home Address Confidentiality Program page, program description; Wis. Stat. 165.68
added.source_title: Wisconsin DOJ: Safe at Home Address Confidentiality Program

added.summary: When a compensation claim arises from sexual assault or another listed sexual offense, the personally identifiable information on the application form is not open to public records inspection or copying.
added.quote: any personally identifiable information, as defined in s. 19.62 (5), provided on the application form is not subject to inspection or copying under s. 19.35 (1).
added.source_title: Wis. Stat. ch. 949, Awards for the Victims of Crimes (subch. I crime victim compensation; subch. II sexual assault forensic examination compensation)

rule.summary: Property loss or damage is not covered beyond the listed evidence items, so a phone that was stolen or broken (not held as evidence) is not covered.
rule.quote: Please note: Property loss or damage is not covered other than those items described above. A victim is not eligible for Crime Victim Compensation if only property damage or loss occurred.
rule.source_title: Wisconsin DOJ: Crime Victim Compensation Program

rule.summary: Mileage and time off work for scheduled appointments or court dates are not paid.
rule.quote: The Program cannot reimburse for mileage or for time off of work for scheduled appointments or court appearances.
rule.source_title: Wisconsin DOJ: Crime Victim Compensation FAQs

rule.summary: Mental health providers' court appearances or evaluations are not paid as counseling.
rule.quote: (c) Court appearances or evaluations are not eligible services.
rule.source_title: Wis. Admin. Code ch. Jus 11, Awards for Victims of Crime

added.title: Wis. Stat. 165.68, Address confidentiality program
Wis. Stat. 103.10(1m), definitions including "sexual abuse" (cross-referenced by 165.68(1)(a)3.)
Wisconsin DOJ: Safe at Home Address Confidentiality Program

added.summary: Mail the completed, notarized application to the Crime Victims Compensation Fund in Charleston.
added.quote: Mail your completed application to: CRIME VICTIMS COMPENSATION FUND 1900 KANAWHA BLVD E ROOM W-334 CHARLESTON WV 25305-0610
added.pinpoint: Application packet, cover page instructions
added.source_title: Application for West Virginia Crime Victims Compensation

added.summary: A claim can also be filed through the Legislature's online claim form.
added.quote: Begin your Online Claim Process This online claim form takes you through 5 simple steps to file your Crime Victims claim.
added.pinpoint: File Your Crime Victims Claim page
added.source_title: File Your Crime Victims Claim (online claim form start page)

added.summary: Send a copy of the police report with the application if you have one; do not hold the application waiting for it near the deadline.
added.quote: Include all the documentation you can - if you have a copy of the police report, hospital or doctor bills, please send with the application.
added.pinpoint: Application packet, cover page instructions
added.source_title: Application for West Virginia Crime Victims Compensation

added.summary: Submit a copy of each of the victim's medical bills. Insurance statements are not acceptable.
added.quote: SUBMIT A COPY OF EACH OF THE VICTIM’S MEDICAL BILLS. INSURANCE STATEMENTS ARE NOT ACCEPTABLE.
added.pinpoint: Application, Victim's Injury Information section
added.source_title: Application for West Virginia Crime Victims Compensation

added.summary: Sign the application's release page in front of a notary; skipping the notary delays the claim.
added.quote: Sign this Application (Page 4) in front of a notary public. Failure to notarize will delay the processing of your claim.
added.pinpoint: Application packet, cover page instructions; Claimant's Release (page 4)
added.source_title: Application for West Virginia Crime Victims Compensation

added.summary: Under the program's procedural rules, the application is filed in duplicate.
added.quote: Within two years after the occurrence of the criminally injurious conduct that is the basis of a claim, an application for an award of compensation shall be filed by a claimant, in duplicate.
added.pinpoint: Rules of Practice and Procedure, Rule 4
added.source_title: Rules of Practice and Procedure under the Crime Victims Compensation Act

added.summary: The claim investigator must file a finding of fact and recommendation within 6 months, unless the Commission extends it.
added.quote: The finding of fact shall be filed within six months, unless extended by the Commission
added.pinpoint: Rules of Practice and Procedure, Rule 5(b)
added.source_title: Rules of Practice and Procedure under the Crime Victims Compensation Act

added.summary: After the 30-day response window, a Commissioner has 45 days from assignment to approve or deny the claim without a hearing.
added.quote: (d) After the expiration of the 30-day period, the Clerk shall assign the claim to a Commissioner. (e) The Commissioner shall, within 45 days after assignment by the Clerk, file an opinion without a hearing and either deny the claim or approve an award to the claimant.
added.pinpoint: Rules of Practice and Procedure, Rule 5(d)-(e)
added.source_title: Rules of Practice and Procedure under the Crime Victims Compensation Act

added.summary: The Secretary of State's Address Confidentiality Program gives victims of sexual assault, domestic violence, stalking and human trafficking a substitute address to use with state and local agencies, plus free first-class mail forwarding. You apply in person through an approved application assistant at a local victim service program.
added.quote: The West Virginia Address Confidentiality Program (ACP) is a program designed to help victims of domestic violence, sexual assault, stalking and human trafficking do business with government agencies and other entities without risking disclosure of their home address.
added.pinpoint: WV Secretary of State ACP page; program created by W. Va. Code 48-28A-103(a)
added.source_title: Address Confidentiality Program (ACP), WV Secretary of State

added.summary: Only for a claim filed on behalf of a minor child who is the subject of a civil abuse and neglect petition: the Fund's records and proceedings are confidential and the parties' identities may not be published. No West Virginia statute or rule found makes an adult survivor's compensation claim confidential.
added.quote: All crime victims’ compensation fund records and proceedings related to a claim filed on behalf of a minor child who is the subject of a civil abuse and neglect petition are confidential and may not be disclosed to any person who is not a necessary participant in the proceedings.
added.pinpoint: W. Va. Code 14-2A-11a(b)
added.source_title: W. Va. Code 14-2A-11a (Application when the victim is the subject of a civil abuse or neglect petition; confidentiality of records)

rule.summary: Personal property is not covered, except medically necessary items such as eyeglasses.
rule.quote: Personal property (except medically necessary items such as eyeglasses)
rule.pinpoint: Eligibility page, Types of Losses Not Covered
rule.source_title: Crime Victims Compensation Fund: Eligibility, Benefits, and Applications

added.quote: IN ORDER TO RECEIVE APPROVED BENEFITS, THIS FORM MUST BE COMPLETED, SIGNED AND DATED!!
added.pinpoint: Application, Request for Taxpayer Identification Number & Certification
added.source_title: Wyoming Primary Victim Compensation Application (SAMPLE, rev. 4/23)

added.summary: By statute, information in victims' compensation claim files and records that is covered by a confidentiality privilege under Wyoming law stays confidential and is not open to public inspection. It is also shielded from legal process and cannot be used as evidence in any proceeding without the consent of the person who gave it.
added.quote: Information contained in the claim files and records of victims, which are subject to any privilege of confidentiality under Wyoming law, shall remain confidential and shall not be open to public inspection. The information shall be immune from legal process and shall not, without the consent of the person furnishing the information, be admitted as evidence or used for any purpose in any action, suit or other judicial, legislative or administrative proceeding.
added.source_title: Crime Victims Compensation Act, W.S. 1-40-101 to 1-40-119 (copy posted by DVS)

rule.summary: Items destroyed or damaged during the crime are not eligible for replacement.
rule.quote: Items destroyed or damaged during the crime are not eligible.
rule.pinpoint: WY DVS Compensation Guidelines and Policy (eff. Jan 1, 2025), Replacement of Personal Property Seized as Evidence
rule.source_title: Wyoming DVS Crime Victim Compensation Guidelines and Policy (effective January 1, 2025)
